quests.title: Dungeoneering
quests.subtitle: Hack 'n Slash
desc: Explorers beware, for terrors await in many seemingly abandoned structures throughout the lands.
Treasure awaits the brave; death awaits the weak.

quests.title: Oh, The Biomes You'll Go
quests.subtitle: It's opener out there, in the wide open air.
desc: Like what you see? Oh, the Biomes You’ll go adds a plethora of beautiful new biomes to spruce up your world.
Take a stroll, look around, see what you like. Maybe you’ll find a new place to call home?

quests.title: Nature's Compass
quests.subtitle: We're not lost, we're right here on this very spot.
desc: Trouble finding your way? Need to find a new desert for some good old-fashioned sand gathering? Maybe a new place to call home, instead?
Craft a Nature’s Compass to help locate rare or unusual biomes.

quests.title: Twilight Forest
desc: Travel to a world swathed in shadow, where frightful beasts call home. Fortune favors the bold!
To form the portal, make a 2x2 pool of water surrounded by grass. Place flowers on the grass blocks and toss a diamond into the water.

quests.title: The Bumblezone
desc: The world of bees is vaster than one might imagine. Throw an Ender Pearl into a hive to see just what’s waiting on the other side.

desc: Trouble finding your way? Need to find a new desert for some good old-fashioned sand gathering? Maybe a new place to call home, instead?
Craft a Nature’s Compass to help locate rare or unusual biomes.

quests.title: Twilight Forest
desc: Enigmatica 9 Expert begins in the Twilight Forest. Face dangerous foes to restore the Tree of Life and branch out to explore new worlds.

quests.title: The Bumblezone
desc: The world of bees is vaster than one might imagine.
Place a Mekanism Teleporter beneath a hive, then throw an Ender Pearl into the hive to see just what’s waiting on the other side.

quests.title: Meteorites!
desc: Crafting a Meteorite Compass will be crucial to finding Certus Quartz, though it is very possible to stumble upon the meteorites above ground. Be sure to bring a decent pickaxe to break through the tough outer shell of the meteorite!

quests.title: Inscribers Presses
desc: Deep in the heart of the meteorites located by the Meteorite Compass lays a Mysterious Cube. Break it to obtain one of each Inscriber Press.
Obtaining these Presses and building an Inscriber to use them in will allow the creation of more advanced machinery.

quests.title: ME Controller Networks
desc: ME Controller Networks consist of an ME Controller multiblock, some amount of cable, and a number of channels depending on the size of the Controller multiblock. In this configuration, channels are distributed in a nearest first manner, so if more than eight devices are connected to a length of Glass Cable, only the eight nearest the controller will be operational.
The multiblock itself is relatively free-form, however certain rules do apply:
1. All ME Controller blocks must be directly connected.
2. The multiblock must fit in a 7x7x7 cube.
3. An ME Controller may have two adjacent blocks in at
most one axis. So, T-Intersections are valid but a
cross is not.
The Controller blocks themselves will accept power for the entire network, meaning an Energy Acceptor is not required.

Each exposed ME Controller face can provide up to 32 channels with a Dense Cable or P2P Tunnel attached to it. More on P2P later. For now, know that a single Dense Cable can transport 32 channels to an area, allowing up to 32 devices to be attached to it.

quests.title: Storage
desc: The primary purpose of any ME network, whether Ad Hoc or Controller based, is storage and logistics. In terms of storage, the ME Network has two options, the ME Storage Bus and the ME Drive.

quests.title: Digital Storage
desc: Capable of holding up to ten Storage Cells, the ME Drive is the heart of AE2’s digital storage system.

Since each Storage Cell has a limited number of material Types it can store, it is often not desirable to allow just anything to go into them. Filters may therefore be set in a Cell Workbench to prevent any other material from being stored in that Cell.
Filters may be conveniently dragged from JEI without needing to have the item in hand.

quests.title: 1k ME Item Storage Cell
desc: Basic Item storage capable of holding up to 63 types of items, such as Stone or Ores. Beware that items with different NBT data on them will be seen as separate types, so dumping all that enchanted armor from your mob farm into storage will very quickly fill the cells.

While the math behind what a Byte is, exactly, can be a little complicated, know that Storage Cells will hold more total if they are limited to a single type than if they’re allowed to store multiple types.

quests.title: 1k ME Fluid Storage Cell
desc: Basic Fluid storage capable of holding up to five types of fluid, such as Lava or Water.

While the math behind what a Byte is, exactly, can be a little complicated, know that Storage Cells will hold more total if they are limited to a single type than if they’re allowed to store multiple types.

{"text":"AE2 Wiki: Storage Maths","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://guide.appliedenergistics.org/1.19.2/features/me-network/storage-cells#:~:text=Portable%20Fluid%20Storage-,Capacity%20Limits,-Storage%20cells%20have"}}

quests.title: 1k ME Chemical Storage Cell
desc: Basic Chemical storage capable of holding up to five types of chemical, such as Sodium or Sulfuric Acid. Radioactive chemicals are not allowed in the system.

While the math behind what a Byte is, exactly, can be a little complicated, know that Storage Cells will hold more total if they are limited to a single type than if they’re allowed to store multiple types.

{"text":"AE2 Wiki: Storage Maths","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://guide.appliedenergistics.org/1.19.2/features/me-network/storage-cells#:~:text=Portable%20Fluid%20Storage-,Capacity%20Limits,-Storage%20cells%20have"}}

quests.title: External Storage
desc: ME Storage Buses act as an interface between most external storage blocks and the ME Network.
This can be as simple as a connection to a single Chest or a Fluid Tank; or may be used to connect much larger storage networks to the Network.

quests.title: Making Connections
desc: The standard workhorse cable, Glass cables can transmit up to eight channels and come in seventeen total colors.
Different colors may be laid out side by side without connecting, allowing them to be used to maintain separations between channels.

quests.title: Covered Cables
desc: Covered Cables are functionally equivalent to Glass Cables, merely offering a cleaner aesthetic.
Dense Covered Cables, on the other hand, transmit four times as many channels per cable, making them the best at extracting channels from an ME controller, extracting as many as 32 channels per side.

However, partial block devices such as Terminals or Buses will not connect to a Dense Cable, so while they make excellent trunk lines, regular cables will still be needed for the final connection to these devices.

item.name: Fluix ME Covered Cable / Fluix ME Dense Covered Cable

quests.title: Autocrafting
desc: Auto Crafting consists of three parts: the Crafting CPU, Pattern Providers, and the Patterns themselves. All three work in concert to run any Auto Crafting request.

quests.title: System Access
desc: Terminals allow manual insertion and extraction from the network, while Crafting Terminals add a built in Crafting Table, allowing quick crafting with materials in the system.

Items may be picked up as normal while Fluids and Chemicals may be retrieved by Left Clicking a Fluid Tank or Chemical tank on the fluid or chemical in the Terminal. Similarly, they may be deposited by Right Clicking the tank into the list in the Terminal.

quests.title: Encoding Patterns
desc: When it comes to actually telling the system how to craft something, a Pattern must be encoded within the Pattern Encoding Terminal. Recipes may be easily encoded by searching them in JEI and clicking the plus (+) button to transfer the items into the Pattern Encoder. It is not necessary to have the ingredients on hand.
Once encoded, place the Pattern in an appropriate Pattern Provider.

quests.title: ME P2P Tunnels
desc: P2P or Point to Point, is a concept of using a single channel to transmit up to 32. Setting up a P2P connection can certainly be daunting for players who are new to AE2, but the basics are fairly accessible.
{"text":"AE2 Wiki: P2P Tunnels","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://guide.appliedenergistics.org/1.19.2/features/me-network/misc/p2p-tunnel"}}
Refer to the following pages for an example on setting this up.
{@pagebreak}
P2P Example:
1. Place down a Controller and power it.
2. Next, place an ME P2P Tunnel against the Controller;
the flat side should be in contact with the Controller.
3. Follow this by running a length of Red ME Glass Cable
from the P2P Tunnel back to the Controller. This
registers the P2P Tunnel on the network. This Red ME
Glass cable will be our Controller line. Any color will
do; the trick is to remain consistent and organized.
4. Now, from any free face on the Controller, run a
Green Covered Cable. Green will represent our carrier
cables and will only be used to transmit P2P
connections. Again, any color will do; however, avoid
using anything that might accidentally cross-connect
with other segments.
5. At the end of this Green Covered Cable, place another
ME P2P Tunnel. This should place with the flat side
facing out, giving a nice view of the Certus texture on
that face.
{@pagebreak}
6. Next, these two Tunnels must be linked; this is
performed with a Memory Card; the color of the card
does not matter.
7. Sneak Right-Click the Card on the ME P2P Tunnel
attached to the Controller. The frequency will change
from 0000 to some random four-character ID.
That ID is now stored in the Memory Card.
10. Now, take the Memory Card to the other P2P Tunnel
and Right-Click the Tunnel. It should now be
configured on the same Frequency ID and should
display as “Linked (Output Side)”. Place a Yellow
Dense Cable against the flat side of this Tunnel and
all 32 channels from the Controller will now be
accessible to the Yellow Dense Cable.
At this point, the Green Covered Cable should show that only one channel has been used, no matter how many connections are made on the Yellow cable.
With such a small network, this may seem like a lot of work for little gain, and that would be an accurate assessment. However, consider a larger Controller multiblock:
● Eight P2P Tunnels can be placed against the Controller
and connected via a single Controller line as above.
● A single Covered Cable can then transmit all eight of
those P2P Tunnels out to a remote place in your base.
● Each of those P2P Tunnels will carry 32 channels for a
total of 256 channels, all being transmitted over a
single Covered Cable.
Doing the same without P2P would require managing eight individual Dense Cables all the way out to the same remote place.

quests.title: Crafting CPU
desc: The Crafting CPU itself is a cuboid multiblock consisting of Crafting Units, Crafting Storage, and optionally Crafting Co-Processing Units.
Crafting Units themselves are strictly filler blocks used to complete the required cuboid shape in the case that more storage is either not accessible or undesirable.
Crafting Storage determines how large a craft may be processed by that CPU. Deeply nested crafts with many steps involved will need larger CPUs to hold everything.

Crafting Co-Processing Units allow a CPU to parallelize, assuming the network is set up to allow it. This means either putting the same pattern in multiple Pattern Providers attached to separate machines, or having multiple Molecular Assemblers attached to a single Pattern Provider

Each Crafting CPU is capable of seeing a single crafting task through from start to finish. This may involve multiple steps, such as turning Logs to Planks, then Planks to Sticks, and finally turning those sticks into a tool.

item.name: Crafting Unit / 1k Crafting Storage / 4k Crafting Storage / 16k Crafting Storage …

quests.title: Crafting
desc: While the Crafting CPU manages the craft, Pattern Providers are responsible for dispensing items and returning the results back to the system.

For basic crafting table style crafting, the Pattern Provider needs one or more adjacent Molecular Assemblers connected to it. The Assemblers will receive the inputs and the pattern from the Pattern Provider, then automatically push the result back to the Pattern Provider upon completion. Molecular Assemblers are also capable of automating the Smithing Table and Stonecutter. The process is identical to basic crafting recipes.

For crafts involving other machines, otherwise known as Processing Patterns, the Pattern Provider should be placed adjacent to the machine on the correct side. For example, automating a vanilla Furnace would require the Pattern Provider to be set on top of the furnace and would require something, such as a hopper, to pull the result from the bottom and return it through a Pattern Provider.
In many cases, it is simplest to use other logistics mods to hand dispensing the inputs and retrieving the outputs, but that’s an exercise for you to solve.
Machines such as Mekanism or Thermal machines, which can push back out the same side they received items on are therefore much simpler to automate, as a single Pattern Provider is all that is needed.

quests.title: ME Annihilation Plane
desc: Exceptionally useful for automation tasks, the Formation and Annihilation Planes allow Placing and Breaking of blocks, respectively. They may also be configured to drop or pick up items.

The Formation Plane will not pull from the network, however. Instead, the items are placed as they enter the system. This means in many cases a separate network, or Subnetwork, will need to be built to make full use of the Formation Plane. This can consist of as little as a Controller or Energy Acceptor for power, an Interface, a Cable, and the Formation Plane. Any items sent into the Interface will be instantly placed.

The Annihilation Plane will work immediately on any block in front of it. It may also be enchanted with Fortune or Silk Touch to allow it to efficiently process things like Certus Quartz Clusters or Ice. It cannot be filtered directly, however. To filter what it breaks, a Subnetwork is required with filtered storage that only allows the desired block to enter the system. For example, when working with Certus Quartz, to ensure it only breaks a full Certus Quartz Cluster, the subnetwork should have a filtered storage on it that only accepts Certus Quartz Crystals. A filtered Storage Bus pointed into a Chest is sufficient.

quests.title: ME Import/Export bus
desc: Where an Interface passively accepts or provides materials, Import and Export Buses actively push and pull them. Set an Export Bus against a tank and configure it to export Water to keep the tank filled, or set an Import bus against a tank of Hydrogen to import it into storage.

quests.title: ME Interface
desc: The ME Interface allows for both insertion and extraction of material from the ME system in a single block. Any material inserted into the Interface is instantly transferred into available storage on the Network. It may optionally be configured to supply up to nine materials, making them accessible for pipes from other mods to extract them from the system.

quests.title: Quantum Network Bridge
desc: The Quantum Network Bridge is a multiblock allowing a network to be extended wirelessly and across dimensions. It consists of a ring of eight ME Quantum Ring blocks surrounding a central ME Quantum Link Chamber and may be built both vertically and horizontally.

Two such structures are required for the multiblock to function, and a pair of Quantum Entangled Singularities must be placed into each end. The remote side will also need to be provided with power to jumpstart it.
Once built, the two sides of the network are seen as the same. Be sure to chunk load both sides, however.
{"text":"AE2 Wiki: Quantum Bridge","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://guide.appliedenergistics.org/1.19.2/features/me-network/quantum-bridge"}}

quests.title: Storage and Conversion Monitors
desc: Storage Monitors allow a window into the Network, displaying the total amount of a given item.
Conversion monitors enhance this functionality by allowing the player to insert and withdraw those items by simply Right-Clicking it.

item.name: ME Storage Monitor / ME Conversion Monitor

quests.title: ME Pattern Access Terminal
desc: Pattern Providers can occasionally end up tucked away in hard-to-reach places. The Pattern Access Terminal grants remote access to every Provider on the network, allowing new Patterns to be easily installed from one location.
Pattern Providers will automatically inherit the name of the block they’re attached to, however, if a custom name is desired for organizational reasons they may be renamed at an Anvil.
Individual Pattern Providers may be hidden from the Terminal by toggling the Pattern Access Terminal button in the GUI.

quests.title: Ad Hoc Networks
desc: Ad Hoc Networks consist of an Energy Acceptor, some amount of cable, and up to eight channels. If more than eight channels are used, the entire network will shut down.

The channel limit can be fairly restrictive but consider that a single ME Storage Bus can be used with a Storage Controller from Functional Storage or Sophisticated Storage; a small Ad Hoc network can therefore allow centralized access to a very large amount of storage, making this a great way to get organized early on.

quests.title: Certus Quartz Crystal
desc: The Flawless Budding Certus Quartz found in meteorites is not easily moved, and breaking it by hand will result in a Flawed Budding Certus Quartz which, when used to grow more Certus, will degrade further over time.
There are ways to move them safely, however, namely Spatial I/O. And there are some ways to craft the block as well, for those inclined to do so.

Automating the collection of Certus Quartz, be it remotely or at home, will be one of the primary challenges to getting into AE2 as Certus Quartz will be in high demand. Several options exist for automated harvesting, including Amethyst Golems from Ars Nouveau.

quests.title: Smart Cables
desc: Smart Cables and Dense Smart Cables function in an identical manner to their Covered Cable counterparts with one addition; they display the number of channels in use on their side.

Note: Smart and Covered cables of the same type and color will connect, so it is not necessary to run long lengths of Smart Cable. Instead, consider using one at the line’s starting point and continuing with Covered Cables from there. This gives an easy indication of the number of channels in use on that entire line.

item.name: Fluix ME Smart Cable / Fluix ME Dense Smart Cable

quests.title: Other P2P Tunnels
desc: P2P may be used for more than transmitting channels, however, allowing long range transportation of many materials over the network that will soon be crisscrossing your base.

To configure a P2P Tunnel for a given transfer type, place down an ordinary ME P2P Tunnel, then Right Click it with an attunement item. For an Energy Tunnel, for example, this will be most any FE compatible item. The item is not consumed and all valid options for each Tunnel type are shown in JEI.
In addition to allowing neater cabling through a base, P2P channels have essentially limitless throughput and no travel time; items inserted in one end come out the other end immediately.
While ME P2P Tunnels may not be nested, the other types of P2P Tunnels may be transmitted over an ME P2P Tunnel connection.

item.name: Chemical P2P Tunnel / Fluid P2P Tunnel / Item P2P Tunnel / Energy P2P Tunnel …

quests.title: Applied Energistics 2
desc: Applied Energistics takes storage and logistics to the next level. On its own, it is capable of automating many crafts while also providing deep storage solutions and capabilities to bridge many mods.
Getting started will require finding some Certus Quartz, and that’s going to take a little exploration. Get your boots and compass, it’s time to head out.

Machines such as Mekanism or Thermal machines, which can push back out the same side they received items on are therefore much simpler to automate, as a single Pattern Provider is all that is needed.

quests.title: ME Annihilation Plane
desc: Exceptionally useful for automation tasks, the Formation and Annihilation Planes allow Placing and Breaking of blocks, respectively. They may also be configured to drop or pick up items.

The Formation Plane will not pull from the network, however. Instead, the items are placed as they enter the system. This means in many cases a separate network, or Subnetwork, will need to be built to make full use of the Formation Plane. This can consist of as little as a Controller or Energy Acceptor for power, an Interface, a Cable, and the Formation Plane. Any items sent into the Interface will be instantly placed.

The Annihilation Plane will work immediately on any block in front of it. It may also be enchanted with Fortune or Silk Touch to allow it to efficiently process things like Certus Quartz Clusters or Ice. It cannot be filtered directly, however. To filter what it breaks, a Subnetwork is required with filtered storage that only allows the desired block to enter the system. For example, when working with Certus Quartz, to ensure it only breaks a full Certus Quartz Cluster, the subnetwork should have a filtered storage on it that only accepts Certus Quartz Crystals. A filtered Storage Bus pointed into a Chest is sufficient.

quests.title: ME Import/Export bus
desc: Where an Interface passively accepts or provides materials, Import and Export Buses actively push and pull them. Set an Export Bus against a tank and configure it to export Water to keep the tank filled, or set an Import bus against a tank of Hydrogen to import it into storage.

quests.title: ME Interface
desc: The ME Interface allows for both insertion and extraction of material from the ME system in a single block. Any material inserted into the Interface is instantly transferred into available storage on the Network. It may optionally be configured to supply up to nine materials, making them accessible for pipes from other mods to extract them from the system.

quests.title: Quantum Network Bridge
desc: The Quantum Network Bridge is a multiblock allowing a network to be extended wirelessly and across dimensions. It consists of a ring of eight ME Quantum Ring blocks surrounding a central ME Quantum Link Chamber and may be built both vertically and horizontally.

Two such structures are required for the multiblock to function, and a pair of Quantum Entangled Singularities must be placed into each end. The remote side will also need to be provided with power to jumpstart it.
Once built, the two sides of the network are seen as the same. Be sure to chunk load both sides, however.
{"text":"AE2 Wiki: Quantum Bridge","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://guide.appliedenergistics.org/1.19.2/features/me-network/quantum-bridge"}}

quests.title: Storage and Conversion Monitors
desc: Storage Monitors allow a window into the Network, displaying the total amount of a given item.
Conversion monitors enhance this functionality by allowing the player to insert and withdraw those items by simply Right-Clicking it.

item.name: ME Storage Monitor / ME Conversion Monitor

quests.title: ME Pattern Access Terminal
desc: Pattern Providers can occasionally end up tucked away in hard-to-reach places. The Pattern Access Terminal grants remote access to every Provider on the network, allowing new Patterns to be easily installed from one location.
Pattern Providers will automatically inherit the name of the block they’re attached to, however, if a custom name is desired for organizational reasons they may be renamed at an Anvil.
Individual Pattern Providers may be hidden from the Terminal by toggling the Pattern Access Terminal button in the GUI.

quests.title: Ad Hoc Networks
desc: Ad Hoc Networks consist of an Energy Acceptor, some amount of cable, and up to eight channels. If more than eight channels are used, the entire network will shut down.

The channel limit can be fairly restrictive but consider that a single ME Storage Bus can be used with a Storage Controller from Functional Storage or Sophisticated Storage; a small Ad Hoc network can therefore allow centralized access to a very large amount of storage, making this a great way to get organized early on.

quests.title: Certus Quartz Crystal
desc: Automating the collection of Certus Quartz will be one of the primary challenges to getting into AE2, as Certus Quartz will be in high demand.
Several options exist for automated harvesting, including Amethyst Golems from Ars Nouveau.

quests.title: Smart Cables
desc: Smart Cables and Dense Smart Cables function in an identical manner to their Covered Cable counterparts with one addition; they display the number of channels in use on their side.

Note: Smart and Covered cables of the same type and color will connect, so it is not necessary to run long lengths of Smart Cable. Instead, consider using one at the line’s starting point and continuing with Covered Cables from there. This gives an easy indication of the number of channels in use on that entire line.

item.name: Fluix ME Smart Cable / Fluix ME Dense Smart Cable

quests.title: Other P2P Tunnels
desc: P2P may be used for more than transmitting channels, however, allowing long range transportation of many materials over the network that will soon be crisscrossing your base.

To configure a P2P Tunnel for a given transfer type, place down an ordinary ME P2P Tunnel, then Right Click it with an attunement item. For an Energy Tunnel, for example, this will be most any FE compatible item. The item is not consumed and all valid options for each Tunnel type are shown in JEI.
In addition to allowing neater cabling through a base, P2P channels have essentially limitless throughput and no travel time; items inserted in one end come out the other end immediately.
While ME P2P Tunnels may not be nested, the other types of P2P Tunnels may be transmitted over an ME P2P Tunnel connection.

item.name: Chemical P2P Tunnel / Fluid P2P Tunnel / Item P2P Tunnel / Energy P2P Tunnel …

quests.title: Applied Energistics 2
desc: Applied Energistics takes storage and logistics to the next level. On its own, it is capable of automating many crafts while also providing deep storage solutions and capabilities to bridge many mods.
Getting started will require finding some Certus Quartz, and that’s going to take a little exploration. Get your boots, it’s time to head out.
{"text":"AE2 Wiki","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://guide.appliedenergistics.org/1.19.2/"}}

quests.title: Ars Nouveau
desc: With Ars Nouveau you will learn to harness the latent energy infused in all things to cast powerful spells, drive arcane machinery, and even to empower some cute friends along the way.
These quests will guide you through the mod, but be sure to refer back to the manual regularly for extra information.
~MuteTiefling

quests.title: Spell Turret
quests.subtitle: T-U-R-R-E-T, Turret
desc: The Spell Turret is an enhanced apparatus used to cast spells on a Redstone pulse. Source for the spell will be provided automatically from nearby Source Jars.
To set a spell, inscribe a Spell Parchment and Right-Click it on the Turret. It may use either Touch or Projectile forms in the spell.

quests.title: Sourcelinks
quests.subtitle: Source Preserves
desc: Source may be found in any living thing, so it should come as no surprise that it may be condensed from most living matter. In a natural cycle, the Source contained in the living is simply passed around from plant to animal and back. A nearby Sourcelink, however, may be used to re-direct that ephemeral dew into specially prepared Source Jars, preserving it for later use.

Each Sourcelink has its own requirements which are covered in detail in the Worn Notebook. They’re all useful in their own way, often the best choice is dictated by what other activities are already happening in an area.
● Agronomic absorbs source from growing plants. Each time a nearby plant progresses a growth stage, some Source is produced. Certain magical plants produce more Source.
● Alchemical re-absorbs the condensed Source present in Potions. Any beneficial spell stored in an adjacent Potion Jar will be absorbed, producing Source. More is produced from stronger potions.
● Mycelial consumes food items placed into adjacent Pedestals. Though all food is rich in Source, those produced from Sourceberries tend to contain the most.
● Vitalic absorbs the life-force of creatures dying nearby.
● Volcanic consumes most burnables from adjacent Pedestals. Coal, long fossilized trees, produces a small amount while Blazing Archwood logs produce more sizeable quantities.
● Fluid absorbs certain liquids from tanks placed below it, converting it into Source at different rates.

item.name: Agronomic Sourcelink / Volcanic Sourcelink / Alchemical Sourcelink / Vitalic Sourcelink …

quests.title: Runic Chalk
quests.subtitle: Chalk it up to Experience
desc: What good is magic if we can’t make it work for us?
Save some effort and imprint spells into a Rune instead. Any time an entity meets it, the spell will trigger. Source for the spell will be provided automatically from nearby Source Jars.
To use Runic Chalk, begin by Right-Clicking it on the ground to draw a rune. Now Right-Click the rune with a prepared Spell Parchment. Valid Spell Parchments must begin with the Touch Form.

quests.title: Spell Parchment
quests.subtitle: Jousting Snails
desc: With some work, common paper can be infused to be a better receptacle for magic. Once infused, these written spells can be used in a variety of ways.

To prepare a Parchment with a spell, first design the spell within the Spell Book. Then place a Parchment on the Scribe's Table and Sneak Right-Click the table with the Spell Book to transfer the selected spell over to the Parchment.
Parchments may be re-used, though it can be useful to keep a library of scribed Parchments to be able to quickly re-apply the spell.

quests.title: Magebloom Seed
quests.subtitle: Putting Down Roots
desc: The Magebloom sits at the border between the mundane and the arcane. It grows as any other plant, but its roots reach through the veil, soaking in more of the Source that infuses the earth.
Growing these will serve two purposes to a budding practitioner:
First, they produce more Source than any mundane plants when grown.
Second, they can be woven into a fabric that when worn close serves as a personal battery for Source.

quests.title: Enchanting Apparatus
quests.subtitle: The Spirit is Willing but the Flesh is Spongy and Bruised
desc: One's own reservoir of Source is limited: the flesh can only hold so much. Certain magical materials exist to assist this but they themselves require access to greater reservoirs to even make.
An external apparatus is therefore required to hold the reagents for such creative endeavors and to assist in funneling the Source into them safely.

To construct the Enchanting Apparatus, place down the Arcane Core with the Enchanting Apparatus on top of it. The Pedestals must be placed within three blocks of the Core. If a recipe indicates a Source cost, a filled Source Jar must also be placed nearby.
To work with the Apparatus, first place the reagents on the pedestals and the focus in the Enchanting Apparatus itself. All items will be consumed during the craft.

The Enchanting Apparatus may also be used to apply specific enchantments to tools and armor, simplifying the process of getting certain enchants to round out a piece of gear. These recipes are only listed in the Worn Notebook.

quests.title: Curious Trinkets
quests.subtitle: Draw me like your French girls
desc: Source is a fickle thing, and keeping it in one place long enough to use can be challenging at best. Aspiring practitioners may find themselves struggling to channel Source for very long. Besides magical accoutrements woven from Mana Fibers, certain other materials can be molded into useful trinkets to serve as an extension of one's own reserves.
Refer to the Worn Notebook's section on Magical Equipment for recipes and to discover more useful curios.

quests.title: Source Relay
quests.subtitle: Witches Abroad
desc: Source permeates all things. Left to its own, it spreads and infuses but rarely collects. Binding it in jars is an excellent way of storing source for later use, but moving it from place to place can be a touchy subject.

Source Relays serve this purpose. They provide a controlled channel for Source to flow through without dissipating back into the world. Source Relays may be linked to other relays as well as jars to provide safe transit from one place to another.
Use a Dominion Wand to set the links.

quests.title: Source Relay: Splitter
quests.subtitle: Equal Rites
desc: Splitter Relays are capable of both sending to and receiving from multiple other Source Relays.
For instance, multiple Source farms might be brought together to transfer across a single line of Relays, or branches might be made to supply Source to different locations for Turrets or Crafting.
They share the same range limitations of normal Relays, but by combining the two a network of Source can be easily strung across an area, making it available wherever it is needed.

quests.title: Bookwyrm Charm
quests.subtitle: Boop the Snoot
desc: An amicable being with a driving need to organize, Bookwyrms are central to using Ars Nouveau’s item management system which allows linking many inventories together into a single access point.

quests.title: Starbuncle Charm
quests.subtitle: In Search of the Golden Acorn
desc: Starbuncles are curious forest critters with a love for all things shiny. Gold, in particular. They may be befriended by tossing them a small amount of gold. Once befriended, they will assist by collecting items and moving them to inventories.
They may be instructed what to do by using a Dominion Wand. Their behavior may be further modified by giving them some Starbuncle Shades or a Wixie hat.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Starbuncles.
These critters can be an uncommon sight even in ancient forests. If none can be found, consider summoning them with the Altar of Birthing.

quests.title: Whirlisprig Charm
quests.subtitle: Whispering Winds
desc: Whirlisprigs are the care-takers of the forest, helping new growth to flourish. They will come with you willingly if you honor them by planting a tree in their stead. Once befriended, a Sprig will tend to a small area and gift you with their bounty. Plant down trees, crops, flowers, and other natural items and over time the Sprig will grow more of these and offer them to you.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Sprigs.
The number of wild Sprigs has dwindled in recent times. If none can be found, consider summoning them with the Altar of Birthing.

quests.title: Familiar Friends
quests.subtitle: Auto-magically
desc: Not all tasks lend themselves to completion by simple automatons like a turret or a rune. There exist certain magical creatures in this world that will help an aspiring practitioner quite willingly if asked nicely.

item.name: Drygmy Shards / Whirlisprig Shards / Siren Shards / Starbuncle Shards …

quests.title: Wixie Charm
quests.subtitle: Wyrd Sisters
desc: Wouldn't it be helpful to have a hand around the Crafting Table? Someone to pass you this, or fetch you that? Or perhaps they could just do the job for you while you further your studies of the arcane?
The Wixie is the friend you seek. Bound by casting Dispel on a Witch at low health, Wixies are summoned by using their Charm on a standard Cauldron, transforming it into a Wixie Cauldron.

To specify what the Wixie ought to craft, simply make one of the items yourself and Right-Click it on her cauldron. She'll take care of gathering the required items from nearby inventories. She will need a jar of Source nearby, however, to keep her productive.

quests.title: Potion Jar
quests.subtitle: Nanny Ogg's Cookbook
desc: Simple item crafting isn’t the only thing these crafty ladies have hidden up their sleeves. They’re quite the adept in a brewery as well, making potions of all types.
Just like with regular crafting, Wixies will need some extras at hand. A Source Jar, a Potion Jar, and an inventory of ingredients.

Each Wixie can only make one potion type at a time. The type is determined by first brewing one the traditional way and, with potion in hand, right-click her cauldron to set the recipe. She’ll get to work as soon as everything is available. Just like traditional brewing, potions must be made in steps. One Wixie will make an Awkward Potion with Nether Wart, the next will add a Golden Carrot to make a Night Vision potion, and a third could add Redstone to extend it.

It is recommended to take that potion and stick it in the jar immediately so that the potion jar can be locked to that type. Sneak + Right-Click the jar with a Dominion Wand to lock it to that type of potion. This is handy when multiple Wixies are at work in the same area.

quests.title: Potion Melder
quests.subtitle: Subtle Infusions
desc: The clever arcanist finds ways to save themselves time, and nothing wastes time like drinking five different potions in preparation for a fight. Why not mix them and drink them all at once?
This is exactly what the Potion Melder does.
The Potion Melder needs two Potion Jars to act as inputs and a third to act as an output.
Using a Dominion Wand, link two Potion Jars to the Melder. These will serve as the inputs. Then, link the Melder to one last Potion Jar to accept the mixed brew.
The process uses some Source from a nearby Source Jar but produces potions that combine all the effects of the two inputs. This process can be chained to produce potions with multiple effects.

quests.title: Potion Flask
desc: Multiple doses all bottled up and ready to go in an eco-friendly re-usable package.
Each Flask can hold up to eight doses of potion and may even be enchanted to increase the potency or duration of the potions within.

quests.title: Enchanter's Wand
quests.subtitle: Cast Wide, Your Net
desc: A rather traditional Arcane Focus, the Casting Wand may be inscribed with a single spell in much the same way as inscribing a Parchment.

Contrary to other casting methods, however, no Form is required on the spell designed in the Spell Book. All spells cast from a Casting Wand are automatically granted the Projectile form for free as well as a level of Accelerate.
This means extra slots for adding Effects or Augments, making them ideal for specialized tools.
Other Arcane Foci exist granting similar benefits, such as the Enchanter’s Mirror and Enchanter’s Sword. The Worn Notebook covers these and more.

quests.title: Ritual Brazier
quests.subtitle: I Love the Smell of Napalm in the Morning
desc: Nothing quite says “Magic” like burning reagents on a pyre!
With a specially crafted Tablet to guide the process and optional reagents to augment it, the Ritual Brazier is capable of producing a wide variety of effects.

To get it going, Right-Click the Brazier with any Tablet. If extra materials are required, they should be thrown atop the flame to be consumed. Once everything is set, Right-Click again with an empty hand to finalize the ritual.

quests.title: Disintegration
quests.subtitle: XP = MC Squared
desc: Killing monsters can be a … messy affair. Why not skip the trouble and simply distill them down into their very essence?
Monsters killed with this ritual will drop Experience Gems worth roughly double the XP they’d drop normally. But, all drops are lost in the process.

quests.title: Cloudshaping
quests.subtitle: Here Comes the Rain Again, Falling On My Head Like a Memory
desc: Sometimes it feels like the rain just never lets up. It has soaked through your armor, flooded your cave, corroded all those fancy schmancy circuits you were told would solve your problems.
But did they solve the rain? No. Now let’s magic that rain away.

quests.title: Celestial Manipulation
quests.subtitle: Ain't nobody got time for that!
desc: Are your days too short? Not enough time for your nocturnal pursuits?
Consider bending time and space to bring the sun or moon around again to for that extra boost of energy or to finish charting out those constellations you find so fascinating.
Surely nothing bad could come of this?

quests.title: Challenge
quests.subtitle: Hear Ye, Hear Ye
desc: All you Lowly Pillagers, Ravaging Vindicators, and Summoners of Questionable Merit are here-by formally summoned to participate in the coming tournaments!
Summons a Pillager Raid to your back door, just in time!

quests.title: Fertility and Growth
quests.subtitle: Magically Sustained Gestation
desc: If you sad in life – use MSG. If you happy in life – use MSG. Put MSG in everything, it’ll turn out better. You just get baby? Put MSG on baby, make smarter.
Magic does wonders when it comes to growing crops and breeding animals. Combine these two rituals to keep your livestock busy and growing quickly.

quests.title: Warp Portals
quests.subtitle: A Wizard Did It!
desc: Going somewhere?
Bring some supplies along before setting out, as having a quick way back and forth can be very handy.
A Warp Scroll may be bound to a location via Right-Click and then used again later to return the player to that exact spot. The Scroll is consumed on use, however.

Alternatively, a portal may be built using any type of Sourcestone in a rectangular shape.  Place a filled Source Jar nearby and toss a bound Warp Scroll through the frame to ignite it, linking it to the coordinates from the scroll. Items, mobs, even spells may pass through these portals, though they are incapable of crossing between dimensions.
Ghostweave, Mirrorweave, and Falseweave may all be used for portal frames as well, allowing for endless customization!

item.name: Sourcestone / Sourcestone: Small Bricks / Smooth Sourcestone / Sourcestone: Mosaic …

quests.title: Drygmy Charm
quests.subtitle: Very A-moose-ing.
desc: Found most anywhere that wild beasts roam, Drygmies are spirits bound to the earth, tending her flock. Through their magic, they can gather items from all manner of beast without causing them harm in any way. They may be enticed to work for you by showing them a token of their mortal enemies: Wilden Defenders.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Drygmies.
The number of wild Drygmies has dwindled in recent times. If none can be found, consider summoning them with the Altar of Birthing.

quests.title: Summon Wilden
quests.subtitle: The Beast of Caerbannog
desc: First shalt thou take out the Holy Pin. Then, shalt thou count to three, no more, no less…
Useful for summoning Wilden of all sizes. When augmented with body parts from each of the lesser Wilden, the Wilden Chimera will appear to avenge his kin.

quests.title: Source Relays: Collectors and Depositors
quests.subtitle: Ebb and Flow
desc: Where Source Relays are typically limited to pulling from or sending to a single linked Source Jar, these specialized Relays will automatically pull from or send to any nearby jars without being linked.

A Depositor therefore makes a great tool for keeping jars filled for other purposes, such as forming Warp Portals. Using both a Collector and a Depositor together also makes for a handy automation friendly means of transferring Source. Fill jars in one location, pick them up, and drain them elsewhere.

item.name: Source Relay: Collector / Source Relay: Depositor

quests.title: Source Relay: Warper
desc: Warp Relays serve as long range Source transportation. By linking two together, Source may be transferred any distance in the same dimension.
A small amount of Source is used in stabilizing this connection over longer distances.

quests.title: Starbuncle
quests.subtitle: Don't You Crittersize Me!
desc: The only thing keeping these cute critters from being a crunchy treat to larger predators are their swift little feet. A power they’ll gladly lend for the price of friendship.

quests.title: Wixie
quests.subtitle: A Spoonful of Sugar Helps the Medicine Go Down...
desc: Though quite pleasant to hang around in more domestic environments, Wixies are known to be quite resourceful in a fight, flinging dangerous brews hither and thither to fend off would be attackers.

quests.title: Drygmy
quests.subtitle: As Luck Would Hoove It
desc: Powerful Earth Spirits with a knack for finding things, Drygmies impart their knowledge upon their friends, bolstering magic and turning up extra loot.

quests.title: Bookwyrm
quests.subtitle: I Will Dewey Decimate You
desc: With their deep link to Source, Bookwyrms make excellent allies, collecting anything they find laying around and bringing it to you.

quests.title: Whirlisprig
quests.subtitle: The Queen of Sauce
desc: Variety is the spice of life, and none know this better than the Sylvan folk. Everything tastes better when they’re around.

quests.title: Binding
quests.subtitle: Friendship is Magic
desc: For ages, sorcerers have been befriending creatures of all sorts to assist in their work. These friendships run deep, forming a symbiotic partnership that grants incredible longevity to the creature and potent abilities to the sorcerer.
Perform the Ritual of Binding near an amenable creature to signal your desire to bond with it. Should it acquiesce, it will grant a token that may be added to a spell book to summon them at any time.
Each familiar grants unique bonuses that are detailed in the Worn Notebook. Explore each to find just the right friend.

quests.title: Getting Started: Source Gems
quests.subtitle: Like Sweet Morning Dew
desc: Source is the driving energy behind every spell and arcane device in Ars Nouveau, but it must be condensed out of the world to harness it for anything beyond the simplest of uses. To that end, we’ll begin with an Imbuement Chamber.

The Imbuement Chamber itself requires Source to operate but can slowly draw some out of the environment for simple crafts; the simplest of which is the Source Gem. Once able, place a filled Source Jar nearby to greatly enhance the crafting speed.

The item in the center of the recipe is to be inserted into the Chamber itself, while any items surrounding it are to be placed on nearby Pedestals. The items on the Pedestals act as keys and are never consumed, while the central item will be converted to the result.

quests.title: Spellcasting
desc: From novice to master alike, much time is dedicated to the art of spell craft, be it preparing and learning new Glyphs, enchanting personal Arcane Foci, or preparing Spell Glyphs or Turrets.
These activities all center around the Scribe’s Table.
New glyphs may be inscribed by Right-Clicking the Scribe’s Table with a Spell Book to open the Codex of all glyphs, known or unknown.

To scribe a glyph, merely locate and select it in the Codex. Follow this by throwing the required ingredients at the table to finish the craft. Finally, learn the Glyph by Right-Clicking it in the air.
Note: Glyphs are stored on the player, not the Spell Book. So, losing a Spell Book does not mean the loss of learned glyphs.

quests.title: Alteration Table
quests.subtitle: Tailor Made
desc: Threads may be woven into a Thread Slot on applicable armor by way of the Alteration Table.
The equipment is to be placed on the right-hand side, whereupon the parchment on the left will display the available slots.

To apply a Thread, Right-Click it onto the side with the parchment. Threads are applied from top to bottom. They may be removed at any time and re-applied, however, and are not lost when removed. Right-clicking with an empty hand will remove them top to bottom.

Do note that some Threads have different or stronger effects when applied in higher tier Thread Slots. Some, like the Thread of Gliding, require a specific level slot to be applied at all. Applying the same Thread more than once will generally have no effect.

quests.title: Siren Charm
quests.subtitle: Darlin' it's better, down where it's wetter
desc: Though they’re often viewed with mistrust and labeled as man-eating beasts (it was just the one time, ok?), Sirens are really only interested in gathering shiny things. Once befriended, a Siren will slowly collect treasures from their watery homes, tucking them away for safe keeping. The prettier their environment, the more likely they are to share those treasures with their friends.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Sirens.
The number of wild Sirens has dwindled in recent times. If none can be found, consider summoning them with the Altar of Birthing.

quests.title: Splash Flask Cannon
desc: The Splash Flask Cannon is a simple device designed to further weaponize harmful potions. Any potion fed into it may be thrown as if it had been brewed into a Splash Potion.
Combined with Flasks, these can make powerful tools in combat.

quests.title: Potion Diffuser
quests.subtitle: Potpourri for the Soul
desc: The Potion Diffuser greatly enhances the efficiency of potions by applying a single dose to all creatures in the area at an enhanced duration.

quests.title: Alchemist's Crown
desc: A wizard in battle has no time to worry about such trivialities as quaffing a potion. The Alchemist’s Crown handles that for them.

By opening the radial menu and selecting one of the potions detected in one’s inventory, the Alchemists Crown will automatically re-apply that potion whenever it’s duration ends. By keeping a few flasks on hand, potion effects can be made to last quite a long time without needing to drink repeatedly.

quests.title: Bound Script: Siren
quests.subtitle: Flippin' your fins really will get you far
desc: Truly an indispensable companion to keep when exploring the depths, Sirens will grant their friends a bonus to water spells and also bestow Dolphin’s Grace upon them while swimming.

quests.title: Bound Script: Flarecannon
quests.subtitle: Burninate the land
desc: When kept as a close companion, Flarecannon will impart some of power upon their friends, boosting fire magics and granting temporary resistance to fire.

quests.title: Flarecannon Charm
quests.subtitle: Five-Alarm Fire
desc: Powerful arcane constructs, these golems known as Flarecannon serve to protect, burning anything hostile that comes in their range.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Flarecannon.

quests.title: Magical Vestments
quests.subtitle: I shall wear midnight
desc: Ideal equipment for the dedicated Wizard, these magically enhanced vestments offer more than simple protection.

Primarily, they act as a personal battery for Source, giving the caster more to draw on in battle. However, they may also have special Threads woven into them to offer more unique and customized boons.

Each set of armor may be upgraded in the Enchantment Apparatus through three different tiers. At each tier, they gain more slots for accepting Threads. The recipe for upgrading the tier is shown in the Worn Notebook.

item.name: Sorceror's Collar / Arcanist's Hat / Battlemage's Hood
Sorceror's Wrap / Arcanist's Robes / Battlemage's Gambeson
Sorceror's Leggings / Arcanist's Pants / Battlemage's Legguards
Sorceror's Footpads / Arcanist's Treads / Battlemage's Boots

quests.title: Awakening
desc: Golems have long been used by those of sorcerous ability to assist them in their work. With a Tablet of Awakening, an experienced mage may bring a form of sentience to Archwood Trees and Budding Amethyst. The resulting creatures are known as Weald Walkers and Amethyst Golems, respectively.
Weald Walkers act as guardians, keeping hostile creatures at bay with their brutish strength.

Amethyst Golems, meanwhile, are more fastidious in nature, gently caring for and harvesting Amethyst from nearby Budding Amethyst. Normal Amethyst blocks in their charge may even be made to bud and grow more.

quests.title: Containment
quests.subtitle: Modern problems require modern solutions
desc: Working with others can be a messy business. Wizards of old spent a great deal of time and effort trying to keep their Drygmies and Villager friends safe from harm. Containment Jars offer a modern solution to this age-old problem.
Any creature under the effect of a Ritual of Containment will be automatically drawn into a nearby empty Containment Jar.
Contained creatures may still be interacted with, however. Villagers with a job will continue to trade, Cows may be milked, and Drygmies will continue to harvest from them.
Naturally, this also makes an excellent means of transport as well, as the jars may be picked up and moved around freely. To release a creature from the Jar, simply cast Dispel upon it.

quests.title: Spell Focuses
quests.subtitle: Focus Pocus
desc: When a wizard chooses to specialize in a particular school of magic, often they will invest in a Focus to enhance their chosen school.
Equipped in a dedicated Curio slot, each focus grants unique boons to their school which are detailed in the Worn Notebook.

item.name: Lesser Focus of Fire / Lesser Focus of Water / Lesser Focus of Air / Lesser Focus of Earth …

quests.title: Scryer's Oculus
quests.subtitle: You Lookin’ at Me Lookin’ at You
desc: On occasion, it can be quite helpful to be able to see into an area without being there in person. Especially environments that may pose a hazard to the person.
A Scryer’s Oculus enables the wizard to perform exactly that sort of long-range monitoring.

Place a Scry Crystal in the location to be monitored, Right-Click it with a Blank Parchment to record the location and place the resulting Scryer’s Scroll on a pedestal near the Oculus. When approached, the Oculus allows the Wizard to select from any of the nearby Scrolls to view the location.

quests.title: Starbuncle Logistics
desc: In addition to transporting items and looking stylish, Starbuncles may be given a few additional accessories to further enhance their abilities.
Configuring their pickup and drop off locations remains the same as with Items; by using a Dominion Wand after equipping them with the appropriate accessory.

Need them to access a specific side? Use a Direction Scroll to set their preferred side. These are set by looking in the desired direction and Sneak + Right-Clicking them. Then use the scroll on the Starbuncle.

quests.title: StarbAttery
quests.subtitle: Watt is love? Baby don't hertz me, n-ohm-ore
desc: A tiny little backpack for transporting FE from place to place.

quests.title: Starbucket
quests.subtitle: Looking a little sloshed
desc: Sealed to prevent spillages, the Starbucket allows the Starbuncle to transport any fluid.

quests.title: Starballoon
quests.subtitle: Let's not get carried away
desc: With a Starballoon in tow, a Starbuncle may transport Mekanism gasses from place to place.

quests.title: Fluid Jar
desc: Though suitable for any fluid, Fluid Containment Jars are particularly useful for working with Potions.

When fluid potions made by other mods such as Create, Hexerei, Thermal, or Immersive Engineering are stored in a Containment Jar, they’ll automatically be deposited into a Potion Jar placed atop it. Meaning any potion may be easily converted for use in devices such as Potion Melders or other alchemical tools offered by Ars Nouveau.

quests.title: Source Condenser
quests.subtitle: Source Reserves
desc: A simple device used for converting Source in its natural form to a more… fluid state, allowing it to be moved around by way of pipes or other conveyances.

quests.title: Energy Conversion
desc: Once thought to be entirely separate, the magical energies know as Source, Aura, and FE are in fact all facets of the same energy. By making use of special crystals, it becomes possible to convert between them with ease.

Pulsating Crystals work by absorbing Source from nearby Source Jars and converting it into usable FE. Should the area contain sufficient Aura, it will also be consumed, greatly enhancing the FE generated.

Resonating Crystals, on the other hand, set up an internal resonance with FE, converting it back into Source or Aura. If a Source Jar is near enough, it will send it there. If there is no jar, or if it is 100% full, the Resonating Crystal will instead convert the incoming FE to Aura and diffuse it into the atmosphere.

item.name: Dim Pulsating Crystal / Bright Pulsating Crystal / Iridescent Pulsating Crystal
Dim Resonating Crystal / Bright Resonating Crystal / Iridescent Resonating Crystal

quests.title: Storage Lectern
desc: The Storage Lectern is the central access point for Bookwyrm based storage. Place one down anywhere and Right-Click one or more Bookwyrm Charms onto it to bind them to the Lectern.
The Bookwyrms are responsible for moving items around and each one may manage up to eight inventories. So, a Lectern with two Bookwyrms attached could be bound to up to 16 nearby inventories.

To bind an inventory to the Lectern, first Sneak Right-Click the inventory with a Dominion Wand, then Right-Click the Lectern. The Lectern may be Right-Clicked again with a Dominion Wand to highlight all attached inventories and Bookwyrms.
This system pairs very nicely with large storage containers like Drawers, Item Vaults, and Dimensional Storage Actuators, creating dense storage capabilities using fewer Bookwyrm connections.

The Lecterns may also be chained to allow remote access to the central storage. Place a new lectern anywhere within 30 blocks of the primary lectern, Right-Click the new one with the Wand, then Right-Click the primary with the wand. The new Lectern will now have access to all of the inventories of the first. Just keep chaining in this way as far as desired to have terminals throughout your home!
Note: Chained Lecterns may not have Bookwyrms or Inventories bound to them. Doing so will sever the connection with the primary network and create a new separate network.

Finally, it should be mentioned that any unbound inventory placed directly adjacent to a Lectern will act as an input for the entire system. Any items that find their way into this inventory will be automatically sorted out to linked inventories by the Bookwyrms. This works for remote Lecterns as well. Items may also be inserted directly into the Lectern via hoppers or other automated logistics.

quests.title: Repository
desc: The Repository is a special block that can hold as much as a Double Chest in a single block space. Unlike a standard Chest, however, they retain their name when broken. This ties in nicely with another feature of the Lectern: Named Tabs

Any named inventories that are bound to the Lectern will show up in a special tab in the interface. Inventories sharing the same name all share the tab and the contents of all of these inventories is grouped together. This allows for some manual organization, such as putting all gems in one set of inventories, or special equipment in another. Think of these as a search group, allowing quick access to all the items at a click.

This feature works with any inventory that can be named in an Anvil, however, it works best with those that retain their name on pickup to avoid having to rename them. Some other examples include Shulker Boxes, Smart Chests, Reinforced Chests, Wooden Storage Crates, and Reinforced Storage Crates to name a few.

quests.title: Display Case
desc: Display Cases are a simple Redstone device to read the contents of an inventory. They may be linked to any inventory or even a Storage Lectern and can output a signal when the configured item is either above or below a defined threshold.
Select the inventory to bind it to with the Dominion Wand. Sneak Right-Click for regular inventories or just a simple Right-Click for a Lectern, then Right-Click the placed Display Case to bind it.
To set the item to monitor, simply Right-Click the item into the Case. This works with Item Scrolls as well.
To set the quantity, use an empty hand to Right-Click the Case to increase and Left-Click to decrease. Sneak Click will increase or decrease by bounds of eight.
To invert the signal, Sneak Right-Click the Case with the Dominion Wand.

quests.title: Enchanter's Eye
desc: Far from home and need a few more potions to top up? The Enchanter’s Eye allows remote casting to a fixed location when bound to a Scry Crystal, or multiple locations with Scryer’s Scrolls.
As a simple example of how this may be useful, a Scry Crystal placed facing a Storage Lectern would allow the following spell form to access the Lectern remotely:
&5Touch&r > &2Interact&r
Adding Sensitive to the spell form would allow remote filling of a flask. Simply hold the flask in the off hand and ensure the Scry Crystal is set facing a Potion Jar:
&5Touch&r > &2Interact&r > &6Sensitive&r

quests.title: Stabilized Warp Scroll
desc: Much like standard Warp Scrolls, Stabilized Warp Scrolls may be used to create portals. They offer two advantages, however.
First, the scroll may be used to bind to coordinates in other dimensions, allowing cross-dimensional transportation.
Second, it may be used on a block at any time to generate a temporary portal to the bound coordinates. This does not consume the scroll.

quests.title: Amethyst Golem
quests.subtitle: Don't Be Shy, Be a Little Boulder!
desc: With their deep connection with the earth, Amethyst Golems make powerful familiars who strengthen one's ties to the ground.

quests.title: Amethyst Golem Charm
quests.subtitle: It's Geo Time!
desc: These steadfast little creatures have an insatiable desire for crystals of all kinds. Give an Amethyst golem a budding crystal and it will not only speed its growth, but also cut you in on the harvest.
Amethyst Golems will work with any Budding Crystal block in the pack. However, their ability to transform blocks into budding blocks is limited to Amethyst.

quests.title: Ars Nouveau
desc: With Ars Nouveau you will learn to harness the latent energy infused in all things to cast powerful spells, drive arcane machinery, and even to empower some cute friends along the way.
These quests will guide you through the mod, but be sure to refer back to the manual regularly for extra information.
~MuteTiefling

item.name: Flashing Archwood Sapling / Cascading Archwood Sapling / Vexing Archwood Sapling / Flourishing Archwood Sapling …

quests.title: Spell Turret
quests.subtitle: T-U-R-R-E-T, Turret
desc: The Spell Turret is an enhanced apparatus used to cast spells on a Redstone pulse. Source for the spell will be provided automatically from nearby Source Jars.
To set a spell, inscribe a Spell Parchment and Right-Click it on the Turret. It may use either Touch or Projectile forms in the spell.

quests.title: Source Links
quests.subtitle: Source Preserves
desc: Source may be found in any living thing, so it should come as no surprise that it may be condensed from most living matter. In a natural cycle, the Source contained in the living is simply passed around from plant to animal and back. A nearby Sourcelink, however, may be used to re-direct that ephemeral dew into specially prepared Source Jars, preserving it for later use.
Each Sourcelink has its own requirements which are covered in detail in the Worn Notebook.

● Alchemical Source Links re-absorb the condensed Source present in Potions. Any beneficial spell stored in an adjacent Potion Jar will be absorbed, producing Source. More is produced from stronger potions.
● Fluid Source Links absorb certain liquids from tanks placed below it, converting them into Source at different rates.

quests.title: Runic Chalk
quests.subtitle: Chalk it up to Experience
desc: What good is magic if we can’t make it work for us?
Save some effort and imprint spells into a Rune instead. Any time an entity meets it, the spell will trigger. Source for the spell will be provided automatically from nearby Source Jars.
To use Runic Chalk, begin by Right-Clicking it on the ground to draw a rune. Now Right-Click the rune with a prepared Spell Parchment. Valid Spell Parchments must begin with the Touch Form.

quests.title: Spell Parchment
quests.subtitle: Jousting Snails
desc: With some work, common paper can be infused to be a better receptacle for magic. Once infused, these written spells can be used in a variety of ways.

To prepare a Parchment with a spell, first design the spell within the Spell Book. Then place a Parchment on the Scribe's Table and Sneak Right-Click the table with the Spell Book to transfer the selected spell over to the Parchment.
Parchments may be re-used, though it can be useful to keep a library of scribed Parchments to be able to quickly re-apply the spell.

quests.title: Magebloom Seed
quests.subtitle: Putting Down Roots
desc: The Magebloom sits at the border between the mundane and the arcane. It grows as any other plant, but its roots reach through the veil, soaking in more of the Source that infuses the earth.
Growing these will serve two purposes to a budding practitioner:
First, they produce more Source than any mundane plants when grown.
Second, they can be woven into a fabric that when worn close serves as a personal battery for Source.

quests.title: Enchanting Apparatus
quests.subtitle: The Spirit is Willing but the Flesh is Spongy and Bruised
desc: One's own reservoir of Source is limited: the flesh can only hold so much. Certain magical materials exist to assist this but they themselves require access to greater reservoirs to even make.
An external apparatus is therefore required to hold the reagents for such creative endeavors and to assist in funneling the Source into them safely.

To construct the Enchanting Apparatus, place down the Arcane Core with the Enchanting Apparatus on top of it. The Pedestals must be placed within three blocks of the Core. If a recipe indicates a Source cost, a filled Source Jar must also be placed nearby.
To work with the Apparatus, first place the reagents on the pedestals and the focus in the Enchanting Apparatus itself. All items will be consumed during the craft.

The Enchanting Apparatus may also be used to apply specific enchantments to tools and armor, simplifying the process of getting certain enchants to round out a piece of gear. These recipes are only listed in the Worn Notebook.

quests.title: Curious Trinkets
quests.subtitle: Draw me like your French girls
desc: Source is a fickle thing, and keeping it in one place long enough to use can be challenging at best. Aspiring practitioners may find themselves struggling to channel Source for very long. Besides magical accoutrements woven from Mana Fibers, certain other materials can be molded into useful trinkets to serve as an extension of one's own reserves.
Refer to the Worn Notebook's section on Magical Equipment for recipes and to discover more useful curios.

quests.title: Source Relay
quests.subtitle: Witches Abroad
desc: Source permeates all things. Left to its own, it spreads and infuses but rarely collects. Binding it in jars is an excellent way of storing source for later use, but moving it from place to place can be a touchy subject.

Source Relays serve this purpose. They provide a controlled channel for Source to flow through without dissipating back into the world. Source Relays may be linked to other relays as well as jars to provide safe transit from one place to another.
Use a Dominion Wand to set the links.

quests.title: Source Relay: Splitter
quests.subtitle: Equal Rites
desc: Splitter Relays are capable of both sending to and receiving from multiple other Source Relays.
For instance, multiple Source farms might be brought together to transfer across a single line of Relays, or branches might be made to supply Source to different locations for Turrets or Crafting.
They share the same range limitations of normal Relays, but by combining the two a network of Source can be easily strung across an area, making it available wherever it is needed.

quests.title: Bookwyrm Charm
quests.subtitle: Boop the Snoot
desc: An amicable being with a driving need to organize, Bookwyrms are central to using Ars Nouveau’s item management system which allows linking many inventories together into a single access point.

quests.title: Starbuncle Charm
quests.subtitle: In Search of the Golden Acorn
desc: Starbuncles are curious forest critters with a love for all things shiny. Gold, in particular. They may be befriended by tossing them a small amount of gold. Once befriended, they will assist by collecting items and moving them to inventories.
They may be instructed what to do by using a Dominion Wand. Their behavior may be further modified by giving them some Starbuncle Shades or a Wixie hat.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Starbuncles.
These critters can be an uncommon sight even in ancient forests. If none can be found, consider summoning them with the Altar of Birthing.

quests.title: Whirlisprig Charm
quests.subtitle: Whispering Winds
desc: Whirlisprigs are the care-takers of the forest, helping new growth to flourish. They will come with you willingly if you honor them by planting a tree in their stead. Once befriended, a Sprig will tend to a small area and gift you with their bounty. Plant down trees, crops, flowers, and other natural items and over time the Sprig will grow more of these and offer them to you.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Sprigs.
The number of wild Sprigs has dwindled in recent times. If none can be found, consider summoning them with the Altar of Birthing.

quests.title: Familiar Friends
quests.subtitle: Auto-magically
desc: Not all tasks lend themselves to completion by simple automatons like a turret or a rune. There exist certain magical creatures in this world that will help an aspiring practitioner quite willingly if asked nicely.

item.name: Drygmy Shards / Whirlisprig Shards / Siren Shards / Starbuncle Shards …

quests.title: Wixie Charm
quests.subtitle: Wyrd Sisters
desc: Wouldn't it be helpful to have a hand around the Crafting Table? Someone to pass you this, or fetch you that? Or perhaps they could just do the job for you while you further your studies of the arcane?
The Wixie is the friend you seek. Bound by casting Dispel on a Witch at low health, Wixies are summoned by using their Charm on a standard Cauldron, transforming it into a Wixie Cauldron.

To specify what the Wixie ought to craft, simply make one of the items yourself and Right-Click it on her cauldron. She'll take care of gathering the required items from nearby inventories. She will need a jar of Source nearby, however, to keep her productive.

quests.title: Potion Jar
quests.subtitle: Nanny Ogg's Cookbook
desc: Simple item crafting isn’t the only thing these crafty ladies have hidden up their sleeves. They’re quite the adept in a brewery as well, making potions of all types.
Just like with regular crafting, Wixies will need some extras at hand. A Source Jar, a Potion Jar, and an inventory of ingredients.

Each Wixie can only make one potion type at a time. The type is determined by first brewing one the traditional way and, with potion in hand, right-click her cauldron to set the recipe. She’ll get to work as soon as everything is available. Just like traditional brewing, potions must be made in steps. One Wixie will make an Awkward Potion with Nether Wart, the next will add a Golden Carrot to make a Night Vision potion, and a third could add Redstone to extend it.

It is recommended to take that potion and stick it in the jar immediately so that the potion jar can be locked to that type. Sneak + Right-Click the jar with a Dominion Wand to lock it to that type of potion. This is handy when multiple Wixies are at work in the same area.

quests.title: Potion Melder
quests.subtitle: Subtle Infusions
desc: The clever arcanist finds ways to save themselves time, and nothing wastes time like drinking five different potions in preparation for a fight. Why not mix them and drink them all at once?
This is exactly what the Potion Melder does.
The Potion Melder needs two Potion Jars to act as inputs and a third to act as an output.
Using a Dominion Wand, link two Potion Jars to the Melder. These will serve as the inputs. Then, link the Melder to one last Potion Jar to accept the mixed brew.
The process uses some Source from a nearby Source Jar but produces potions that combine all the effects of the two inputs. This process can be chained to produce potions with multiple effects.

quests.title: Potion Flask
desc: Multiple doses all bottled up and ready to go in an eco-friendly re-usable package.
Each Flask can hold up to eight doses of potion and may even be enchanted to increase the potency or duration of the potions within.

quests.title: Enchanter's Wand
quests.subtitle: Cast Wide, Your Net
desc: A rather traditional Arcane Focus, the Casting Wand may be inscribed with a single spell in much the same way as inscribing a Parchment.

Contrary to other casting methods, however, no Form is required on the spell designed in the Spell Book. All spells cast from a Casting Wand are automatically granted the Projectile form for free as well as a level of Accelerate.
This means extra slots for adding Effects or Augments, making them ideal for specialized tools.
Other Arcane Foci exist granting similar benefits, such as the Enchanter’s Mirror and Enchanter’s Sword. The Worn Notebook covers these and more.

quests.title: Ritual Brazier
quests.subtitle: I Love the Smell of Napalm in the Morning
desc: Nothing quite says “Magic” like burning reagents on a pyre!
With a specially crafted Tablet to guide the process and optional reagents to augment it, the Ritual Brazier is capable of producing a wide variety of effects.

To get it going, Right-Click the Brazier with any Tablet. If extra materials are required, they should be thrown atop the flame to be consumed. Once everything is set, Right-Click again with an empty hand to finalize the ritual.

quests.title: Disintegration
quests.subtitle: XP = MC Squared
desc: Killing monsters can be a … messy affair. Why not skip the trouble and simply distill them down into their very essence?
Monsters killed with this ritual will drop Experience Gems worth roughly double the XP they’d drop normally. But, all drops are lost in the process.

quests.title: Cloudshaping
quests.subtitle: Here Comes the Rain Again, Falling On My Head Like a Memory
desc: Sometimes it feels like the rain just never lets up. It has soaked through your armor, flooded your cave, corroded all those fancy schmancy circuits you were told would solve your problems.
But did they solve the rain? No. Now let’s magic that rain away.

quests.title: Celestial Manipulation
quests.subtitle: Ain't nobody got time for that!
desc: Are your days too short? Not enough time for your nocturnal pursuits?
Consider bending time and space to bring the sun or moon around again to for that extra boost of energy or to finish charting out those constellations you find so fascinating.
Surely nothing bad could come of this?

quests.title: Challenge
quests.subtitle: Hear Ye, Hear Ye
desc: All you Lowly Pillagers, Ravaging Vindicators, and Summoners of Questionable Merit are here-by formally summoned to participate in the coming tournaments!
Summons a Pillager Raid to your back door, just in time!

quests.title: Fertility and Growth
quests.subtitle: Magically Sustained Gestation
desc: If you sad in life – use MSG. If you happy in life – use MSG. Put MSG in everything, it’ll turn out better. You just get baby? Put MSG on baby, make smarter.
Magic does wonders when it comes to growing crops and breeding animals. Combine these two rituals to keep your livestock busy and growing quickly.

quests.title: Warp Portals
quests.subtitle: A Wizard Did It!
desc: Going somewhere?
Bring some supplies along before setting out, as having a quick way back and forth can be very handy.
A Warp Scroll may be bound to a location via Right-Click and then used again later to return the player to that exact spot. The Scroll is consumed on use, however.

Alternatively, a portal may be built using any type of Sourcestone in a rectangular shape.  Place a filled Source Jar nearby and toss a bound Warp Scroll through the frame to ignite it, linking it to the coordinates from the scroll. Items, mobs, even spells may pass through these portals, though they are incapable of crossing between dimensions.
Ghostweave, Mirrorweave, and Falseweave may all be used for portal frames as well, allowing for endless customization!

item.name: Sourcestone / Sourcestone: Small Bricks / Smooth Sourcestone / Sourcestone: Mosaic …

quests.title: Drygmy Charm
quests.subtitle: Very A-moose-ing.
desc: Found most anywhere that wild beasts roam, Drygmies are spirits bound to the earth, tending her flock. Through their magic, they can gather items from all manner of beast without causing them harm in any way. They may be enticed to work for you by showing them a token of their mortal enemies: Wilden Defenders.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Drygmies.
The number of wild Drygmies has dwindled in recent times. If none can be found, consider summoning them with the Altar of Birthing.

quests.title: Source Relays: Collectors and Depositors
quests.subtitle: Ebb and Flow
desc: Where Source Relays are typically limited to pulling from or sending to a single linked Source Jar, these specialized Relays will automatically pull from or send to any nearby jars without being linked.

A Depositor therefore makes a great tool for keeping jars filled for other purposes, such as forming Warp Portals. Using both a Collector and a Depositor together also makes for a handy automation friendly means of transferring Source. Fill jars in one location, pick them up, and drain them elsewhere.

item.name: Source Relay: Collector / Source Relay: Depositor

quests.title: Source Relay: Warper
desc: Warp Relays serve as long range Source transportation. By linking two together, Source may be transferred any distance in the same dimension.
A small amount of Source is used in stabilizing this connection over longer distances.

quests.title: Starbuncle
quests.subtitle: Don't You Crittersize Me!
desc: The only thing keeping these cute critters from being a crunchy treat to larger predators are their swift little feet. A power they’ll gladly lend for the price of friendship.

quests.title: Wixie
quests.subtitle: A Spoonful of Sugar Helps the Medicine Go Down...
desc: Though quite pleasant to hang around in more domestic environments, Wixies are known to be quite resourceful in a fight, flinging dangerous brews hither and thither to fend off would be attackers.

quests.title: Drygmy
quests.subtitle: As Luck Would Hoove It
desc: Powerful Earth Spirits with a knack for finding things, Drygmies impart their knowledge upon their friends, bolstering magic and turning up extra loot.

quests.title: Bookwyrm
quests.subtitle: I Will Dewey Decimate You
desc: With their deep link to Source, Bookwyrms make excellent allies, collecting anything they find laying around and bringing it to you.

quests.title: Whirlisprig
quests.subtitle: The Queen of Sauce
desc: Variety is the spice of life, and none know this better than the Sylvan folk. Everything tastes better when they’re around.

quests.title: Binding
