quests.subtitle: Friendship is Magic
desc: For ages, sorcerers have been befriending creatures of all sorts to assist in their work. These friendships run deep, forming a symbiotic partnership that grants incredible longevity to the creature and potent abilities to the sorcerer.
Perform the Ritual of Binding near an amenable creature to signal your desire to bond with it. Should it acquiesce, it will grant a token that may be added to a spell book to summon them at any time.
Each familiar grants unique bonuses that are detailed in the Worn Notebook. Explore each to find just the right friend.

quests.title: Getting Started: Source Gems
quests.subtitle: Like Sweet Morning Dew
desc: Source is the driving energy behind every spell and arcane device in Ars Nouveau, but it must be condensed out of the world to harness it for anything beyond the simplest of uses. To that end, we’ll begin with an Imbuement Chamber.

The Imbuement Chamber itself requires Source to operate but can slowly draw some out of the environment for simple crafts; the simplest of which is the Source Gem. Once able, place a filled Source Jar nearby to greatly enhance the crafting speed.

The item in the center of the recipe is to be inserted into the Chamber itself, while any items surrounding it are to be placed on nearby Pedestals. The items on the Pedestals act as keys and are never consumed, while the central item will be converted to the result.

quests.title: Spellcasting
desc: From novice to master alike, much time is dedicated to the art of spell craft, be it preparing and learning new Glyphs, enchanting personal Arcane Foci, or preparing Spell Glyphs or Turrets.
These activities all center around the Scribe’s Table.
New glyphs may be inscribed by Right-Clicking the Scribe’s Table with a Spell Book to open the Codex of all glyphs, known or unknown.

To scribe a glyph, merely locate and select it in the Codex. Follow this by throwing the required ingredients at the table to finish the craft. Finally, learn the Glyph by Right-Clicking it in the air.
Note: Glyphs are stored on the player, not the Spell Book. So, losing a Spell Book does not mean the loss of learned glyphs.

quests.title: Alteration Table
quests.subtitle: Tailor Made
desc: Threads may be woven into a Thread Slot on applicable armor by way of the Alteration Table.
The equipment is to be placed on the right-hand side, whereupon the parchment on the left will display the available slots.

To apply a Thread, Right-Click it onto the side with the parchment. Threads are applied from top to bottom. They may be removed at any time and re-applied, however, and are not lost when removed. Right-clicking with an empty hand will remove them top to bottom.

Do note that some Threads have different or stronger effects when applied in higher tier Thread Slots. Some, like the Thread of Gliding, require a specific level slot to be applied at all. Applying the same Thread more than once will generally have no effect.

quests.title: Siren Charm
quests.subtitle: Darlin' it's better, down where it's wetter
desc: Though they’re often viewed with mistrust and labeled as man-eating beasts (it was just the one time, ok?), Sirens are really only interested in gathering shiny things. Once befriended, a Siren will slowly collect treasures from their watery homes, tucking them away for safe keeping. The prettier their environment, the more likely they are to share those treasures with their friends.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Sirens.
The number of wild Sirens has dwindled in recent times. If none can be found, consider summoning them with the Altar of Birthing.

quests.title: Splash Flask Cannon
desc: The Splash Flask Cannon is a simple device designed to further weaponize harmful potions. Any potion fed into it may be thrown as if it had been brewed into a Splash Potion.
Combined with Flasks, these can make powerful tools in combat.

quests.title: Potion Diffuser
quests.subtitle: Potpourri for the Soul
desc: The Potion Diffuser greatly enhances the efficiency of potions by applying a single dose to all creatures in the area at an enhanced duration.

quests.title: Alchemist's Crown
desc: A wizard in battle has no time to worry about such trivialities as quaffing a potion. The Alchemist’s Crown handles that for them.

By opening the radial menu and selecting one of the potions detected in one’s inventory, the Alchemists Crown will automatically re-apply that potion whenever it’s duration ends. By keeping a few flasks on hand, potion effects can be made to last quite a long time without needing to drink repeatedly.

quests.title: Bound Script: Siren
quests.subtitle: Flippin' your fins really will get you far
desc: Truly an indispensable companion to keep when exploring the depths, Sirens will grant their friends a bonus to water spells and also bestow Dolphin’s Grace upon them while swimming.

quests.title: Bound Script: Flarecannon
quests.subtitle: Burninate the land
desc: When kept as a close companion, Flarecannon will impart some of power upon their friends, boosting fire magics and granting temporary resistance to fire.

quests.title: Flarecannon Charm
quests.subtitle: Five-Alarm Fire
desc: Powerful arcane constructs, these golems known as Flarecannon serve to protect, burning anything hostile that comes in their range.
Refer to the Worn Notebook for an in-depth guide on using Flarecannon.

quests.title: Magical Vestments
quests.subtitle: I shall wear midnight
desc: Ideal equipment for the dedicated Wizard, these magically enhanced vestments offer more than simple protection.

Primarily, they act as a personal battery for Source, giving the caster more to draw on in battle. However, they may also have special Threads woven into them to offer more unique and customized boons.

Each set of armor may be upgraded in the Enchantment Apparatus through three different tiers. At each tier, they gain more slots for accepting Threads. The recipe for upgrading the tier is shown in the Worn Notebook.

item.name: Sorceror's Collar / Arcanist's Hat / Battlemage's Hood
Sorceror's Wrap / Arcanist's Robes / Battlemage's Gambeson
Sorceror's Leggings / Arcanist's Pants / Battlemage's Legguards
Sorceror's Footpads / Arcanist's Treads / Battlemage's Boots

quests.title: Awakening
desc: Golems have long been used by those of sorcerous ability to assist them in their work. With a Tablet of Awakening, an experienced mage may bring a form of sentience to Archwood Trees and Budding Amethyst. The resulting creatures are known as Weald Walkers and Amethyst Golems, respectively.
Weald Walkers act as guardians, keeping hostile creatures at bay with their brutish strength.

Amethyst Golems, meanwhile, are more fastidious in nature, gently caring for and harvesting Amethyst from nearby Budding Amethyst. Normal Amethyst blocks in their charge may even be made to bud and grow more.

quests.title: Containment
quests.subtitle: Modern problems require modern solutions
desc: Working with others can be a messy business. Wizards of old spent a great deal of time and effort trying to keep their Drygmies and Villager friends safe from harm. Containment Jars offer a modern solution to this age-old problem.
Any creature under the effect of a Ritual of Containment will be automatically drawn into a nearby empty Containment Jar.
Contained creatures may still be interacted with, however. Villagers with a job will continue to trade, Cows may be milked, and Drygmies will continue to harvest from them.
Naturally, this also makes an excellent means of transport as well, as the jars may be picked up and moved around freely. To release a creature from the Jar, simply cast Dispel upon it.

quests.title: Spell Focuses
quests.subtitle: Focus Pocus
desc: When a wizard chooses to specialize in a particular school of magic, often they will invest in a Focus to enhance their chosen school.
Equipped in a dedicated Curio slot, each focus grants unique boons to their school which are detailed in the Worn Notebook.

item.name: Lesser Focus of Fire / Lesser Focus of Water / Lesser Focus of Air / Lesser Focus of Earth …

quests.title: Scryer's Oculus
quests.subtitle: You Lookin’ at Me Lookin’ at You
desc: On occasion, it can be quite helpful to be able to see into an area without being there in person. Especially environments that may pose a hazard to the person.
A Scryer’s Oculus enables the wizard to perform exactly that sort of long-range monitoring.

Place a Scry Crystal in the location to be monitored, Right-Click it with a Blank Parchment to record the location and place the resulting Scryer’s Scroll on a pedestal near the Oculus. When approached, the Oculus allows the Wizard to select from any of the nearby Scrolls to view the location.

quests.title: Starbuncle Logistics
desc: In addition to transporting items and looking stylish, Starbuncles may be given a few additional accessories to further enhance their abilities.
Configuring their pickup and drop off locations remains the same as with Items; by using a Dominion Wand after equipping them with the appropriate accessory.

Need them to access a specific side? Use a Direction Scroll to set their preferred side. These are set by looking in the desired direction and Sneak + Right-Clicking them. Then use the scroll on the Starbuncle.

quests.title: StarbAttery
quests.subtitle: Watt is love? Baby don't hertz me, n-ohm-ore
desc: A tiny little backpack for transporting FE from place to place.

quests.title: Starbucket
quests.subtitle: Looking a little sloshed
desc: Sealed to prevent spillages, the Starbucket allows the Starbuncle to transport any fluid.

quests.title: Starballoon
quests.subtitle: Let's not get carried away
desc: With a Starballoon in tow, a Starbuncle may transport Mekanism gasses from place to place.

quests.title: Fluid Jar
desc: Though suitable for any fluid, Fluid Containment Jars are particularly useful for working with Potions.

When fluid potions made by other mods such as Create, Hexerei, Thermal, or Immersive Engineering are stored in a Containment Jar, they’ll automatically be deposited into a Potion Jar placed atop it. Meaning any potion may be easily converted for use in devices such as Potion Melders or other alchemical tools offered by Ars Nouveau.

quests.title: Source Condenser
quests.subtitle: Source Reserves
desc: A simple device used for converting Source in its natural form to a more… fluid state, allowing it to be moved around by way of pipes or other conveyances.

quests.title: Energy Conversion
desc: Once thought to be entirely separate, the magical energies know as Source, Aura, and FE are in fact all facets of the same energy. By making use of special crystals, it becomes possible to convert between them with ease.

Pulsating Crystals work by absorbing Source from nearby Source Jars and converting it into usable FE. Should the area contain sufficient Aura, it will also be consumed, greatly enhancing the FE generated.

Resonating Crystals, on the other hand, set up an internal resonance with FE, converting it back into Source or Aura. If a Source Jar is near enough, it will send it there. If there is no jar, or if it is 100% full, the Resonating Crystal will instead convert the incoming FE to Aura and diffuse it into the atmosphere.

item.name: Dim Pulsating Crystal / Bright Pulsating Crystal / Iridescent Pulsating Crystal
Dim Resonating Crystal / Bright Resonating Crystal / Iridescent Resonating Crystal

quests.title: Storage Lectern
desc: The Storage Lectern is the central access point for Bookwyrm based storage. Place one down anywhere and Right-Click one or more Bookwyrm Charms onto it to bind them to the Lectern.
The Bookwyrms are responsible for moving items around and each one may manage up to eight inventories. So, a Lectern with two Bookwyrms attached could be bound to up to 16 nearby inventories.

To bind an inventory to the Lectern, first Sneak Right-Click the inventory with a Dominion Wand, then Right-Click the Lectern. The Lectern may be Right-Clicked again with a Dominion Wand to highlight all attached inventories and Bookwyrms.
This system pairs very nicely with large storage containers like Drawers, Item Vaults, and Dimensional Storage Actuators, creating dense storage capabilities using fewer Bookwyrm connections.

The Lecterns may also be chained to allow remote access to the central storage. Place a new lectern anywhere within 30 blocks of the primary lectern, Right-Click the new one with the Wand, then Right-Click the primary with the wand. The new Lectern will now have access to all of the inventories of the first. Just keep chaining in this way as far as desired to have terminals throughout your home!
Note: Chained Lecterns may not have Bookwyrms or Inventories bound to them. Doing so will sever the connection with the primary network and create a new separate network.

Finally, it should be mentioned that any unbound inventory placed directly adjacent to a Lectern will act as an input for the entire system. Any items that find their way into this inventory will be automatically sorted out to linked inventories by the Bookwyrms. This works for remote Lecterns as well. Items may also be inserted directly into the Lectern via hoppers or other automated logistics.

quests.title: Repository
desc: The Repository is a special block that can hold as much as a Double Chest in a single block space. Unlike a standard Chest, however, they retain their name when broken. This ties in nicely with another feature of the Lectern: Named Tabs

Any named inventories that are bound to the Lectern will show up in a special tab in the interface. Inventories sharing the same name all share the tab and the contents of all of these inventories is grouped together. This allows for some manual organization, such as putting all gems in one set of inventories, or special equipment in another. Think of these as a search group, allowing quick access to all the items at a click.

This feature works with any inventory that can be named in an Anvil, however, it works best with those that retain their name on pickup to avoid having to rename them. Some other examples include Shulker Boxes, Smart Chests, Reinforced Chests, Wooden Storage Crates, and Reinforced Storage Crates to name a few.

quests.title: Display Case
desc: Display Cases are a simple Redstone device to read the contents of an inventory. They may be linked to any inventory or even a Storage Lectern and can output a signal when the configured item is either above or below a defined threshold.
Select the inventory to bind it to with the Dominion Wand. Sneak Right-Click for regular inventories or just a simple Right-Click for a Lectern, then Right-Click the placed Display Case to bind it.
To set the item to monitor, simply Right-Click the item into the Case. This works with Item Scrolls as well.
To set the quantity, use an empty hand to Right-Click the Case to increase and Left-Click to decrease. Sneak Click will increase or decrease by bounds of eight.
To invert the signal, Sneak Right-Click the Case with the Dominion Wand.

quests.title: Enchanter's Eye
desc: Far from home and need a few more potions to top up? The Enchanter’s Eye allows remote casting to a fixed location when bound to a Scry Crystal, or multiple locations with Scryer’s Scrolls.
As a simple example of how this may be useful, a Scry Crystal placed facing a Storage Lectern would allow the following spell form to access the Lectern remotely:
&5Touch&r > &2Interact&r
Adding Sensitive to the spell form would allow remote filling of a flask. Simply hold the flask in the off hand and ensure the Scry Crystal is set facing a Potion Jar:
&5Touch&r > &2Interact&r > &6Sensitive&r

quests.title: Stabilized Warp Scroll
desc: Much like standard Warp Scrolls, Stabilized Warp Scrolls may be used to create portals. They offer two advantages, however.
First, the scroll may be used to bind to coordinates in other dimensions, allowing cross-dimensional transportation.
Second, it may be used on a block at any time to generate a temporary portal to the bound coordinates. This does not consume the scroll.

quests.title: Amethyst Golem
quests.subtitle: Don't Be Shy, Be a Little Boulder!
desc: With their deep connection with the earth, Amethyst Golems make powerful familiars who strengthen one's ties to the ground.

quests.title: Amethyst Golem Charm
quests.subtitle: It's Geo Time!
desc: These steadfast little creatures have an insatiable desire for crystals of all kinds. Give an Amethyst golem a budding crystal and it will not only speed its growth, but also cut you in on the harvest.
Amethyst Golems will work with any Budding Crystal block in the pack. However, their ability to transform blocks into budding blocks is limited to Amethyst.

quests.title: Item Router
quests.subtitle: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
desc: Modular Routers are very powerful tools for automation. They're a single block that can be augmented to do many things, like breaking blocks, sorting items, pushing items into remote inventories, or all of the above at once, and more!
All of the modules/upgrades/augments in Modular Routers have info tooltips, just hold 'i' while holding the mouse over them in JEI or your inventory for some hints as to how they operate.
(tooltips won't work if a JEI recipe window is open)
There is also a mod guidebook "Modular Routers Manual", which will have details on everything.

quests.title: XNet Controller
desc: xNet acts as a programmable logistics interface which can adapt to external conditions based on programmed logic. It can transfer Items, Fluids, Gases, and Power rapidly and in precise amounts in addition to its logic capabilities.
To get started, all that is required is a Controller, some Cables, and some Connectors of the same color. The Controller itself needs a small amount of power to operate as well.
Place Connectors against machines or Redstone devices, then use regular cables to connect them back to the Controller. Another Connector is required at the Controller as well.

All programming is performed within the Controller itself by first creating channels and then selecting connectors in the GUI to program what they will do. Watching a few videos on this is highly recommended, as it is not something that’s easily learned without visual guides.

item.name: Red Network Cable / Green Network Cable / Blue Network Cable / Yellow Network Cable
Red Connector / Green Connector / Blue Connector / Yellow Connector

quests.title: Redstone and Logic
desc: Mods bring a lot to the table when it comes to using redstone. From cable that can transmit 16 different signals at once, compact one-block timers or latches, or just wireless inter-dimensional connections, there's bound to be a solution to your redstone needs.

quests.title: Blank Module
desc: Modules represent the Router’s basic programming; at least one is required for the Router to do anything at all. Up to nine Modules may be installed in a single Router and each will activate in order from left to right whenever the Router activates.

quests.title: Distributor Module
desc: Distributor Modules function much like MK2 Senders and Pullers and are bound to a block in the same way. However, the Distributor may be bound to as many as eight different sides or blocks.
Open the module’s GUI to set it to transfer either into the Router or Out, and to set a distribution strategy, such as Round Robin or Random.

quests.title: Breaker Module
desc: The Breaker Module breaks blocks adjacent to the Router. It uses the properties of the Pickaxe used to craft it, including enchantments, break level, and other special features, so be sure to craft the Module with an appropriate Pickaxe.

quests.title: Activator Module
desc: Activator Modules will attempt to Right-Click blocks or entities with the item in their buffer.
They may also be used to attack entities if given a weapon and set to Attack mode.

quests.title: Vacuum Module
desc: Vacuum Modules are powerful automation tools that allow picking up items from the ground based on complex filters.
If Augmented with an XP Vacuum, they can even be used to collect XP orbs and convert it to compatible XP fluids or Bottles O’ Enchanting.

quests.title: Fluid Modules
desc: Fluid Modules work as either a Puller or a Sender, transferring fluids into or out of the router. Note that the Router has no built-in fluid tank to store anything, so one must be provided. A bucket or most modded tanks will work fine, simply place it in the Router’s buffer.
It will either interact with a tank or with fluid in the world, allowing it to place and collect fluid in a block space if desired.
The MK1 variant may only interact with a block space directly adjacent to the router. The direction may be set in the modules GUI.
The MK2 variant must be linked to a block space by Sneak Right-Clicking the module on the desired block.

item.name: Fluid Module Mk1 / Fluid Module Mk2

quests.title: Redstone Pen
desc: The Redstone Pen and Quill can "draw" redstone dust on any side of a block, with full manual control of connections. Just right click to start drawing! Just having a charged path running over a block won't power the block, but you can choose to do so by right clicking in the center of the redtone path with the pen.

The Quill uses up redstone dust from your inventory, while the Pen version is charged up with redstone and doesn't need any from your inventory. Craft the pen with dust or blocks to recharge it. The Pen also re-absorbs the redstone when you clear a segment of path by left clicking it.

quests.title: Redstone Link
desc: Cheap wireless redstone, with unlimited channels, and good but not unlimited range.
For a detailed explanation on how to use this, use the 'ponder' feature by holding your mouse over the item in JEI or an inventory, and holding the ponder key (default: w).

quests.title: Linked Controller
desc: Can remotly activate connected Redstone Links.
For a detailed explanation on how to use this, use the 'ponder' feature by holding your mouse over the item in JEI or an inventory, and holding the ponder key (default: w).

quests.title: Powered Latch
desc: Set the output with a signal at the back, and reset the output with a signal from the side. Perfect for toggling your power generation automatically.
For a detailed explanation on how to use this, use the 'ponder' feature by holding your mouse over the item in JEI or an inventory, and holding the ponder key (default: w).

quests.title: Redstone Proxy (Update)
desc: When attempting to read Redstone signals from non-vanilla sources, a Proxy block is often required. These should be placed so that the Redstone source points into the Proxy, and then the xNet Connector is placed against the Proxy itself.
In some cases, a block update is also required. For those, use the Redstone Proxy (update) block instead.

quests.title: Cog Block
desc: Acts like redstone dust, but in solid block form. Easy vertical transmission!

quests.title: RS Pen Relays
desc: Simple relays that can be placed on any side of a block. The tooltips explain how each one works.
When placing, right click the side of the block face you want the output side to face.

item.name: Redstone Relay / Inverted Redstone Relay / Bi-Stable Redstone Relay / Pulse Redstone Relay …

quests.title: Blank Upgrade
desc: Upgrades are installed in the Router itself and augment how it operates, such as speeding it up or making it immune to blast damage.

quests.title: Augment Core
desc: Augments are installed within individual Modules and apply only to that module, changing how it operates.

quests.title: Pulse Repeater
desc: Sends a pulse a set amount of time after receiving a signal
For a detailed explanation on how to use this, use the 'ponder' feature by holding your mouse over the item in JEI or an inventory, and holding the ponder key (default: w).

quests.title: Powered Toggle Latch
desc: Uses an input pulse to toggle the output. Use a repeater to send a pulse from the output back to the input, with a delay, to make a pulse lengthener.
For a detailed explanation on how to use this, use the 'ponder' feature by holding your mouse over the item in JEI or an inventory, and holding the ponder key (default: w).

quests.title: Filter Module
desc: The RF Tools filter is compatible with xNet and is required for tag filtering.
Insert the filter into one of the 4 slots at the top of the UI and choose which filter a connector uses with the 'filter index' button on the right.

quests.title: The Regulator Augment
desc: Regulator Augments act differently based on what Module they’re installed in. In general, they put a condition on when the module can act. For a Sender, they’ll only send if the target inventory has fewer items than the limit.
Check the entry in the Modular Routers Manual for details on how it changes each module.

quests.title: Stack Upgrade
desc: Speed and Stack Upgrades help to control how quickly the Router operates.
Install more Speed upgrades to get the Router to run through its program more frequently.
Stack Upgrades, on the other hand, allow the Router to move more items per operation. For example, moving a full stack of items every few seconds is generally more efficient than one item every tick.
Both may be combined, of course, to achieve the desired goal.

quests.title: Blast Upgrade
desc: Makes the router fully blast proof, making them immune to both TnT and Withers, making them a valuable upgrade for working with explosions or building Withers.

quests.title: Sender Modules
desc: Sender and Puller Modules send items to or pull items from remote inventories, respectively.

The MK1 variants may only operate in a straight line, but line of sight is not required. Therefore, a Puller MK1 could retrieve items from a chest on the other side of a wall. They will only interact with the first inventory in range, however.

MK2 variants do away with the straight line, instead interacting with a specific side of a block. Sneak Right-Click the module on the side of a block it should interact with to bind it. For example, to retrieve the output of a furnace, it would need to be bound to the bottom face of the furnace.

MK3 Senders go one step further still, allowing the router to send any distance, even across dimensions. The remote inventory must be loaded, of course. Otherwise, they are bound to a side of an inventory the same way as MK2 variants.

item.name: Sender Module Mk1 / Sender Module Mk2 / Sender Module Mk3
Puller Module Mk1 / Puller Module Mk2

quests.title: Energy Distributor Module
desc: The Energy Output and Energy Distribution Modules allow the Router to supply power to nearby blocks.
Where the Energy Output Module may only output to adjacent blocks, the Distribution Module may send to up to eight remote blocks within range.

In either case, some source of power is required. This can be in the form of an energy containing item in the Router’s Buffer, or from the Router’s internal energy buffer if Energy Upgrades are installed.

quests.title: Energy Upgrade
desc: Grants the Router some amount of energy storage, allowing the router to handle both Item and Energy transfer at once.

quests.title: Range Augments
desc: When installed in Modules that work at range, these will adjust the working area. A Vacuum Module, for example, could have its range reduced to prevent picking up items for some other automation, or a Sender could have the range increased to reach further inventories.

item.name: Range Down Augment / Range Up Augment

quests.title: Camouflage Upgrade
desc: Sneak Right-Click these on another block and then install it in a Router to upgrade its look and feel. Make the Router look like practically anything at all, even flowers!

quests.title: Extruder Module
desc: Whether for automation, retractable drawbridges, or fancy doors, the Extruder Module may be of use in many situations.

The MK1 variant will place blocks from the Router’s buffer on a high Redstone signal and then retract them again on a low signal. Bear in mind that the Breaker module used to craft it must have been crafted with a sufficiently high tier Pickaxe to break whatever blocks are being retrieved.
When combined with some external logic, these can be great for collecting blocks from in-world transformations, such as oxidized copper.
The MK2 variant is mostly just for aesthetic uses such as bridges or doors. All the blocks it places are ‘ghost’ blocks and will allow a player to walk on them or prevent them from passing through.
With a Mimic Augment installed, the blocks retain some of the target block’s properties, such as light level and hardness.
With a Pushing Augment installed, the Extruder will push entities as blocks are extruded.
When using multiple Extruders together, the Sync Upgrade can help ensure that they all run simultaneously.

item.name: Extruder Module Mk1 / Extruder Module Mk2

quests.title: More Filtering
desc: Need more advanced filters? Or just a bigger filter? Modular Routers has a variety of filter items that may be used in the filter slots of all Modules, enabling some truly advanced capabilities.

item.name: Bulk Item Filter / Inspection Filter / Mod Filter / Regex Filter

quests.title: Pulse Extender
desc: Holds redstone signal specified amount of time after initial signal was removed.
For a detailed explanation on how to use this, use the 'ponder' feature by holding your mouse over the item in JEI or an inventory, and holding the ponder key (default: w).

quests.title: Fluid Transfer Upgrade
desc: Fluid Transfer Upgrades act a bit like Stack upgrades for Fluids, allowing the Router to handle more fluid per activation. Rates will still need to be set in the Fluid Module.

quests.title: Filter Round Robin Augment
desc: Filter Round Robin Augments change the nature of a Modules filter, turning it into a round robin list instead. Each time the Module activates, it will cycle to the next item in the filter and only act on that. This can be very useful for times when the Router should pick up a different item each time it activates.

quests.title: Pickup Delay Augment
desc: Used in Flingers and Droppers, Pickup Delay Augments prevent the dropped or flung item from being immediately picked up by a player. Each one adds a ten second delay.

quests.title: Fast Pickup Augment
desc: Fast Pickup Augments are used in Vacuum Modules and force the Module to ignore any pickup delay on the item, picking it up as soon as possible.

quests.title: Redstone Augment
desc: The Redstone Augment allows a single Module to be disabled or enabled based on the Redstone signal the Router is receiving.
The Router still needs to run for this to work, however. So, it should be set to Redstone Mode: Always while this is installed in a module, allowing specific Modules to be disabled or enabled.

quests.title: Stack Augment
desc: Stack Augments simply increase the stack size for a given Module independent of other Modules.
For example, a Puller could be given two Stack Augments to allow it to pull four items at a time, then four Senders could be used to distribute those four items evenly to four different inventories.

quests.title: Flinger Module
desc: Flingers and Droppers are a great way to get items into the world.
While Droppers will simply drop the item straight down, Flingers can impart some velocity like a Vanilla Dispenser. The speed and direction are configurable, however.
When setting the Speed, start small and experiment; the Flinger is quite powerful. A Speed of 1.0 and Pitch of 45.0 can launch items about 18 blocks. At max speed, the items may never be seen again.

quests.title: Redstone Wiring
desc: Redstone Wiring represents an advancement in Redstone technology, allowing a dedicated Engineer to build complex logic circuits that are less prone to the failings of traditional Redstone Dust. A color-coded channel system also allows a single small network to interact with multiple independent machines.
Redstone Wires may be stretched between Redstone Wire Connectors, Probe Connectors, or Interface Connectors. These carry the Redstone signal without the signal decaying.
Redstone Wire Connectors act as Input and Output points for a signal and may be placed directly on a block. They must have their mode and color channel set by using a Screwdriver on them.

Redstone Probe Connectors act very much like Comparators with a few extra built-in features. Most Immersive Engineering machines will output special comparator signals that may also be read by this Connector. Refer to the Engineer’s Manual for specifics about each machine.
Redstone Interface Connectors are used in conjunction with special blocks like Item Batchers and Logic Units, allowing the signals used by those blocks to be read.

quests.title: Logic Unit
desc: The Logic Unit represents a compact and potentially very complex Redstone Logic computer. Up to ten Logic Circuits must be programmed and placed within and a Redstone Interface Connector attached to the outside.

Whenever the inbound signal changes, the Unit will cycle through each of the installed circuits once, performing each operation, allowing multiple logic gates to be applied to a signal, or even multiple color codes to be used as Input and Output signals.

quests.title: Engineer's Circuit Table
desc: Logic Circuits themselves are crafted in the Engineer’s Circuit Table.
This workbench requires power, which is input from the back, as well as some quantity of Runic Proto-Boards, Lead Wire, and Vacuum Tubes. Different logic operations will require different quantities.
Circuits are programmed with an operator as well as Input and Output colors.
When ready, the completed circuit is withdrawn from the right side of the GUI.
Circuits may have their Inputs and Outputs reprogrammed by placing them back in the upper slot, but the operator is locked in upon first creation.

quests.title: Redstone Modules
quests.subtitle: Redstone Evolution
desc: Redstone Modules are used to read and output Redstone signals by transmitting them over a pipe network. Each Module may be set to a color channel, allowing up to 16 different signals over the same tube network.
This requires no air and signals do not degrade over distance.

Installing a Module Expansion card into a Module in Receiving mode, it may be set to behave exactly like a vanilla Comparator, getting a signal from blocks that emit special values for Comparators, like the Refinery.

By installing such a card into a Module in Emitting mode, several features become available. For example, by making use of the color channels, it can function as an AND gate, OR gate, compare against another channel or against a constant value, and much more. By chaining them together, some truly compact Redstone logic can be made.

quests.title: Universal Sensor
quests.subtitle: Under the Radar
desc: The Universal Sensor is a powerful block that will output a redstone signal based on various conditions, such as detecting a nearby player, when a player Right-Clicks a block, the presence of blocks, light level, or even the current heat of a block.
When reading heat, try aiming it at a heat pipe or a PNC:R machine, rather than at an inventory with a heat frame.

quests.title: Decoration
quests.subtitle: Dirt Hut No More
desc: Welcome to the Building Chapter
This section contains a list of building/decoration based mods, and a handful of tools to help you get the job done, and set you on your way to becoming a seasoned builder.

quests.title: Connected Glass
quests.subtitle: I can see all obstacles in my way
desc: Connected Glass adds additional glass blocks and panes with connected textures. This of course covers the clear glass, and all 16 dyed glass types from Vanilla.

quests.title: Simply Light
quests.subtitle: Let there be light
desc: The mod name really says it all. It's simply that, a lights mod.
But don't let the name fool you. Simply Light offers a wide range of lights to keep your base lit with style.

quests.title: Framed Blocks
quests.subtitle: Sky is the limit
desc: Are you looking for Glass Stairs? or maybe a Netherite door? How about an Endstone Sign? Well, look no further.
Framed Blocks introduces a blank template of various shapes and blocks which mimics the texture of the block clicked on them.
They can even be made to glow by right clicking them with glowstone!

quests.title: Framed Drawers
quests.subtitle: Build-a-Drawer
desc: Are you fed up with that Oak Drawer that is sticking out like a sore thumb in the middle of your build, completely mismatching your building palette?

Framed Drawers gives you a blank template which you can combine in a crafting table with different blocks to use their texture instead, whether it's the front, the sides, or the trim, these Framed Drawers are highly customizable visually.
Needless to say, Functional Storage has more than just a single drawer style template, it actually has a template for each type of drawer, whether it is a 1x2, 2x2 or even a Compacting Drawer.

item.name: Framed Drawer (1x1) / Framed Drawer (1x2) / Framed Drawer (2x2) / Framed Compacting Drawer

quests.title: Engineer's Decor
quests.subtitle: Immersive Decorating
desc: If you love the industrial look of Immersive Engineering, then you will probably love Engineer's Decor.

This mod adds a handful of decorative blocks that should feel right at home in your Immersive Engineering base. Whether it is a DANGER! sign, or an industrial platforms and support beams, Engineer's Decor has got you covered.

quests.title: Decorative Blocks
quests.subtitle: Stay a while and listen...
desc: If you are into your medieval or rustic builds, whether it is a castle on a cliff, a cabin in the woods, or a hearty tavern for a weary traveler, Decorative Blocks will have some blocks that fits your style.
Decorative Blocks offers many nicely textured and well designed blocks for your building needs.

quests.title: General Building Tools
quests.subtitle: The right tools for the job
desc: Rome wasn’t built in a day, but with tools like these it certainly could have been.
Read on to discover some handy tools to vastly reduce the time it takes to make large scale projects come to life.

quests.title: Portable Stonecutter
quests.subtitle: It's like the Chisel, but fatter
desc: It cuts, it grinds, it chisels, polishes and even cooks and cleans!
All the power of a Stone Cutter, now in a compact portable format in your Sophisticated Backpack or Chest!
Disclaimer: Will not actually cook or clean. Not for Commercial Use.
Warning: Keep away from children, animals, nitwits. Do not place hand on blade while in motion. Extended use may lead to fatigue and loss of vision.

quests.title: Building Gadget
quests.subtitle: It builds stuff
desc: An advanced building device with several modes allowing for the quick construction of walls, stairs, and platforms.
Sneak Right Click on a block to set the block it’ll build with. Use the Building Gadgets Settings Menu key [default: g] to access advanced features.

quests.title: Exchange Gadget
quests.subtitle: It exchanges stuff
desc: Quickly swap blocks in an area without having to break and manually place each one. Enchant with Silk Touch to work with delicate blocks such as glass.
Sneak Right Click on a block to set the block it’ll build with. Use the Building Gadgets Settings Menu key [default: g] to access advanced features.

quests.title: Copy-Paste Gadget
quests.subtitle: It copies and pastes stuff
desc: A powerful tool that allows copying large areas and rebuilding them instantly elsewhere, making short work of repeating large sections of a build, such as a repeating wall pattern, or sprucing up an area with a few different prefab homes.
Sneak Right Click on a block to set the block it’ll build with. Use the Building Gadgets Settings Menu key [default: g] to access advanced features.

quests.title: Destruction Gadget
quests.subtitle: Guess what it does ..
desc: For those times when you simply want to clear a hole to build in, and don’t really care what happens to the blocks that were there.
Be warned, this tool destroys all blocks it removes!
Sneak Right Click in the air to configure the area to void. Use the Building Gadgets Settings Menu key [default: g] to access advanced features.

quests.title: Construction Wands
quests.subtitle: Accio
desc: A modded classic, the Construction Wand simply extends the blocks that are already placed in the world. This can make it easy to build a wall by first laying the foundation, then building up with the wand.
This version comes with a few added features as well, such as the ability to destroy blocks, place in mid air, or even place random blocks from those in your hot bar.
Ctrl Shift the wand in the air to access a menu with advanced options, or Ctrl Scroll Wheel to quickly toggle between building modes.

quests.title: Extendo Grip
quests.subtitle: BOING! BOING!
desc: The Extendo Grip increases your reach distance, thus allowing you to place and break blocks at a larger distance.
To use the Extendo Grip, put it in your Off-Hand, and then use blocks or tools in your Main-Hand as you normally would.
While wearing a Copper Tank, the Extendo Grip loses no Durability and instead uses some of the air pressure you have stored in your tank.

quests.title: Wand of Symmetry
quests.subtitle: Lay your weary OCD to rest
desc: The Wand of Symmetry does not disappoint those who love a little symmetry in their life.
This tool will automatically place blocks in mirrored positions around a center point, making large projects a breeze.
To start, Right Click a block on the ground to select the center point. Once selected, Sneak Right Click to open the configuration GUI to choose the plane type and the mirroring axis.

quests.title: Quark
quests.subtitle: Jack of all Trades
desc: Quark is such a massive mod, and while it could have had it's own section, or even be part of the main Building section, we felt like having it as a stand-alone info quest fits better. While it would be near impossible to write down everything Quark has to offer, the below are some of the highlights for builders to make their life a little easier.
- Decorative Blocks: Quark offers a plethora of blocks, both crafted like the different themed Chests, or gathered from around the world like the Corundum Crystal Blocks.
- Trowel: This tool allows the randomization of block placement. It selects block(s) for your hotbar when used.
For more information on what else Quark has to offer you as a builder, visit their official website.
{"text":"Quark Wiki","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://quarkmod.net/#features"}}

quests.title: Abacus
desc: Need a measuring tape? Well, how about an Abacus instead. This little guy will quickly tally up the number of blocks between point A and point B, perfect for planning large builds. Just Right-Click the ground at the start and walk to the end point.

quests.title: Player Door Sensor
desc: A simple sensor that can be placed over any door. When a player approaches, the door will open automatically. Their vertical detection range may be adjusted with a Redstone Key, allowing them to work on larger doors.

quests.title: Mysterious Shears
desc: Enchanted shears that, when used upon a Rainbow Sheep, will produce Rainbow Wool.

quests.title: Saving Schematics
quests.subtitle: Archetecture 101
desc: Create has a set of tools dedicated to saving schematics of structures and replicating them.
The Schematic and Quill will allow you to save a schematic of an existing structure. This saved schematic will allow you to build the structure somewhere else.
1) Right-Click to select the two opposite corners of the structure you want to save.
2) Point at a face of the selected area and ctrl-scroll to adjust that side.
3) Right-click to name and save the schematic.
The Create GitHub has a wiki page with examples of saving schematics:
{"text":"Saving a Schematic","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://github.com/Creators-of-Create/Create/wiki/Saving-a-Schematic"}}

quests.title: Placing Schematics
quests.subtitle: Filing for Building Permits
desc: In order to place your saved structures, you need to create a Schematic - this is done on the Schematic Table.

Choose the schematic you want to create by mousing over the box in the middle of the GUI and scrolling. Place an Empty Schematic into the left slot on the table. Click the checkmark to print the schematic - this uploads it to the server and can take a while for very large schematics. You can close the table while this process completes and come back later. Pressing the “Open Folder” button will open the Schematic folder in your instance, and pressing “Refresh” will update the list of available schematics.

Schematic in hand, you can place it in-world by right clicking. An on-screen HUD provides options for adjusting the schematic - moving, rotating, or flipping. Shift-right clicking the schematic will also allow you edit placement and rotation/mirroring. You can use this as a building guide, but there are better uses for it...
Note: Schematics for common multiblocks are included by default. You can use the "Open Folder" button to relocate any schematics you aren’t using and then refresh the list.
The Create GitHub has a wiki with examples of loading schematics:
{"text":"Loading a Schematic","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://github.com/Creators-of-Create/Create/wiki/Loading-a-Schematic"}}

quests.title: Printing Schematics
quests.subtitle: Constructive Detonation
desc: The Schematicannon is how you're going to build your structures. It uses gunpowder as a propellent, and will take blocks from adjacent inventories.

Take your freshly placed schematic and load it into the Schematicannon. Load gunpowder in the top left - the cannon will use one for each 400 blocks. Hit the Play button in the middle of the interface to begin placing blocks!

By default the cannon will pause if it doesn't have the block required, and it will replace any blocks in the way, but will protect tile entities (think chests and similar). Replaced blocks don't drop and are lost - the cannon IS NOT a quarry tool! These settings can be controlled by clicking the button in the bottom left.
Note: The cannon isn't very fast, but it's possible to split the workload between multiple cannons, and Time in a Bottle works wonders on it!
The Create GitHub has a wiki with examples of printing schematics:
{"text":"Printing a Schematic","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://github.com/Creators-of-Create/Create/wiki/Printing-a-Schematic"}}

quests.title: Basic Metallurgy
desc: The Wilden Grove practiced a particular form of druidic magic that would slowly draw materials from deep in the earth up into mounds where they could be easily extracted with minimal harm to the land.
Undoubtedly many of these mounds remain. Seek them out, though beware that in the absence of the Grove, others may have claimed these places for themselves.
Metal processing has been heavily customized with many metals having unique methods of acquisition. Be certain to examine EMI carefully!

quests.title: Naga Trophy
quests.subtitle: Fear is the Mind-Killer
desc: Strange. At one time, this fen was kept by the Wilden Grove, a circle of druids sworn to preserve and watch over the surrounding wildlands. Yet no sign remains and creatures such as this Naga now terrorize the lands.
With its defeat, the Fae that call this place home will undoubtedly show their gratitude.
Locate and kill the Naga.

It should be located somewhere nearby in a large stone courtyard. Though quick, Naga are not known for their intelligence and in their blind rage they are easily dodged. Keep some distance and aim for the head.
Once the deed is done, a chest will appear in the center of the arena. Be sure to grab the contents.
Note that the Twilight Forest progression system is disabled for Enigmatica 9: Expert. From this point forward, areas may be explored in any order.

quests.title: Mixing Cauldron
desc: By distilling down various natural ingredients, their energies may be tapped more easily.

Potions of all types may be brewed from surprisingly common ingredients. Be sure to check out what can be brewed, as potions will prove indispensable when facing off against the less friendly creatures that now roam the lands.
Use the Mixing Cauldron to brew up some Potions of Ancient Knowledge, or any other potions you find interesting. Once brewed, they may be bottled by Right-Clicking the Cauldron with glass bottles.

Note that Hexerei potion fluids do not show in JEI. The simplest way to find the recipes is to look at the Vanilla potion, then check the uses on the ingredients. All potion ingredients are the same between the two systems.

quests.title: Brilliant Fiber
desc: These lands have flourished for millennia under the stewardship of the Grove and despite their absence, great power remains concentrated here.

The key to harvesting those energies starts in the trees. Craft some Brilliant Fiber in a Mortar and weave it among the leaves of any tree. As it takes hold, the leaves will be transformed, allowing Gold Leaf to be harvested.

quests.title: Ritual of the Forest
desc: Sneak Right-Click the Gold Leaves on any Log to transform it into the Wooden Stands required for the Ritual of the Forest.
Refer to the Book of Natural Aura for a visual representation of this structure and an explanation on its use.

quests.title: Druidic Roots
desc: With the seeds, herbs, and saplings found among the Naga’s remains, its time to take root, so to speak, and lay out a garden.

It seems the Tree of Life and the Archwood groves maintained by the Wilden Grove have all faded from this land since their departure. Restoring them will be critical as they form the basis for all the magic concentrated here.
Use the Ritual of the Forest to obtain each of the Archwood saplings and begin growing them along with the other seeds and plants that have been obtained.
The fruits in the pouch may be grown upon the trunks of the Archwood trees in much the same way as Cocoa Beans. Each fruit grows only on its specific type of Archwood tree.
The Ancient Sapling and Elder Sapling may also be obtained through this ritual, with both offering unique benefits.

The wood of the Ancient tree concentrates magical energies into it, making it useful for certain devices. Meanwhile, the Resplendent Elder tree's fruit seems to carry the memories of those who've come before.

item.name: Blazing Archwood Sapling / Flashing Archwood Sapling / Flourishing Archwood Sapling / Vexing Archwood Sapling …

quests.title: Imbuement Chamber
desc: Though slow at first, the Imbuement Chamber will be of great assistance in restoring the Tree of Life. Not only for condensing Source Gems, which have many uses of their own, but in obtaining the Elemental Essences as well; mastering these essences will allow the tree to be regrown.
The focus items placed on pedestals nearby are never consumed and act merely as a key to determine the result.
Source from a Jar is optional. The Imbuement Chamber will run perfectly fine without it, though it will be slower.

quests.title: Straight from the Source
desc: An Alchemical Sourcelink will allow converting potions into more contained and portable magical energy, Source, which can be transmitted and manipulated quite easily, making it ideal for many focused magical pursuits.
Place a Potion Jar directly adjacent to a Sourcelink and it’ll perform the conversion, placing Source into any nearby Source Jars.
Be sure to send some to a Source Jar near that Imbuement Chamber to get it operating faster too!
See the following page for methods on inserting potions into Potion Jars.
{@pagebreak}
&nFilling Potion Jars&r
Potions may be inserted into Potion Jars through the following methods:
● Wixies: Potions brewed by Wixies are automatically
inserted into nearby Potion Jars.
● Starbuncles: When equipped with a Wixie Hat, Starbuncles
may be used to transport potions from one jar to
another.
● Fluid Containment Jars: Any liquid potion piped into these
Jars will be automatically inserted into a Potion Jar
placed atop it. This can be used to convert potions from
Create, Immersive Engineering, Hexerei, and Thermal into
Potion Jar Potions for use in Alchemical Sourcelinks.
● Item Drain: Create Item Drains will drain Potion Bottles,
converting them to fluid form. This may be combined with
Fluid Containment Jars.
● Manually: Potion Bottles may be Right-Clicked onto a
Potion Jar to insert them.

quests.title: Ironwood
desc: Processing Iron is incredibly difficult and will take far more advanced arcane machinery to properly extract pure Iron from ore. By fusing it into a living amalgam known as Ironwood, however, it can be used in a variety of magical applications.

quests.title: Gold Leaf
desc: Obtain a Gold Leaf and Sneak + Right-Click a block of Ironwood to convert it to a Natural Altar.
Be sure to build the rest of the required structure as well. Any type of wood plank may be used.

quests.title: Compressed Stone
desc: By balancing the outward force of Aura with the inward crushing of this spell, we’re able to reach a stable equilibrium that is strong and durable enough to assist in advanced metallurgy: Compressed Stone.
The following spell form will crush blocks placed in the world:
&5Touch&r > &aCrush&r
Note: Sensitive is &nnot&r required for crushing blocks.

quests.title: Arcane Compressor
desc: A Blitz is bound into this device by way of Gythia’s Perpetual Geas and uses the supplied magical energies to generate enormous volumes of air.
Be mindful of the heat the device produces, however, as the Blitz must remain cool to function efficiently.

quests.title: Pressure Chamber Interface
desc: The Pressure Chamber is a crucial arcane construct, used in many applications, from extracting Aluminum from Kaolin Clay, to crafting potent ensorcelled projectiles, and many more in between.
Take special note of the Module Expansion Crystals used in this craft. These may be inserted onto most Tube Modules to enhance their abilities.
Using one on a Pressure Gauge Tube Module, for instance, will greatly simplify controlling a Compressor.
Meanwhile, using one on a Regulator Tube Module allows fine tuning when it comes to the amount of pressure allowed through a tube system.

quests.title: Dim Pulsating Crystal
desc: Enigmatic Unity’s Pulsating Crystals serve as the basis for generating most FE, though a few other methods are available.

They require a Source Jar nearby from which they’ll periodically draw a quantity of Source, converting it into FE. If there is any Aura present when this happens, a portion of Aura will also be consumed, generating far more FE in the process.

quests.title: Applied Energistics
desc: With Certus Quartz purified and growing, the real work may begin. When charged by a Pulsating Crystal, an arcane field is induced within their lattice that may be exploited to transport matter and energy great distances both instantly and in a very controlled and directed manner.
Construct an Ad Hoc ME network consisting of an Energy Acceptor, an ME Crafting Terminal, and one or more ME Storage Buses connected by ME Glass Cable.
Consider combining these with Functional Storage or Sophisticated Storage controllers to make the most out of the limited number of channels.

quests.title: Learning to Fly
desc: What is a witch without her broom?
Crafting a broom to get around might help in avoiding some more… deadly obstacles.

Obtain the necessary Blood by crafting a Blood Sigil and installing it in a Mixing Cauldron. Jump up and down inside to fill the Cauldron with your own blood and bottle it by Right-Clicking with a Glass Bottle.
Consider crafting a Magebloom Broom Brush. For a strong enough magic user, these will never break, restoring themselves from the owner’s mana.

item.name: Willow Broom / Archwood Broom / Witch Hazel Broom

quests.title: Superior Shields
desc: A wise witch will use every tool at her disposal, and Superior Shields offer a potent source of protection when exploring these lands.

item.name: Bronze Shield / Electrum Shield / Constantan Shield / Ironwood Shield …

quests.title: Blaze Burner
desc: A Blaze will need to be summoned and bound into appropriate materials to create this device. Luckily, with control of the elements, summoning forth a single Blaze should prove to be a trivial task.
Each type of elemental may be summoned using Gythia’s Perpetual Geas. These elementals will be summoned with their AI and loot disabled.

quests.title: Aluminum
desc: The strange process of making Aluminum will begin with Clay converted to Kaolin Clay.
Discover the rest of the process through JEI.

quests.title: Novice Spell Book
desc: Perhaps paying a visit to the local mage tower will turn up more information, or at least more useful tools, to assist in restoring the Tree of Life?

quests.title: Scribe's Table
desc: With a steady supply of Antique Ink secured, glyphs may finally be crafted. Of course, using higher tier glyphs will still require further repair of the Spell Book.

quests.title: Air Essence
desc: Often the first elemental essence mastered by druids of the Grove, Air requires the gift of a feather from their closest allies, the Ravens, as well as a test of the druid’s combat prowess.
Obtaining Blitz Motes:
Seek out Spawners in the world and break them. They have a chance of causing a rupture in space, allowing creatures of all types to flow through, including Blitz and other elementals.
Defeat them to obtain Blitz Motes and close the rift if you can.

quests.title: Water Essence
desc: Surviving the cold and retrieving fur from an Alpha Yeti was considered quite the feat of fortitude. Enter the Yeti Lair in the Snowy Forest and face down these fierce creatures to obtain the fur.
Obtaining Blizz Cubes:
Seek out Spawners in the world and break them. They have a chance of causing a rupture in space, allowing creatures of all types to flow through, including Blizz and other elementals.
Defeat them to obtain Blizz Cubes and close the rift if you can.

quests.title: Earth Essence
desc: A test of cunning for young druids, obtaining Magic Beans involves sneaking into a Troll den and absconding with their sacred beans.

Locating their dens is often the trickiest part, as they live deep underground in the Highlands. It is said the soil above their dens, however, is particularly fertile. Perhaps seeking out this marker will help in locating them.
Obtaining Basalz Shards:
Seek out Spawners in the world and break them. They have a chance of causing a rupture in space, allowing creatures of all types to flow through, including Basalz and other elementals.
Defeat them to obtain Basalz Shards and close the rift if you can.

quests.title: Anima Essence
desc: Druids of the Grove commonly carried tokens with them, Charms of Life, to help prevent their untimely demise facing down some of the dangerous creatures they dealt with. Though death is part of the natural cycle, they held no issue with prolonging life through medicines and other such charms.

Undeath, on the other hand, was abhorrent to them and it is particularly cruel that their honored dead appear to have been re-animated and set to foul purpose. Seek out the mage’s tower and see if any answers can be found there.

quests.title: Summon Death Tome
desc: Luckily, despite the decrepit state of the spell book, the Crush glyphs appear whole and in a usable state. Many others are going to need repair, but this will serve for now.

Some speculate that the Death Tome enchantment was developed to protect the knowledge stored within ancient spell tomes, but it may just as well have been done to vex the librarians who housed them. Either way, it is still possible to extract useful glyphs from them, despite their dangerous nature.
Perform this ritual to summon a murder of Death Tomes. They’ll be an excellent way to supplement the missing glyphs in this newfound spell book.

quests.title: Fire Essence
desc: The Wilden Grove had once befriended and tamed the Hydras that call the Fire Swamp their home. How they did this remains a mystery… It seems there’s only one way of obtaining the blood of one now. Don’t approach too closely or you’ll surely become its next meal.
Obtaining Blaze Rods:
Seek out Spawners in the world and break them. They have a chance of causing a rupture in space, allowing creatures of all types to flow through, including Blaze and other elementals.
Defeat them to obtain Blaze Rods and close the rift if you can.

quests.title: Subzero Crystal Shard
quests.subtitle: River of Memory
desc: With the elements mastered, only one task remains before the Tree of Life may be restored: Winter’s Reign must end.
Travel to the frigid glaciers and defeat the Snow Queen to obtain Subzero Crystals.
Through the natural transmutation magics imbued in a Botanist’s Pickaxe, it should be possible to purify the Subzero Crystal and induce it to grow.

quests.title: Fiery Ingot
desc: Native to the elemental plane of fire, Fiery Metal is particularly suited for containing Fire Elementals.
Though not found naturally in this plane, it can be created through the careful application of Fire Essence and other materials.

quests.title: Conjuration Essence
desc: Conjuration is a skill mastered early by the druids of the Wilden Grove and requires only basic alchemical knowledge to make and grow Magebloom Seeds.

quests.title: Familiar Friends
desc: A lonely witch is a busy witch.
With all the potions, crafting, gathering, and other running around there is to do in a day, a few helping hands would certainly be appreciated, no?
Thankfully with the Naga out of the way, there's no shortage of Fae willing to help in any way they can.
Draw the pentacle known as Aching’s Amicable Accord which is detailed in the Dictionary of Spirits.
A selection of Occultism, Hexerei, and Ars Nouveau critters may be summoned; research uses for Mindful Trance Blend to see what is available.

quests.title: Mechanical Press
desc: More finely crafted devices will need more delicately processed materials than can easily be done by hand.
These tough mechanical devices are up to the task.
● Millstone - Capable of grinding
materials much more finely than can
be achieved by hand, the Millstone will
occasionally produce secondary
materials that may be quite useful,
such as Lead and Quartz.
● Rolling Mill - Working from Ingots, the
Rolling Mill can create the fine Rods
and Wires required by many
advanced devices.
● Mechanical Press - A device strong
enough to flatten Ingots into Plates
in only a few strokes. Well worth the
effort of setting it up.

quests.title: Arcane Furnace
desc: An upgrade to the basic furnace used up till now. This simple apparatus merely channels the energies into an Extraneous Firestarter to produce heat. Crude, but effective.

quests.title: Pestle and Mortar
desc: Forging metals requires specialized tools and processes, none of which are readily available.
With a bit of effort, simpler materials may be harvested from ore, however. Craft a Pestle and Mortar to begin grinding them and a Blast Furnace to smelt it down into a useful form.
The Pestle and Mortar is easily automated with just a hopper, no manual effort is required.
To begin, simple metals such as Copper may be worked into an ingot by crushing, blasting, crushing, and blasting one final time. Better methods will become available later.

quests.title: Alloying
desc: Alloying requires finely ground metals mixed with some form of flux to help with bonding and removal of impurities before heating it all to produce a quality ingot. For now, a Pestle and Mortar will serve well enough.

quests.title: Keeping Organized with Bookwyrms
desc: Keeping things organized is a chore nobody has time for. Nobody except Bookwyrms, that is.
With just a few of these and smart use of large storage containers, however, Bookwyrms can give you easy access to all your items in one convenient place.
Refer to the Ars Nouveau quests and Worn Notebook for in-depth information on how this works.

quests.title: Autocrafting with Wixies
desc: When it comes to brewing potions, Wixies are among the best. Be sure to summon a few to help keep the Source flowing.

To let the Wixie know what potions to brew, place some brewed potions on Arcane Pedestals or Platforms adjacent to her Cauldron. These can be obtained by brewing in the Mixing Cauldron and Right-Clicking it with Glass Bottles.

The entire chain must be present for her to do her job. So, to brew a Potion of Ancient Knowledge, she’ll need a pedestal with an Awkward Potion and another with a Potion of Ancient Knowledge. She’ll need a Potion Jar for each step as well. Multiple Wixies may work together, with each fulfilling the next step in the chain.
More information can be found in the Worn Notebook.

quests.title: Starbuncle Logistics
desc: Multi-talented and friendly, Starbuncles may be tasked with moving around items, fluids, gases, energy, and even potions.

They’re smart enough to automate a lot of early tasks, such as bringing herbs to a Drying Rack to dry, returning the dried herbs to storage, stocking a furnace, moving potions from place to place, and much more.
They’ll need some equipment to do each of these tasks, so be sure to outfit them appropriately.  Search for Starbuncle Equipment in JEI to find everything they can use.

quests.title: Combat Assistance - Familiars
desc: Though not exhaustive, the list below highlights some of the benefits to be had by befriending these Familiars. More than one may be called forth at a time.
For full details on these and other Familiars, refer to the Dictionary of Spirits under Familiar Rituals.
Combat
● Mummy – Fights for you.
● Beholder – Shoots magical lasers out of its eyes.
Utility
● Guardian – A walking Totem of Undying.
● Greedy – Collects items like a magnet.
● Beaver – Helps break wood faster.
Buffs
● Drikwing – Grants multi jump, jump boost, and slow fall.
● Dragon – Increases XP gains.
● Bat – Grants Night Vision.
● Cthulhu – Grants Water Breathing.
● Deer – Grants Jump Boost.
● Devil – Grants Fire Resistance.
Other
● Blacksmith – Repairs equipment and applies upgrades to
other familiars, enhancing them in a multitude of ways.
Note: Familiars are protected from friendly fire, and as such it is generally safe to fight near them. In additions, some of the combat oriented ones have been buffed to help them survive.

quests.title: Budding Crystal Harvesting
desc: Diligent creatures once employed by the Wilden Grove, Amethyst Golems were likely the key to their high-quality Amethyst production.
Despite their name, they’ll gladly work with other budding crystals besides Amethyst.

quests.title: Crow Assisted Crop Harvesting
desc: Though the Wilden Grove were noted for the Ravens in their employ, there were more than a few who preferred to befriend the smaller, though equally intelligent, Crow.

Perform this ritual to summon a tamed Crow. These helpful critters can be equipped with a weapon and hat and will defend their friends to the death. They're also exceptional helpers around crops, being able to harvest, replant, and gather many useful plants.
Discover more about Crows in the Hexerei quest chapter.

quests.title: Manipulation Essence
desc: One of the simpler Essences to master, Manipulation is associated with transmutation and long-range interactions.
Everything required to make it should be easily dug from the ground.

quests.title: Source Gem
desc: The Wilden Grove was well known for the high-quality Amethyst they’d extract from the earth which they used to produce Source Gems.
Undoubtedly, some can be found in the ruins of their homes or within the ore hills they’ve left behind.

quests.title: Tree of Life
desc: Restoring the Tree of Life to its full glory will be no easy task. Use the knowledge obtained thus far to grow the Primordial Seed. With time and sacrifice, it will grow stronger.
Choose a ritual site with plenty of room to give the tree the space it needs to take root. Performing this ritual will grow the tree immediately, centered upon the ritual pentacle.
Note: The Tree of Life will be facing North with a small entrance going down into the pentacle chamber. This rotation cannot be changed.
This structure is 23x23 and extends both into the ground and sky. It will overwrite blocks near it when it grows. You've been warned.

quests.title: Aura Generation
desc: Much like the Alchemical Sourcelink can distill the magical essences in Potions down into Source, the Lingering Absorber is a structure that helps re-direct those energies back into the environment as Aura.
This is a large multiblock structure, so be sure to check the Book of Natural Aura for a preview to assist in building it.

Using this structure to generate Aura will require making Lingering potions and throwing them on the golden cross on the Absorber. Throwing higher quality potions, with greater strength and duration, will result in more Aura.

It is important to note that Wixies, as crafty as they are, are incapable of making Lingering or Splash potions. They’re easily automated with Create’s brewing system, however, as well as with Industrial Foregoing's Potion Brewer later on.

quests.title: Emergency Aura
desc: Having trouble with Aura? Need a quick boost?
Perform this ritual to convert Twilight Forest boss trophies into a large infusion of Aura.

quests.title: Ritual Brazier
desc: Ritual magic is yet another facet of the mystical arts and takes many forms, from chalking arcane circles on the ground to burning specially prepared spell tablets.
The Ritual Brazier opens many options for automation and defense. Explore what each tablet can do and see what uses they can be put to.

quests.title: Certus Farming
desc: There’s far more to magic than just the showy bits of wiggling one’s fingers and making sparkly lights. Indeed, a great deal can be done through the arcane arts with the right materials and processes.

Long ago, specialists in transmutation and conjuration discovered ways of creating vast networks of crystalline conduits capable of wondrous feats. They kept hordes of materials stored away in dimensional arrays and could use them to create nearly anything on a whim.
That all seems rather far out of reach for now, but simple transport seems viable at least.
Begin by locating some Certus Quartz; the Wilden Grove will undoubtedly have left some behind in their ore mounds.
Through the natural transmutation magics imbued in a Botanist’s Pickaxe, it should be possible to purify the Certus Quartz and induce it to grow.

quests.title: Altar of Birthing
desc: Honey’s healing properties are well known to Witches and have been used for centuries to treat countless ailments. With an extra little touch of magic, it can even be transmuted into a powerful substance known as Breath of Twilight.
Sadly, the bees all appear to have abandoned this area. Perhaps they can be enticed back now that someone is around to tend to them?
Search the ruined homes in the forest for any remaining honeycomb and use it to craft a suitable home for some bees.
The bees themselves may be summoned with the Altar of Birthing, just bring some tasty flowers for them!

quests.title: Glyph Dispel
desc: Though crafting the most powerful spells may not be immediately viable, tier one glyphs can still be plenty powerful.
Of note is the Dispel glyph, which can quickly remove the powerful potion effects that appear on many stronger mobs.
Be sure to spend some time experimenting with the Spell Book, as it is easily one of the most powerful weapons in the hands of an experienced witch.

quests.title: Potions
desc: Magic is to be found everywhere for someone with sharp eyes and an open heart. Witches have been brewing since time immemorable, using the latent powers of the land to aid them in their pursuits.
Having access to the right potion at the right time can make all the difference in surviving.
A variety of custom potion recipes have been added, making them accessible quite early on. Indeed, brewing will prove quite crucial to everything moving forward.

Strength can help enormously when facing toughened monsters, while Swiftness and Invisibility can help avoid them entirely. In addition, Ars Nouveau allows mixing potions and storing them in Flasks for a single quick dose to apply multiple effects.

quests.title: Survival Essentials
desc: A brave witch is a dead witch, or so the saying goes. Surviving this world filled with deadly monsters requires more than brute strength; a cunning mind and swift feet are far more important.
A clever witch knows when to run away.
Of course, sometimes a fight is unavoidable. The world isn’t fair, after all. So, when it seems that everything is out for blood, remember that goes both ways: Fight dirty.

quests.title: Potion Charms
desc: Similar to the Alchemist’s Crown, Potion Charms serve to keep an effect applied much longer than normal. A Potion Charm crafted from three-minute potions, for example, will last 8 seconds per point of durability.
Even without being enchanted, these will last considerably longer than the potions used to craft them.

quests.title: Tipped Arrows
desc: Skeletons frequently make use of tipped arrows, which are a recipe for a bad day if one is caught unaware.

Tipped arrows may be easily crafted by Right-Clicking an arrow on a Potion Jar, no lingering potions required! Blasting arrows make for a particularly nasty weapon that’s useful against both the living and the dead.

quests.title: Alchemist's Crown
desc: Potions certainly do not last long, and drinking more manually isn’t always easily done. Be sure to check out the Alchemist’s Crown for an easy way to keep potions active for longer.
Of special interest is that the Crown will draw from Potion Flasks, meaning mixed potions can be kept active easily.

quests.title: Glyph Crush
desc: Ordinarily Crush may only be used on blocks placed in the world. For example, when creating Compressed Stone.
However, by augmenting it with Sensitive, it can target items dropped on the ground as well allowing it to function on Raw Ore as well.
The following spell form will crush items on the ground:
&5Projectile&r > &aCrush&r > &6Sensitive&r

quests.title: Diamond Divination Rod
desc: The practice of divination dates back centuries and all manner of material has been used for a focus, from tea leaves to entrails.
While certainly effective, those methods were preferred by some merely for the spectacle; anything can be used to tune one’s mind for the task.

quests.title: Questing Ram
desc: One of the few remaining guardians of these lands, the Questing Ram makes its home in the Enchanted Forest.
Seek them out and complete their task. It is doubtful they’ll know precisely what happened, but they may have knowledge vital to the restoration of the Tree of Life.
Obtain Wool of each color and provide it to the Ram.
Through the natural transmutation magics imbued in a Botanist’s Pickaxe, it should be possible to purify the Therium and induce it to grow.

quests.title: Primordial Seed
desc: The Questing Ram has agreed to assist in renewing the Tree of Life by providing the necessary knowledge for recreating the Primordial Seed. However, they’ll need some help to do so.
Summon forth the elemental spirits of this land to imbue their energy into the Seed.

quests.title: Lingering Absorber Automation
desc: With heightened spell casting ability comes the ability to improve some automation through Spell Turrets.
As a practical example, the following spell form will allow a Spell Turret to pull a standard potion from an adjacent Potion Jar, convert it to Lingering and throw it where the projectile lands.
&5Projectile&r > &aInfuse&r > &6Extend Time&r
These lingering potions will work exactly as their crafted variety for the purpose of running a Lingering Absorber without the need to craft beyond the base potion.

quests.title: Flight
desc: An empowered ritual that grants an hour of flight to up to five entities. Useful for exploration far from home. Be sure to bring the materials to re-cast it if necessary.

quests.title: Dim Arcanite Crystal
desc: The Cult of the Ur-Ghast, foolish as they were, were not far off in their research. Carminite has excellent arcane resonance, but the Redstone they coupled it with was too strong of a moderator. The resulting superradiant instability quickly became too much for their contraption to manage.
Fusing it with Source Gems, on the other hand, appears to properly channel the arcane fields. These first attempts appear imperfect, however.
The process needs refining.
To perform Lightning Channeling recipes, a source of lightning is required. For our purposes, Lightning Charges are simple enough to obtain.
Toss down the ingredients shown in EMI and then use the Lightning Charge on them. Be sure to pick up the results quickly before they burn!

quests.title: Market
desc: Build it and they’ll come, or so it was said. These tiny market stalls were once a common sight in places of business, trade, and agriculture and served as a way of making offerings to fae creatures that roam the lands.
With so few offerings happening these days, setting one out will surely attract some helpful company.
The Market is in many cases the only source for seeds and saplings, and is therefore invaluable. Crafting one is highly recommended for obtaining missing plants one might need.

quests.title: Energy Transfer
desc: Routers are capable of some truly impressive tasks and are indispensable to a fledgling witch. However, their ability to transfer power is often overlooked.
A single router, for example, could receive power from Pulsating Crystals on all six sides, while wirelessly transmitting to up to 72 devices within a 48-block radius.
One can easily serve as a central power distribution for a moderate crafting area, keeping everything supplied with the magical energies they need to keep on ticking.

quests.title: Plastic
desc: Through some alchemical manipulation and transmutational trickery, simple plants may be transformed into this impressive material.
Mastering its creation early on will prove advantageous.
Follow the recipes back from Liquid Plastic, keeping an eye on the PneumaticCraft machines, such as the Fluid Mixer and Thermopneumatic Processing Plant.
The process requires multiple steps but can easily be performed with a little witchy ingenuity.

quests.title: Nomadic Life
desc: Life on the road has its ups and downs but a nice warm tent to call home can smooth over many of the rougher parts of such a life-style.
Nomadic Tents offer a portable home that can make a wonderful base of operations early on. Not only may the be moved with ease, but they may also be upgraded while retaining their contents.
Consider setting up a bed, basic storage, and some essential crafting stations inside!
● Right-Click and Hold the tent on the
ground to place the frame.
● Right-Click each frame with a mallet
to form that section.
A Golden Mallet will form the entire
tent at once!
● Right-Click or walk into the door to
enter and exit.
● Right-Click the door from the outside
with a mallet to pack up the tent as
an item.

quests.title: Antique Ink
desc: Though many glyphs may be found and used to repair the spell book, they may also be crafted with appropriate materials.
Finding proper spell ink, however, may prove rather difficult as it must be specially prepared using a process that can take years.
It was once heavily traded by the seafaring folk that specialized in its creation. Perhaps some could be retrieved with some good old-fashioned trawling.
