quests.title: Mote of Pandemonium
desc: After some experimentation with the Echo Shards, it appears they may be further refined into a substance known as Pandemonium; the purest form of chaos with powerful creational capabilities.

quests.title: Sculk
desc: Though found in the wild, creating a local farm for Sculk is recommended. Whenever a mob dies near a Sculk Catalyst, it will cause nearby Stone to be converted into Sculk.
Silk-Touch is required to harvest the resulting Sculk.
Devise a way to automate harvesting this material.

quests.title: Echo Shard
desc: Refined from Sculk, this mineral is associated with primal chaos.
Normally exceptionally rare, the ancients of this land appear to have been harvesting it for unknown purposes.

quests.title: Supercritical Phase Shifter
desc: Thought lost to time by many magical practitioners, the creation of Aetherium has remained a closely guarded secret by Witches due to it’s raw potential. It seems likely that its use was what eventually led this civilization to its downfall, but it’s hard to be certain.
It seems that it needs to be created once more, however, to fully restore the Tree of Life.

quests.title: Aetheric Transmutation Chamber
desc: With Aetherium secured, a special chamber must be crafted to contain the reaction; letting this loose could devastate the land for millennia to come…

quests.title: Aetheric Brass Ingot
desc: This metal hums with potential and seems uniquely attuned to the shadow people known as Endermen.
Undoubtedly, it will help anchor a teleportation ritual to wherever they call home.

quests.title: Visit The End
desc: Travel to the home of the Endermen is risky in and of itself, and tales tell of many a practitioner who attempted the journey never to return.
By all accounts, bringing some means of flying will be critical to successfully navigating this land.
Teleportation using the Tree of Life is prone to… drift. Be sure to bring along some means to return home as well as to set up a portal on the other side.

quests.title: Tree of Life
desc: Death follows life, and life thrives on death. Such is the circle of all things.
The Tree of Life is not exempt from this cycle either; an infusion of souls would likely do it wonders at this stage.
Nourish the Tree once more and prepare to travel to the home of the Endermen in search of the final reagents required to fully restore it.

quests.title: Ender Dragon
desc: True dragons passed from our world ages ago. Finding one here in this realm is quite a surprise, though certainly welcome. The magic and knowledge it bears will be vital in the final restoration of the Tree.
It does seem a shame to cage such a majestic creature…
Shame or not, it must be done. No sentient creature of this power would allow itself to be contained through lesser means.
By enchanting the dragon into a lens, we’ll be able to safely extract what we need to fully restore the Tree of Life.

quests.title: Tree of Life: Stage 4
desc: With the final Shard obtained, the Tree of Life will finally be restored to its full glory.
May its roots delve deep as its branches reach for the sun.

quests.title: Heart of the Sea
desc: Reach deep to the vivifying waters...

quests.title: Heart of the Mountain
desc: Rock to dust, dust to loam...

quests.title: Heart of the Inferno
desc: Grow tall, stretch to the sun's kiss...

quests.title: Heart of the Tempest
desc: Lean into the wind's gentle embrace...

quests.title: Advanced Machine Frame
desc: With greater knowledge of spatial dimensions, the Afrit is capable of carving out an even greater internal volume for use by the spirits running this apparatus, allowing them to perform more complex tasks.

quests.title: Final Rites
desc: Though its roots dig deep, and its branches scrape the sky, the Tree of Life remains in a tenuous state. It must be bolstered by the elements to ensure it never fades again.

quests.title: Ancient Debris
desc: It would seem the Cult of the Ur-Ghast were up to something far more sinister than previously thought. The rift they opened with their Carminite Reactor also gave them the opportunity to obtain this strange debris.

quests.title: Netherite
desc: With some research, it appears the Cult of the Ur-Ghast were preparing to summon a great evil into the land. To what purpose is still unclear.
Just the same, this debris will need to be purified before being put to use.

quests.title: Celestial Gold
desc: Celestial Gold, blessed by the gods themselves, would ring out across the dimensions like a clear bell on a calm day. The perfect bait for summoning a great corruption into the land.

quests.title: Gate Pearl
desc: Only a well-prepared witch should ever consider summoning the Wither Council, using every trick at her disposal to defeat them in a timely manner.
Perhaps one should be captured for further study, however…
The Gateway for this fight is on a short timer.
Capture a Wither and defeat the rest. The captured Wither will be used to mine Blighted Ichor, which may be used to produce Nether Stars.
Feel free to repeat this fight, but it is not intended to be needed more than once.

quests.title: Visit the Nether
desc: With items attuned to the destination it is now possible to travel to the Nether.
Teleportation using the Tree of Life is prone to… drift. Be sure to bring along some means to return home as well as to set up a portal on the other side.

quests.title: Laser Bases
desc: It is time once more to enlist the aid of the elemental spirits, this time to bring forth materials from the depths of their environments. By focusing tight beams of focused Source through these bases, the elementals will be able to retrieve what is needed.
From the Earth, Soul Powder.
From the Sea, Abyssal Seawater.

quests.title: Soul Steel Ingot
desc: A magically enhanced alloy with an affinity for souls.
Curiously, when combined with the scraps of material found in the Ur-Ghast tower, it appears to be capable of generating a powerful anti-magic field.

quests.title: Saturated Magebloom Filter
desc: Abyssal Seawater, water from the deepest parts of the ocean, rich in rare minerals found nowhere else. It will need to be filtered and refined in order to obtain everything it has to offer. Begin by filtering it through a Magebloom Filter.

The resulting Brine may then be cooked down to obtain Lithium and Iesnium, while the saturated filters may be processed to obtain Abyssaline, a potent form of Source useful in operating tools such as the Artificer’s Mining Drill and Buzzsaw.

quests.title: Soul Powder
desc: A fine mineral said to be steeped with the souls of those interred in the earth.
Though common in the Nether, Soul Powder is also abundant in some spooky places in the Twilight Forest such as the Dark Forest surrounding the Ur-Ghast Tower.

quests.title: Large Pillar
desc: Congratulations on completing Enigmatica 9: Expert!

quests.title: Ritual of Cleansing
desc: Fire and Water both possess the cleansing power to remove the taint from Netherite, restoring it to its former glory. Choose one and develop an enchanting setup capable of performing the ritual.

item.name: Heart-Forged Seashelf / Crystalline Seashelf / Glowing Hellshelf / Blazing Hellshelf

quests.title: Ritual of Growth
desc: Long ago, the peoples of this realm attempted to call forth a great power to aid them in their time of need. This creature, known as the Warden, protected them for centuries before their civilization collapsed and their cities fell to ruin.
It is said the Warden still wanders those ancient broken halls. Locate it and lay it to rest.
Travel to a Deep Dark biome far underground in the Overworld and make enough noise to force the Warden out of hiding.
Locating an Ancient City will be challenging without assistance, however. Perhaps seek the Queen Bee's aid to craft a special Honey Compass attuned to the Ancient City.
Slay the Warden to obtain a Warden Tendril. This may be transformed into Genius Loci; a powerful catalyst used in the creation of Elysium.

quests.title: Enderium Ingot
desc: The ancient wisdom of the Ender Dragon, artfully distilled into a powerful material known as Enderium.

quests.title: Gloaming Catalyst
desc: While the sun sets on the Wilden Grove, so too does the moon rise for your coven.
Embrace the night.

quests.title: Enchanting Apparatus
desc: Capable of imparting a number of enchantments on items, this Enchanting Apparatus will no doubt be of enormous value in the endeavors to come.

quests.title: Gate Pearl
desc: As the Queen tells it, The Wilden Grove invoked a dangerous ritual to attempt to stop the Cult of the Ur-Ghast before it was too late.
Sadly, the ritual was too much, and they lost themselves to the Call of the Beast.
Send a message on the Queen’s behalf. Tell them &7“Your friendship is mourned. Rest now.”&r, then put them down.
The Gateway for this fight is on a short timer.
Capture a Wilden Chimera and defeat the rest to obtain a Wilden Tribute. The captured Wilden Chimera will be used to mine Magicite, which has multiple uses.
Feel free to repeat this fight, but it is not intended to be needed more than once.

quests.title: Mark of Mastery
desc: The Wilden Tribute, found in the aftermath of the fight with the Wilden Grove, is a mark held by those who have reached the pinnacle of magical ability.

quests.title: Crushing Wheel
desc: Extracting useful quantities of elemental iron from ore is no simple task and will require some specialized apparatus to work through the process.

To begin, a specially enchanted Crushing Wheel will be required to break the ore into smaller pieces. The resulting crushed ore will then need to be treated in an acid bath at high heat to begin removing impurities.

quests.title: Resonating Crystal Ball
desc: Focused bursts of controlled magical energies are necessary for transmuting certain materials. As it happens, a specially prepared crystal ball acts as the perfect lens for this sort of transmutation; accepting and amplifying the energies sent in from outside.
Energizing Rods must be attached to a block that outputs power; they may not be placed on their own.

Placing them on the bottom of a Pulsating Crystal works but may be a little awkward. Instead, consider using an Energy Meter or a Modular Router as the block to place them against. Just configure them to output to the side the Energizing Rod will be placed on.

quests.title: Improved Blast Furnace
desc: Obtaining the high heat and perfect conditions required to continue purifying Iron will require the construction of yet another magical apparatus, the Enhanced Blast Furnace.
This device uses Blazing Crystals as fuel and while it is ideal for Iron, it works well for processing many other metals as well.

quests.title: Light Machinery
desc: The following multiblock machines may be constructed with Novice Artificing Blocks:
● Metal Press
● Mixer
● Bottling Machine
● Assembler
● Sawmill

quests.title: Energetic Transference Matrix
quests.subtitle: Interdimensional Outsourcing
desc: There exists a certain imbalance in magical energies in the realms. While some, like this world, are positively overflowing with magical potential, others have a notable lack.
With the Tree of Life partially restored, it is safe to resume the ancient bargain struck with the spirits of the Otherworld, trading Source for their labor.

The Energetic Transference Matrix serves as the bridge to facilitate this exchange. When properly integrated into an arcane apparatus, materials and Source may be funneled through to the Otherworld. In exchange, the spirits residing there will transform the materials and return them, keeping the Source as payment.
Quite the fair trade, really.

quests.title: Metallurgic Infuser
desc: A specialized apparatus for magically infusing materials with various substances, the Metallurgic Infuser is critical in the process of purifying elemental iron.
With the inclusion of elemental fire, Crude Iron may be tempered into steel, while the inclusion of elemental air will purify the metal down into malleable Iron.

quests.title: Honey Compass
desc: The Cell Maze seems a likely a place as any to start. Locate it and search around for clues to the Queen's whereabouts.  They’re notable for their large cells partitioned off by Honey Web and contain countless Honey Cocoons.
Be sure to obtain the Protection of the Hive before entering!
While in the Bumblezone, Right-Click the Honey Compass in the air to attune it to the Cell Maze.

quests.title: Honey Compass
desc: At last, the Queen!
Earn the boon of the Queen by completing the tasks they require, or by returning to them that which is rightfully theirs.
Essence of the Bees is a very rare reward, indeed, so do not squander it!
Use it to first craft the Gloaming Catalyst before consuming it to receive the rest of the permanent rewards it grants.

quests.title: Honey Compass
desc: The meandering pathways in the Bumblezone are built for hive minds, and so can be difficult for others to follow. Crafting a Honey Compass will be the safest way forward.

Remember to show the bees respect while in their home. Feed bees and Honeycomb Brood Blocks some tasty honey treats to earn the Protection of the Hive. Only honored guests are allowed in their most sacred places.
While in the Bumblezone, it is possible to leave at any time by mining to the roof or floor. Above or below a certain point, you’ll be teleported back to where you came from.

quests.title: Orichalcum Ingot
desc: Known to the ancients as mountain copper, this unique alloy is of particular use in advanced enchanting as an amplifier.

quests.title: Telling of the Bees
desc: In places that still keep the old ways, bees hold a privileged position in community life. From the birth of a child to the death of a friend, news of important events are shared first with the bees.
It was widely known that the Wilden Grove were avid bee-keepers and some speculated that the bees would carry messages to them through dreams, keeping them apprised of news from far and wide.
A pretty story, but surely a simple scrying would have done the same.

Just the same, the practice never really died out, especially among the Grove. It seems likely that as the Cult of the Ur-Ghast rose in prominence in this place, the druids may have discussed the events with the bees, perhaps even seeking advice from the Queen.
Seek out the Queen Bee to see if they have any clues to offer.
In order to travel to the Bumblezone, a Teleporter must be placed directly beneath a Beehive and then an Ender Pearl thrown at the Beehive.

quests.title: Tree of Life
desc: As a boon for services rendered, the Queen grants safe passage to a lush realm of plenty.
Nourish the Tree of Life with their gifts and travel to the Overworld in search of more answers in restoring the Tree.

quests.title: Visit The Overworld
desc: With items attuned to the destination and the blessings of the Queen Bee, travel to the Overworld is now achievable.
Teleportation using the Tree of Life is prone to… drift. Be sure to bring along some means to return home as well as to set up a portal on the other side.

quests.title: ME Controller
desc: The beating heart of a magical energy network, the elementals bound into the ME Controller direct the flow of magical energies between the various components of the network, enabling a witch to perform the most wondrous of feats imaginable.

quests.title: Eldritch Engine
desc: Known for their strength and endurance, Basalz will work tirelessly to power Create machinery if properly compensated with magical energies.

quests.title: Simple Machine Frame
desc: Runic Manifolds serve to stabilize a greater dimensional pocket, allowing more spirits to work concurrently on the required task, while requiring less physical space for the apparatus itself. Fancy!

quests.title: Heavy Machinery
desc: The following multiblock machines may be constructed with Adept Artificing Blocks:
● Industrial Fermenter
● Industrial Squeezer
● Refinery
● Crusher

quests.title: Spellbound Invar Ingot
desc: While useful in its own right for precision artificing, Invar is better known amongst artificers for its unique ability to resist magical compression.
Enchant Invar to form Spellbound Invar.
The following spell form will crush items on the ground:
&5Projectile&r > &aCrush&r > &6Sensitive&r

quests.title: Quantum Network Bridge
desc: Having friends on the Other Side is proving quite advantageous, as it seems that distances mean little to them in their realm.
A Quantum Network Bridge exploits this feature quite handily, making it possible to transport items, fluids, gasses, even power over incredibly long distances and between realms.
Refer to the quest in the Applied Energistics 2 chapter for more information on constructing this multiblock.

quests.title: Tier Installers
desc: Machines feeling a bit slow? Just make room for some more Spirits in there with Tier Installers. Give them some help as well by installing Energy and Speed upgrades.

item.name: Basic Tier Installer / Advanced Tier Installer / Elite Tier Installer / Ultimate Tier Installer

quests.title: Matter Condenser
desc: Though somewhat onerous by hand, it appears to be possible to chip off small shards from the Dimensional Crystal Matrix.

Shoving large amounts of material into these crystals without any form of planar stabilization appears to have collapsed the pocket-realm, forming a singularity that appears capable of linking distant places through some other space.
A 4K Storage Component will be sufficient for crafting Singularities.

quests.title: Dimensional Crystal Matrix
desc: Though tenuous, the pocket realm contained within this Crystal Matrix should prove quite useful for storing materials.
But perhaps there’s more to be discovered here as well. Perhaps with a very sharp knife…

quests.title: Dimensional Storage Actuator
desc: As suspected, with even a minimal amount of stabilization, the Matrix can store a wondrous quantity of items.
More experimentation with planar stabilizers is certainly warranted.

quests.title: Glistering Honey Crystal
desc: Light refracts strangely through these crystals... as if it has travelled a much greater distance. Perhaps there's some truth to those stories after all?
Indeed, these Glistering Honey Crystals display a very unusual topology after infusing them with Aura.
Dimensional Crystals may be converted into a Budding block and grown much like Amethyst, making it quite simple to obtain more.

quests.title: Create
desc: Welcome to Create! At its core, Create follows the same primary purpose as Vanilla Redstone: Give the player items to enable fanciful creations.
What sort of creations, you ask? Well, just about anything. Make rideable trains, tunnel bores, massive functional windmills, or even a working Rubik’s Cube!
Your imagination is the limit.

Naturally, with so much ground to cover, these quests will not be exhaustive. Instead, the goal will be to introduce basic concepts of Create to give you a solid footing to begin experimenting on your own.

quests.title: Getting Started: Rotational Power
quests.subtitle: Some Assembly Required
desc: As with many systems, power is required. For Create, this generally means making something spin. There are, of course, multiple ways to do this, but let’s go over some basics briefly.
First, there are Generators and Consumers. Naturally, Generators will make things spin, while Consumers operate with the Rotation provided. But not all Generators and Consumers are equal.

Each Generator is capable of outputting a given number of Stress Units which are divided up among all connected Consumers. If the consumers need more SU than is being output, then the entire system will grind to a halt.
The faster a Consumer is operating, the higher its impact and the more SU it uses.
To get an idea of how many SU are being generated or consumed, wear a pair of Engineer’s Goggles while looking at a block.

As a final note, while Create has no in game guidebook, it does have a Ponder system which shows how everything works through short in game animated sequences. Hover over most items and press the Ponder key shown in the tooltip to view them.

item.name: Compressed Stone Casing / Enchanted Casing / Copper Casing

quests.title: Windmill
quests.subtitle: Batteries Not Included
desc: Perhaps the first multi part contraption to be made is the Windmill. This is a High SU generator capable of operating at high RPMs. Generating more SU and higher speed is merely a function of adding more Sails or Wool Blocks to the structure.

Where to begin? Place down the Windmill Bearing. The sticky looking green side is where the rest of the structure will be built. Power will come out the opposite end. Note that they may be built in any orientation.
Next, attach the Radial Chassis to the sticky side of the bearing. The Radial Chassis here acts as the axle for the windmill and the blades will extend from it.
The Chassis can be made sticky by Right-Clicking with a Slime Ball (does not consume the slime) and most any decorative block may be attached out to the connection limit of the Windmill.

To view the current connective radius of the Chassis, hold your wrench and look at the chassis. The highlighted blocks will be part of the structure. The radius may be adjusted with your scroll-wheel.

Note that glue is only needed for connecting blocks that aren't captured by a Chassis, for instance if blocks extend in front of the wind mill. Glue is not needed at all if sails are attached directly to the Chassis, but then, where’s the fun of that? Make it Pretty!

item.name: Windmill Sail / Windmill Sail Frame / Any #forge:wool

quests.title: Water Wheel
quests.subtitle: Like A Record, Baby
desc: The Water Wheel, while considerably simpler to set up than a Windmill, also produces far fewer SU and operates at a much lower speed.
It is useful for applications where small size is more important than speed. For instance, when making a fancy door to your base.
To get it going, simply allow water to flow past it.

quests.title: Encased Fan
quests.subtitle: I'm a Big Fan
desc: An integral part of any factory, the Encased Fan may be used both for Crafting operations and for moving items or mobs.

To use the fan for crafting, it must be set up to blow through Lava, Water, Fire, or Soul Fire. Items dropped in the stream of air on the far side will be Smelted, Washed, Smoked, or Haunted, respectively.
The air stream can pass through certain blocks like Iron Bars and Trap Doors, allowing safe containment of your Lava and Water.
Of special note, the Fan can be used to process items directly on a Depot or Belt, however the items on a belt do not stop moving while they are being processed.

To make efficient use of a fan and belt setup, make it blow across the length of the belt. Faster spin speeds mean the air stream blows farther. This also allows the fan to process multiple stacks at once.

quests.title: Shaft
quests.subtitle: Shut Yo Mouth
desc: Making a pretty windmill is probably not the only reason you’re here. Most likely, you’d like this thing to actually do something useful, but it’s way up there and we’re way down here…
As it happens, conveying rotational force is quite simple. Shafts can be used to convey power linearly while cogs may be used to change direction and speed.

quests.title: Casings
quests.subtitle: That's Below the Belt
desc: Tired of unsightly holes in your base? Shivering from drafty shaft seals? Look no further.
Right-Click a Casing onto a Shaft or Cog to cover it. Perfect for those times when the shaft is passing through walls or floors.
Covering a Cog will also prevent its shaft from connecting to any adjacent blocks unless wrenched. Existing connections are not disabled when a Casing is applied.
They also look great under Mechanical Belts.

quests.title: Brackets
quests.subtitle: Brace Yourselves
desc: That’s a long run of shaft you’ve got there. Seems a little unsupported, no?
Brackets may be attached to Shafts or Cogs and are entirely decorative. They sure do make things look nicer though!

quests.title: Gearbox
quests.subtitle: Let's Try a Change in Tack
desc: Slightly more costly than a pair of cogs, Gear Boxes serve the same purpose as perpendicular cogs, to change the direction of a shaft line.
However, they have a slight advantage in that they can be used to split power off in two directions. They also have a vertical variant to get a shaft line running up or down.

quests.title: Cogwheels
quests.subtitle: Spacely's Sprockets
desc: Just because our windmill is running a little slowly doesn’t mean everything else needs to. The rotational speed of a system can be stepped up (or down) by way of simple gear ratios.

For instance, assume your power is turning a small cogwheel. Connecting the teeth to a large cogwheel’s teeth will result in the shaft of the larger cogwheel rotating at half the speed of the drive shaft.
Similarly, a large cogwheel that is interlocked with the teeth of a small cogwheel will cause that cogwheel’s shaft to rotate at twice the speed.
These effects may be chained but bear in mind that the faster the consumers in this system run, the higher the SU cost.
Additionally, two large cogwheels can be interlocked perpendicularly to allow a shaft to change directions. Useful for going around corners or bringing power down from high above.

quests.title: Mechanical Belts
quests.subtitle: You're On a Roll Now
desc: As with many things in Create, the Mechanical Belt is a multi-purpose item.
Its primary purpose is item transportation and can carry items along horizontally, as well as up and down 45-degree slopes.
However, it can also convey power from one shaft to another. This can be an excellent way to power multiple parallel shafts while maintaining the direction of rotation.
A single belt can stretch up to 20 blocks and each block space could conceivably attach it to another shaft line if necessary.
To attach them to a Shaft, simply place two Shafts and then Right-Click each with the belt in hand. Right-Click a Shaft into an existing Belt to add a connection.

quests.title: Encased Chain Drive
quests.subtitle: Working on the Chain Gang
desc: Encased Chain Drives may be used much like belts, connecting perpendicular shafts together.
They may also be used to change the direction of power by placing multiple of them in-line and rotating them 90-degrees from one another.

quests.title: Rotation Speed Controller
quests.subtitle: Kick It Into Overdrive
desc: It is not always practical to chain hundreds of cogs to achieve the exact right speed. Enter, the Rotation Speed Controller. Place a Large Cogwheel in the top slot and power it.
The Controller will automatically adjust to any RPM on its two output shafts. Set the speed with the scroll-wheel.

quests.title: Compressed Stone Funnel
quests.subtitle: Bit of a Slippery Slope
desc: Funnels serve both to push into and pull from inventories.
A funnel attached to a chest, for instance, can extract from the chest and dump onto an adjacent Belt line. Similarly, a belt feeding into a funnel will push items into the attached inventory.

quests.title: Chutes
quests.subtitle: Learning To Take Things in Slide
desc: The chute is a simple yet fast way to convey items downwards. Simply drop them in the top and they’ll come out the bottom.

The advantage that chutes offer over simply dropping an item in the world is that they can move items at a 45-degree angle and multiple chutes can converge into a single chute, allowing better control of where the item ends up.

Chutes may also be used to convey items upwards. If a chute has an encased fan set up directly on top of it, it can be used to pull items off a Belt. Of course, getting that item out requires some way of extracting from the chute, such as a Funnel.

quests.title: Compressed Stone Tunnel
quests.subtitle: Double Slit Experiment
desc: Far from simple covers for your Mechanical Belts, Tunnels serve a useful purpose in splitting items.
As a stack of items passes through an Andesite Tunnel, it will automatically take one item from the stack and place it onto adjacent belts or depots.
Brass Tunnels work a bit differently than Andesite Tunnels. Rather than splitting onto adjacent belts, a line of Tunnels can be formed along multiple parallel belts.
As items pass into one tunnel, they’ll be evenly split among all connected tunnels on the other side.

quests.title: Depot
quests.subtitle: Buffer Allocation Failed
desc: A simple item buffer.
Depots will hold a single stack of items, but they will also interact with Encased Fan Washing, Blasting, Smoking, and Haunting recipes, as well as the Plate Press.

quests.title: Enchanted Arm
quests.subtitle: Number 5 is Alive
desc: Mechanical Arms serve as advanced short range item transport. They may be linked to multiple points at once for both extraction and insertion operations
Linking is done prior to placing the Arm, simply Right-Click it onto permitted inventory types, such as Depots, Funnels, or Belts. Right-Click again to toggle between input and output modes.
The Mechanical Arm can reach up to four blocks away in total.

quests.title: Millstone
quests.subtitle: You Know What Really Grinds My Gears?
desc: Millstones have been used for ages, representing some of our oldest technology still in use. They’re far more efficient than grinding things by hand.
Create’s Millstone is an excellent early way to stretch materials a little further.

quests.title: Crushing Wheels
quests.subtitle: It's Crunch Time
desc: Crushing Wheels are the big brother to the Millstone used until now. In general, they do a better job, producing more per input than the Millstone would.
Their harder surface is also capable of dealing with materials that the Millstone cannot.

Setting up a pair of Crushing Wheels will require a little bit of clever thinking as both wheels must be rotated in opposite directions with the tops rotating inwards towards the point where the two wheels meet.

Place the wheels with a single block gap between them. Items may be either dropped in the top or inserted in a more controlled manner by funneling them into the ‘block’ space where the two wheels meet.
Crushing Wheels may also be placed horizontally, allowing them to interface nicely with a Belt system.

quests.title: Deployer
quests.subtitle: Getting Down to Brass Tacks
desc: Useful for both Crafting and other Automation pursuits, the Deployer will find it’s way into many creations.

An item may be inserted into the Deployer by Belt, Funnel, Hopper, or most any other item transport method. When powered, it will continuously attempt to Right-Click the held item on any entity in front of it, be it item or mob.
Right-Clicking the hand with a Wrench will switch the Deployer into Left-Click mode, allowing it to attack mobs with a weapon, or otherwise interact with things that need to be Left-Clicked.

quests.title: Getting Started: Material Processing
quests.subtitle: Just a Little Something I Whipped Up
desc: With some basic power and logistics under our belts, it’s time we get our hands dirty and get down to business. Create offers several new crafting mechanics that are important to understand to work with the mod.

item.name: Compressed Stone Casing / Enchanted Casing / Copper Casing

quests.title: Mechanical Press
quests.subtitle: Boil 'em, Mash 'em, Stick 'em in a Stew
desc: The Mechanical Press is a great way to flatten things in need of smashing. It will also compact materials when combined with a Basin, making Ingots from Nuggets, for example.
For Plates, the Press can be installed over a Belt, Depot, or any other block.
If placed over a Belt, it will automatically cause the Belt to pause while the Press is operating.
When over a Depot, it will similarly work as soon as it detects an item below that needs pressing.
While over any other block, however, a redstone signal is required to make it start.

quests.title: Mechanical Mixer
quests.subtitle: There's Been a Mix-Up, Officer
desc: The Mechanical Mixer helps blend both solids and liquids into more useful forms, from brewing potions, making tea, or making advanced alloys, the mixer does it all. A basin below the mixer is required.
Note that some recipes require heat, this is provided by way of a Blaze Burner.

If a Depot or Item Drain is placed adjacent and one block down from the Basin, recipes will automatically be output. A small spout will appear on the Basin when the Depot or Item Drain is placed correctly.

quests.title: Blaze Burner
quests.subtitle: Dat Ash Tho
desc: When high temperatures are required, there’s nothing quite like the scorching heat of the Nether. Why not bring it home with you?
Blaze Burners are created by Right-Clicking an empty burner on either a Blaze (consumes the mob) or a Blaze Spawner (does not consume the spawner). They’ll burn hot, but not forever.
Feed them coal or other burnable material to get them riled up again if they cool down.

quests.title: Blaze Cake
quests.subtitle: Forbidden Snacks
desc: What do you mean that’s not hot enough? Well, let them eat cake!
When a recipe calls for Super-Heating, a Blaze Cake is in order to fuel the Blaze Burner.
Making Blaze Cake will really test your skills as it combines a lot of different mechanics. How far can you take your automation?

quests.title: Mechanical Pump
quests.subtitle: Archimedean Screw
desc: Just as moving items isn’t free, so to does it require some rotational force to pump and work with fluids.
The Mechanical Pump accepts power from a cog, pressurizing a section of pipe to cause fluid to flow in one direction or the other, depending on the direction of rotation.
The block has a handy little directional indicator to help visualize the flow. A single pump can pressurize a large section of pipe, so be sure to spread them out.

quests.title: Fluid Valve
quests.subtitle: Shut The Front Door
desc: Fluid valves may be opened and closed by applying some rotational force, for example with a Valve Handle.

quests.title: Smart Fluid Pipe
quests.subtitle: Reverse Osmosis Filter
desc: Doing the impossible is just another Tuesday in modded. Smart Fluid Pipes act as a fluid filter, either controlling what is allowed to be pulled from a connected tank, or what is allowed to continue down the line.

quests.title: Fluid Tanks
quests.subtitle: Unfathomably Deep
desc: Fluid Tanks are a thematic multi-block tank for all your fluid storing needs.
While they can't be interacted with by the player directly, needing pipes to insert and extract fluids, they merge with adjacent tanks to form large multi-blocks for bulk storage.
They can have a 1x1, 2x2, or 3x3 base and may be extended vertically.

quests.title: Enchanted Crafter
desc: For those times when a simple 3x3 grid simply isn’t good enough, there’s the Mechanical Crafter. Or, Crafters, to be precise. These interlocking blocks connect to form a large crafting interface. Each block accepting a single item for the craft.
Several advanced items may only be crafted this way.

Take note when placing the crafters themselves as there will be an arrow pointing towards the block that was clicked to place it. This arrow indicates which way items will travel as the crafters work and all arrows must connect to a single crafter.

For example, placing the first crafter on the ground will make the arrow point down, this would be the output. A crafter to the side of the first would need to be placed against the side so that its arrow points into the first, making a channel.

Crafter Slot Covers can be used to disable a given slot, which is required for any craft that has empty spaces in it. For instance, when crafting a chest with a 3x3 grid of Mechanical Crafters, the middle slot must be covered.
Items may be inserted with hoppers, belts and funnels, mechanical arms and more. Experiment to see what you can come up with!

quests.title: Spout
quests.subtitle: Spouting Off Nonsense
desc: The spout is paired with a Depot by placing it above the Depot. It will attempt to fill any item appearing on the Depot. For example, to make buckets of water, fill potion bottles, or make delicious tea!

quests.title: Modular Contraptions
desc: Modular Contraptions are build-it-yourself multiblock structures with nearly endless possibilities.
They can either be fixed in place and run using rotational power, or they can be attached to a minecart and run for free, requiring only powered rails to keep the cart moving.
The following are some of the specialized blocks that may be used for these contraptions.

quests.title: Mechanical Piston
quests.subtitle: Engineering Outreach Program
desc: When it comes to moving contraptions, Mechanical Pistons can be a great early start.

As a simple example of where one might use these, imagine a long field of crops. A Mechanical Piston could be used to push a harvesting contraption back and forth over the field periodically to gather crops.

quests.title: Cart Assembler
quests.subtitle: Putting the Cart Before the Horse
desc: Cart Assemblers are used to build a contraption destined to ride a mine cart.
The contraption should be built on top of the Assembler. Once prepared, giving the assembler a Redstone signal will convert all connected blocks into one entity.
The entire cart can then be picked up by using a wrench on it, allowing for easy transport of the device.

A great example of a mine cart-based contraption would be a tunnel bore mining machine. It could be set up to lay down its own track in front of it and pull up track behind it. It could even build its own bridges to avoid ravines!

quests.title: Mechanical Bearing
quests.subtitle: Getting Out of an Unbearable Situation
desc: Similar to Windmill Bearings, Mechanical Bearings may be used to build rotating contraptions.
For instance, a long sweeping armed contraption could be built that swings through a tree farm, cutting down all the trees it encounters.

quests.title: Chassis
desc: Chassis blocks serve to form a base for larger creations.
Linear chassis connect to one another along the darker edge and will automatically be treated as a ‘whole’ piece that other parts may be glued to.
They will also capture a line of blocks attached to the lighter side if glue is placed on the chassis itself.
Similarly, Radial chassis can capture blocks in a circular plane so long as they all touch and the one in contact with the light face of the chassis has been glued in place.

This results in the ability to build very large contraptions with very little glue. However, they are not required. Instead, blocks may simply be glued together to form a larger piece in an irregular shape.
Worry not, once the contraption is formed, the glue marks will become invisible, allowing for very aesthetic builds.
Use your scroll wheel while holding a wrench and looking at the chassis to configure its capture range.
Note: A slime ball may be used infinitely to set glue marks on Chassis blocks themselves. Right-Click with the slime ball to apply to one side. Double Right-Click to apply to all sides.

quests.title: Mechanical Harvester
quests.subtitle: Outstanding In Its Field
desc: A smart harvester that gently harvests only mature crops.

quests.title: Mechanical Drill
quests.subtitle: Nothing to See Here, Just a Boring Machine
desc: Mobile or Stationary, the Mechanical Drill serves as a capable mining apparatus.

quests.title: Mechanical Plough
quests.subtitle: A Groundbreaking Innovation
desc: Ploughing Fields is hard work. Make a machine to do it for you!
The Mechanical Plow is useful for more than simple farm maintenance, however, and can make a great addition to a moving minecart machine for pulling up extra track behind it.

quests.title: Mechanical Saw
quests.subtitle: Cutting Edge Technology
desc: From Chopping Trees to Carving Stone, this Saw has seen it all.
When stationary and powered, it can serve both for cutting logs to planks and for any stonecutter recipe. Stonecutter recipes will give a random output unless a filter is set on the Saw itself.
When attached to a moving machine, it will chop whole trees in one swoop. Handy for a simple tree farm.

quests.title: Portable Interfaces
quests.subtitle: Plug and Play
desc: In many cases, the tools that can be attached to a moving contraption will also automatically pick up the items they’re harvesting, so long as there is ample storage on the device.
Simply gluing a chest in place is sufficient for providing that storage place, but getting items out again is another matter.

Interfaces act as a proxy for the inventories on moving machines. Whenever a Portable Interface on a contraption meets an Interface sitting in the world, the contraption will pause briefly, creating a connection.
If something is set up to pull from, or push to that interface, the machine will remain paused until nothing is flowing through the Interface. Once the flow has stopped, it will move on.
To prevent this pause, or interrupt it early, a Redstone signal can be supplied to the fixed position Interface.

quests.title: Rope Pulley
quests.subtitle: It Has It's Ups and Downs
desc: Need a Lift?
Build your own with a Rope Pulley by attaching your own platform.
Use a Gearshift to reverse direction with ease.

quests.title: Adjustable Chain Gearshift
quests.subtitle: Shifting Into Higher Gear
desc: Slightly finer control than messing with gear ratios, an Adjustable Chain Gearshift uses a Redstone signal to set the variable speed, up to twice the input speed.
Consider using an Analogue Lever to easily set a fixed speed.

quests.title: Hose Pulley
quests.subtitle: Well, There's an Upside and a Downside
desc: With a Hose Pulley, fluids may be pumped into or out of the world. Create massive lakes or drain them dry to let your factory grow!

Very large bodies, such as oceans or massive lava lakes in the Nether will be considered Bottomless, so if you wish to drain something like an Ocean Monument, it may still be necessary to build some retaining walls to break things up.
Note, the Hose Pulley does not pump by itself. Lower the hose into the fluid body set up a Mechanical Pump to do the work for you.

quests.title: Gearshift
quests.subtitle: Time to Switch Things Up
desc: Need to reverse direction? Then the Gearshift is what you’re looking for.
Applying a Redstone signal to the block will cause the output side to start spinning in the opposite direction relative to the drive side.

quests.title: Clutch
quests.subtitle: Going to Have to Stop You Right There
desc: Quite the simple device, really. A Clutch disengages power on a shaft line, making for a simple on/off switch.
It could useful for more advanced contraptions that need precise timing, as well.

quests.title: Builder's Tea
quests.subtitle: Hello Brew-TEA-Full!
desc: Stayed out too late par-tea-ing like it's 1773? Need a little more tranquili-tea in your life?
Try some Builder's Tea! It doesn't take too long to prepare.

quests.title: Item Drain
quests.subtitle: Bless the Drains Down in Africa
desc: The Item drain is useful for draining fluids from any fluid-containing items, like buckets or bottles. It's also quite handy for getting fluids out of a Basin.
It has small internal tank, from which fluids can be accessed by pipes.

quests.title: Steam Engine
quests.subtitle: A Newcomen on the Block
desc: With a source of heat, water, and an enclosed space, a Steam Engine can be manufactured to produce enormous amounts of SU.

A basic Boiler setup requires four Fluid Tanks placed in a square and at least one Steam Engine attached. Filling the tanks with water and providing a source of heat below it will get things moving. Click a Shaft against the Steam Engine to get power out of the system

Boilers may be heated passively by any campfire or magma block, however by actively heating them with a Blaze Burner, they reach much higher temperatures and therefore produce more SU. Either way, they’ll need a constant supply of Water, with more used per operation as the number of Engines increases.

quests.title: Trains
quests.subtitle: Watch Your Step
desc: Be it simple Transportation of goods or people, or powering a moving quarry, Trains offer an elegant solution.

Trains are large mobile contraptions that may be automated by way of Train Stations, Train Schedules, and Train Signals. They’ll move through un-loaded chunks, making long-distance transport of materials feasible; only the Station needs to be loaded. Drills and other machines will not function in un-loaded chunks, however.
Building trains begins with the Train Station. Due to the complexity of this feature, watching the Ponder for each of the various pieces of Train equipment is highly recommended.

quests.title: Getting Started: Logistics and Storage
quests.subtitle: From Here to There, Funny Things Were Everywhere
desc: Half the joy of Create is seeing things move, and its logistics options do not disappoint. From Belts that render their contents, to Pipes showing fluids flowing through them, Create offers ways of moving around most anything.

item.name: Compressed Stone Casing / Enchanted Casing / Copper Casing

quests.title: Item Vault
quests.subtitle: Hoarder's Dream
desc: Like the shipping crates they replicate, Item Vaults can hold an enormous number of items per block. They don’t allow manual interaction, however, so items must be inserted or extracted via automation.
Vaults may be combined to form a multi-block storage container. The base must remain square and can be expanded up to 3x3, while the length can be up to 3x the diameter for a maximum size of 3x3x9.

quests.title: Eldritch Engine
quests.subtitle: Getting Wired Up
desc: These simple electric motors make an excellent and compact source of SU.

Provide power from any source of FE to get them spun up and set their operating speed on the back. Spinning faster allows them to provide more SU, but at an increasing FE cost. For high SU, low speed applications, be sure to pair them with a Rotation Speed Controller.

quests.title: Straw
quests.subtitle: A Quantum of Solace
desc: Who knew a Blaze could get thirsty? They’re certainly not interested in Water, but other combustible fluids seem to hit the spot just fine.
Giving the Blaze a Straw allows them to accept liquid fuels instead. Check the uses on the Straw or Blaze Burner to see what fuels are valid.

quests.title: Rolling Mill
quests.subtitle: Keep them ingots rollin'
desc: The Rolling Mill is well suited for rolling out some clean rods or extruding wires suitable for electronics use. These may be used manually, or inline with conveyor belts as part of a larger factory.

quests.title: Tesla Coil
quests.subtitle: Assault and Battery
desc: A high-powered electrical device capable of charging objects wirelessly by induced currents, the Tesla Coil can be quite useful in any factory.

When placed above a Belt or Depot and provided sufficient power, the Tesla coil will impart a charge into items on the Belt or Depot. This works not only with crafting recipes, but also for charging equipment like tools and batteries.
The Coil may be deployed for more destructive purposes as well by placing it and providing a Redstone Signal in addition to the power. In this mode, it will damage nearby entities

quests.title: Alternator
quests.subtitle: Spin Me Right Round
desc: Working on the same principles as Electric Motors, Alternators effectively just operate in reverse. By spinning the shaft, a current is induced in the coils which may be used to power devices.
The faster these are spun, the more SU they’ll use and FE they’ll produce.

quests.title: Mechanical Roller
desc: Placed in front of a rail-based contraption, Mechanical Rollers may be used to flatten terrain or fill gaps below the contraption.
This can be put to great use with a contraption that is designed to lay down track over a great distance.

quests.title: Elevator Pulley
desc: A more advanced form of the Rope Pulley which allows for intelligent floor control as an elevator. The elevator may be called from any floor and can be sent to any floor without stopping between.

quests.title: Create
desc: Welcome to Create! At its core, Create follows the same primary purpose as Vanilla Redstone: Give the player items to enable fanciful creations.
What sort of creations, you ask? Well, just about anything. Make rideable trains, tunnel bores, massive functional windmills, or even a working Rubik’s Cube!
Your imagination is the limit.

Naturally, with so much ground to cover, these quests will not be exhaustive. Instead, the goal will be to introduce basic concepts of Create to give you a solid footing to begin experimenting on your own.

quests.title: Getting Started: Rotational Power
quests.subtitle: Some Assembly Required
desc: As with many systems, power is required. For Create, this generally means making something spin. There are, of course, multiple ways to do this, but let’s go over some basics briefly.
First, there are Generators and Consumers. Naturally, Generators will make things spin, while Consumers operate with the Rotation provided. But not all Generators and Consumers are equal.

Each Generator is capable of outputting a given number of Stress Units which are divided up among all connected Consumers. If the consumers need more SU than is being output, then the entire system will grind to a halt.
The faster a Consumer is operating, the higher its impact and the more SU it uses.
To get an idea of how many SU are being generated or consumed, wear a pair of Engineer’s Goggles while looking at a block.

As a final note, while Create has no in game guidebook, it does have a Ponder system which shows how everything works through short in game animated sequences. Hover over most items and press the Ponder key shown in the tooltip to view them.

item.name: Compressed Stone Casing / Enchanted Casing / Copper Casing

quests.title: Windmill
quests.subtitle: Batteries Not Included
desc: Perhaps the first multi part contraption to be made is the Windmill. This is a High SU generator capable of operating at high RPMs. Generating more SU and higher speed is merely a function of adding more Sails to the structure.

Where to begin? Place down the Windmill Bearing. The sticky looking green side is where the rest of the structure will be built. Power will come out the opposite end. Note that they may be built in any orientation.
Next, attach the Radial Chassis to the sticky side of the bearing. The Radial Chassis here acts as the axle for the windmill and the blades will extend from it.
The Chassis can be made sticky by Right-Clicking with a Slime Ball (does not consume the slime) and most any decorative block may be attached out to the connection limit of the Windmill.

To view the current connective radius of the Chassis, hold your wrench and look at the chassis. The highlighted blocks will be part of the structure. The radius may be adjusted with your scroll-wheel.

Note that glue is only needed for connecting blocks that aren't captured by a Chassis, for instance if blocks extend in front of the wind mill. Glue is not needed at all if sails are attached directly to the Chassis, but then, where’s the fun of that? Make it Pretty!

item.name: Windmill Sail / Windmill Sail Frame / Any #

quests.title: Water Wheel
quests.subtitle: Like A Record, Baby
desc: The Water Wheel, while considerably simpler to set up than a Windmill, also produces far fewer SU and operates at a much lower speed.
It is useful for applications where small size is more important than speed. For instance, when making a fancy door to your base.
To get it going, simply allow water to flow past it.

quests.title: Encased Fan
quests.subtitle: I'm a Big Fan
desc: An integral part of any factory, the Encased Fan may be used both for Crafting operations and for moving items or mobs.

To use the fan for crafting, it must be set up to blow through Lava, Water, Fire, or Soul Fire. Items dropped in the stream of air on the far side will be Smelted, Washed, Smoked, or Haunted, respectively.
The air stream can pass through certain blocks like Iron Bars and Trap Doors, allowing safe containment of your Lava and Water.
Of special note, the Fan can be used to process items directly on a Depot or Belt, however the items on a belt do not stop moving while they are being processed.

To make efficient use of a fan and belt setup, make it blow across the length of the belt. Faster spin speeds mean the air stream blows farther. This also allows the fan to process multiple stacks at once.

quests.title: Shaft
quests.subtitle: Shut Yo Mouth
desc: Making a pretty windmill is probably not the only reason you’re here. Most likely, you’d like this thing to actually do something useful, but it’s way up there and we’re way down here…
As it happens, conveying rotational force is quite simple. Shafts can be used to convey power linearly while cogs may be used to change direction and speed.

quests.title: Casings
quests.subtitle: That's Below the Belt
desc: Tired of unsightly holes in your base? Shivering from drafty shaft seals? Look no further.
Right-Click a Casing onto a Shaft or Cog to cover it. Perfect for those times when the shaft is passing through walls or floors.
Covering a Cog will also prevent its shaft from connecting to any adjacent blocks unless wrenched. Existing connections are not disabled when a Casing is applied.
They also look great under Mechanical Belts.

quests.title: Brackets
quests.subtitle: Brace Yourselves
desc: That’s a long run of shaft you’ve got there. Seems a little unsupported, no?
Brackets may be attached to Shafts or Cogs and are entirely decorative. They sure do make things look nicer though!

quests.title: Gearbox
quests.subtitle: Let's Try a Change in Tack
desc: Slightly more costly than a pair of cogs, Gear Boxes serve the same purpose as perpendicular cogs, to change the direction of a shaft line.
However, they have a slight advantage in that they can be used to split power off in two directions. They also have a vertical variant to get a shaft line running up or down.

quests.title: Cogwheels
quests.subtitle: Spacely's Sprockets
desc: Just because our windmill is running a little slowly doesn’t mean everything else needs to. The rotational speed of a system can be stepped up (or down) by way of simple gear ratios.

For instance, assume your power is turning a small cogwheel. Connecting the teeth to a large cogwheel’s teeth will result in the shaft of the larger cogwheel rotating at half the speed of the drive shaft.
Similarly, a large cogwheel that is interlocked with the teeth of a small cogwheel will cause that cogwheel’s shaft to rotate at twice the speed.
These effects may be chained but bear in mind that the faster the consumers in this system run, the higher the SU cost.
Additionally, two large cogwheels can be interlocked perpendicularly to allow a shaft to change directions. Useful for going around corners or bringing power down from high above.

quests.title: Mechanical Belts
quests.subtitle: You're On a Roll Now
desc: As with many things in Create, the Mechanical Belt is a multi-purpose item.
Its primary purpose is item transportation and can carry items along horizontally, as well as up and down 45-degree slopes.
However, it can also convey power from one shaft to another. This can be an excellent way to power multiple parallel shafts while maintaining the direction of rotation.
A single belt can stretch up to 20 blocks and each block space could conceivably attach it to another shaft line if necessary.
To attach them to a Shaft, simply place two Shafts and then Right-Click each with the belt in hand. Right-Click a Shaft into an existing Belt to add a connection.

quests.title: Encased Chain Drive
quests.subtitle: Working on the Chain Gang
desc: Encased Chain Drives may be used much like belts, connecting perpendicular shafts together.
They may also be used to change the direction of power by placing multiple of them in-line and rotating them 90-degrees from one another.

quests.title: Rotation Speed Controller
quests.subtitle: Kick It Into Overdrive
desc: It is not always practical to chain hundreds of cogs to achieve the exact right speed. Enter, the Rotation Speed Controller. Place a Large Cogwheel in the top slot and power it.
The Controller will automatically adjust to any RPM on its two output shafts. Set the speed with the scroll-wheel.

quests.title: Compressed Stone Funnel
quests.subtitle: Bit of a Slippery Slope
desc: Funnels serve both to push into and pull from inventories.
A funnel attached to a chest, for instance, can extract from the chest and dump onto an adjacent Belt line. Similarly, a belt feeding into a funnel will push items into the attached inventory.

quests.title: Chutes
quests.subtitle: Learning To Take Things in Slide
desc: The chute is a simple yet fast way to convey items downwards. Simply drop them in the top and they’ll come out the bottom.

The advantage that chutes offer over simply dropping an item in the world is that they can move items at a 45-degree angle and multiple chutes can converge into a single chute, allowing better control of where the item ends up.

Chutes may also be used to convey items upwards. If a chute has an encased fan set up directly on top of it, it can be used to pull items off a Belt. Of course, getting that item out requires some way of extracting from the chute, such as a Funnel.

quests.title: Compressed Stone Tunnel
quests.subtitle: Double Slit Experiment
desc: Far from simple covers for your Mechanical Belts, Tunnels serve a useful purpose in splitting items.
As a stack of items passes through an Andesite Tunnel, it will automatically take one item from the stack and place it onto adjacent belts or depots.
Brass Tunnels work a bit differently than Andesite Tunnels. Rather than splitting onto adjacent belts, a line of Tunnels can be formed along multiple parallel belts.
As items pass into one tunnel, they’ll be evenly split among all connected tunnels on the other side.

quests.title: Depot
quests.subtitle: Buffer Allocation Failed
desc: A simple item buffer.
Depots will hold a single stack of items, but they will also interact with Encased Fan Washing, Blasting, Smoking, and Haunting recipes, as well as the Plate Press.

quests.title: Enchanted Arm
quests.subtitle: Number 5 is Alive
desc: Mechanical Arms serve as advanced short range item transport. They may be linked to multiple points at once for both extraction and insertion operations
Linking is done prior to placing the Arm, simply Right-Click it onto permitted inventory types, such as Depots, Funnels, or Belts. Right-Click again to toggle between input and output modes.
The Mechanical Arm can reach up to four blocks away in total.

quests.title: Millstone
quests.subtitle: You Know What Really Grinds My Gears?
desc: Millstones have been used for ages, representing some of our oldest technology still in use. They’re far more efficient than grinding things by hand.
Create’s Millstone is an excellent early way to stretch materials a little further.

quests.title: Crushing Wheels
quests.subtitle: It's Crunch Time
desc: Crushing Wheels are the big brother to the Millstone used until now. In general, they do a better job, producing more per input than the Millstone would.
Their harder surface is also capable of dealing with materials that the Millstone cannot.

Setting up a pair of Crushing Wheels will require a little bit of clever thinking as both wheels must be rotated in opposite directions with the tops rotating inwards towards the point where the two wheels meet.

Place the wheels with a single block gap between them. Items may be either dropped in the top or inserted in a more controlled manner by funneling them into the ‘block’ space where the two wheels meet.
Crushing Wheels may also be placed horizontally, allowing them to interface nicely with a Belt system.

quests.title: Deployer
quests.subtitle: Getting Down to Brass Tacks
desc: Useful for both Crafting and other Automation pursuits, the Deployer will find its way into many creations.

An item may be inserted into the Deployer by Belt, Funnel, Hopper, or most any other item transport method. When powered, it will continuously attempt to Right-Click the held item on any entity in front of it, be it item or mob.
Right-Clicking the hand with a Wrench will switch the Deployer into Left-Click mode, allowing it to attack mobs with a weapon, or otherwise interact with things that need to be Left-Clicked.

quests.title: Getting Started: Material Processing
quests.subtitle: Just a Little Something I Whipped Up
desc: With some basic power and logistics under our belts, it’s time we get our hands dirty and get down to business. Create offers several new crafting mechanics that are important to understand to work with the mod.

item.name: Compressed Stone Casing / Enchanted Casing / Copper Casing

quests.title: Mechanical Press
quests.subtitle: Boil 'em, Mash 'em, Stick 'em in a Stew
desc: The Mechanical Press is a great way to flatten things in need of smashing. It will also compact materials when combined with a Basin, making Ingots from Nuggets, for example.
For Plates, the Press can be installed over a Belt, Depot, or any other block.
If placed over a Belt, it will automatically cause the Belt to pause while the Press is operating.
When over a Depot, it will similarly work as soon as it detects an item below that needs pressing.
While over any other block, however, a redstone signal is required to make it start.

quests.title: Mechanical Mixer
quests.subtitle: There's Been a Mix-Up, Officer
desc: The Mechanical Mixer helps blend both solids and liquids into more useful forms, from brewing potions, making tea, or making advanced alloys, the mixer does it all. A basin below the mixer is required.
Note that some recipes require heat, this is provided by way of a Blaze Burner.

If a Depot or Item Drain is placed adjacent and one block down from the Basin, recipes will automatically be output. A small spout will appear on the Basin when the Depot or Item Drain is placed correctly.

quests.title: Blaze Burner
quests.subtitle: Dat Ash Tho
desc: When high temperatures are required, there’s nothing quite like the scorching heat of the Nether. Why not bring it home with you?
Blaze Burners are created by Right-Clicking an empty burner on either a Blaze (consumes the mob) or a Blaze Spawner (does not consume the spawner). They’ll burn hot, but not forever.
Feed them coal or other burnable material to get them riled up again if they cool down.

quests.title: Blaze Cake
quests.subtitle: Forbidden Snacks
desc: What do you mean that’s not hot enough? Well, let them eat cake!
When a recipe calls for Super-Heating, a Blaze Cake is in order to fuel the Blaze Burner.
Making Blaze Cake will really test your skills as it combines a lot of different mechanics. How far can you take your automation?

quests.title: Mechanical Pump
quests.subtitle: Archimedean Screw
desc: Just as moving items isn’t free, so to does it require some rotational force to pump and work with fluids.
The Mechanical Pump accepts power from a cog, pressurizing a section of pipe to cause fluid to flow in one direction or the other, depending on the direction of rotation.
The block has a handy little directional indicator to help visualize the flow. A single pump can pressurize a large section of pipe, so be sure to spread them out.

quests.title: Fluid Valve
quests.subtitle: Shut The Front Door
desc: Fluid valves may be opened and closed by applying some rotational force, for example with a Valve Handle.

quests.title: Smart Fluid Pipe
quests.subtitle: Reverse Osmosis Filter
desc: Doing the impossible is just another Tuesday in modded. Smart Fluid Pipes act as a fluid filter, either controlling what is allowed to be pulled from a connected tank, or what is allowed to continue down the line.

quests.title: Fluid Tanks
quests.subtitle: Unfathomably Deep
desc: Fluid Tanks are a thematic multi-block tank for all your fluid storing needs.
While they can't be interacted with by the player directly, needing pipes to insert and extract fluids, they merge with adjacent tanks to form large multi-blocks for bulk storage.
They can have a 1x1, 2x2, or 3x3 base and may be extended vertically.
Note, the storage capacity of Fluid Tanks has been increased substantially in Enigmatica 9.

quests.title: Spout
quests.subtitle: Spouting Off Nonsense
desc: The spout is paired with a Depot by placing it above the Depot. It will attempt to fill any item appearing on the Depot. For example, to make buckets of water, fill potion bottles, or make delicious tea!

quests.title: Modular Contraptions
desc: Modular Contraptions are build-it-yourself multiblock structures with nearly endless possibilities.
They can either be fixed in place and run using rotational power, or they can be attached to a minecart and run for free, requiring only powered rails to keep the cart moving.
The following are some of the specialized blocks that may be used for these contraptions.

quests.title: Mechanical Piston
quests.subtitle: Engineering Outreach Program
desc: When it comes to moving contraptions, Mechanical Pistons can be a great early start.

As a simple example of where one might use these, imagine a long field of crops. A Mechanical Piston could be used to push a harvesting contraption back and forth over the field periodically to gather crops.

quests.title: Cart Assembler
quests.subtitle: Putting the Cart Before the Horse
desc: Cart Assemblers are used to build a contraption destined to ride a mine cart.
The contraption should be built on top of the Assembler. Once prepared, giving the assembler a Redstone signal will convert all connected blocks into one entity.
The entire cart can then be picked up by using a wrench on it, allowing for easy transport of the device.

A great example of a mine cart-based contraption would be a tunnel bore mining machine. It could be set up to lay down its own track in front of it and pull up track behind it. It could even build its own bridges to avoid ravines!

quests.title: Mechanical Bearing
quests.subtitle: Getting Out of an Unbearable Situation
desc: Similar to Windmill Bearings, Mechanical Bearings may be used to build rotating contraptions.
For instance, a long sweeping armed contraption could be built that swings through a tree farm, cutting down all the trees it encounters.

quests.title: Chassis
desc: Chassis blocks serve to form a base for larger creations.
Linear chassis connect to one another along the darker edge and will automatically be treated as a ‘whole’ piece that other parts may be glued to.
They will also capture a line of blocks attached to the lighter side if glue is placed on the chassis itself.
Similarly, Radial chassis can capture blocks in a circular plane so long as they all touch and the one in contact with the light face of the chassis has been glued in place.

This results in the ability to build very large contraptions with very little glue. However, they are not required. Instead, blocks may simply be glued together to form a larger piece in an irregular shape.
Worry not, once the contraption is formed, the glue marks will become invisible, allowing for very aesthetic builds.
Use your scroll wheel while holding a wrench and looking at the chassis to configure its capture range.
Note: A slime ball may be used infinitely to set glue marks on Chassis blocks themselves. Right-Click with the slime ball to apply to one side. Double Right-Click to apply to all sides.

quests.title: Mechanical Harvester
quests.subtitle: Outstanding In Its Field
desc: A smart harvester that gently harvests only mature crops.

quests.title: Mechanical Drill
quests.subtitle: Nothing to See Here, Just a Boring Machine
desc: Mobile or Stationary, the Mechanical Drill serves as a capable mining apparatus.

quests.title: Mechanical Plough
quests.subtitle: A Groundbreaking Innovation
desc: Ploughing Fields is hard work. Make a machine to do it for you!
The Mechanical Plow is useful for more than simple farm maintenance, however, and can make a great addition to a moving minecart machine for pulling up extra track behind it.

quests.title: Mechanical Saw
quests.subtitle: Cutting Edge Technology
desc: From Chopping Trees to Carving Stone, this Saw has seen it all.
When stationary and powered, it can serve both for cutting logs to planks and for any stonecutter recipe. Stonecutter recipes will give a random output unless a filter is set on the Saw itself.
When attached to a moving machine, it will chop whole trees in one swoop. Handy for a simple tree farm.

quests.title: Portable Interfaces
quests.subtitle: Plug and Play
desc: In many cases, the tools that can be attached to a moving contraption will also automatically pick up the items they’re harvesting, so long as there is ample storage on the device.
Simply gluing a chest in place is sufficient for providing that storage place, but getting items out again is another matter.

Interfaces act as a proxy for the inventories on moving machines. Whenever a Portable Interface on a contraption meets an Interface sitting in the world, the contraption will pause briefly, creating a connection.
If something is set up to pull from, or push to that interface, the machine will remain paused until nothing is flowing through the Interface. Once the flow has stopped, it will move on.
To prevent this pause, or interrupt it early, a Redstone signal can be supplied to the fixed position Interface.

quests.title: Rope Pulley
quests.subtitle: It Has It's Ups and Downs
desc: Need a Lift?
Build your own with a Rope Pulley by attaching your own platform.
Use a Gearshift to reverse direction with ease.

quests.title: Adjustable Chain Gearshift
quests.subtitle: Shifting Into Higher Gear
desc: Slightly finer control than messing with gear ratios, an Adjustable Chain Gearshift uses a Redstone signal to set the variable speed, up to twice the input speed.
Consider using an Analogue Lever to easily set a fixed speed.

quests.title: Hose Pulley
quests.subtitle: Well, There's an Upside and a Downside
desc: With a Hose Pulley, fluids may be pumped into or out of the world. Create massive lakes or drain them dry to let your factory grow!

Very large bodies, such as oceans or massive lava lakes in the Nether will be considered Bottomless, so if you wish to drain something like an Ocean Monument, it may still be necessary to build some retaining walls to break things up.
Note, the Hose Pulley does not pump by itself. Lower the hose into the fluid body set up a Mechanical Pump to do the work for you.

quests.title: Gearshift
quests.subtitle: Time to Switch Things Up
desc: Need to reverse direction? Then the Gearshift is what you’re looking for.
Applying a Redstone signal to the block will cause the output side to start spinning in the opposite direction relative to the drive side.

quests.title: Clutch
quests.subtitle: Going to Have to Stop You Right There
desc: Quite the simple device, really. A Clutch disengages power on a shaft line, making for a simple on/off switch.
It could useful for more advanced contraptions that need precise timing, as well.

quests.title: Builder's Tea
quests.subtitle: Hello Brew-TEA-Full!
desc: Stayed out too late par-tea-ing like it's 1773? Need a little more tranquili-tea in your life?
Try some Builder's Tea! It doesn't take too long to prepare.

quests.title: Item Drain
quests.subtitle: Bless the Drains Down in Africa
desc: The Item drain is useful for draining fluids from any fluid-containing items, like buckets or bottles. It's also quite handy for getting fluids out of a Basin.
It has small internal tank, from which fluids can be accessed by pipes.

quests.title: Steam Engine
quests.subtitle: A Newcomen on the Block
desc: With a source of heat, water, and an enclosed space, a Steam Engine can be manufactured to produce enormous amounts of SU.

A basic Boiler setup requires four Fluid Tanks placed in a square and at least one Steam Engine attached. Filling the tanks with water and providing a source of heat below it will get things moving. Click a Shaft against the Steam Engine to get power out of the system

Boilers may be heated passively by any campfire or magma block, however by actively heating them with a Blaze Burner, they reach much higher temperatures and therefore produce more SU. Either way, they’ll need a constant supply of Water, with more used per operation as the number of Engines increases.

quests.title: Trains
quests.subtitle: Watch Your Step
desc: Be it simple Transportation of goods or people, or powering a moving quarry, Trains offer an elegant solution.

Trains are large mobile contraptions that may be automated by way of Train Stations, Train Schedules, and Train Signals. They’ll move through un-loaded chunks, making long-distance transport of materials feasible; only the Station needs to be loaded. Drills and other machines will not function in un-loaded chunks, however.
Building trains begins with the Train Station. Due to the complexity of this feature, watching the Ponder for each of the various pieces of Train equipment is highly recommended.

quests.title: Getting Started: Logistics and Storage
quests.subtitle: From Here to There, Funny Things Were Everywhere
desc: Half the joy of Create is seeing things move, and its logistics options do not disappoint. From Belts that render their contents, to Pipes showing fluids flowing through them, Create offers ways of moving around most anything.

item.name: Compressed Stone Casing / Enchanted Casing / Copper Casing

quests.title: Item Vault
quests.subtitle: Hoarder's Dream
desc: Like the shipping crates they replicate, Item Vaults can hold an enormous number of items per block. They don’t allow manual interaction, however, so items must be inserted or extracted via automation.
Vaults may be combined to form a multi-block storage container. The base must remain square and can be expanded up to 3x3, while the length can be up to 3x the diameter for a maximum size of 3x3x9.
Note, the storage capacity of Vaults has been increased substantially in Enigmatica 9.

quests.title: Eldritch Engine
quests.subtitle: Getting Wired Up
desc: These simple electric motors make an excellent and compact source of SU.

Provide power from any source of FE to get them spun up and set their operating speed on the back. Spinning faster allows them to provide more SU, but at an increasing FE cost. For high SU, low speed applications, be sure to pair them with a Rotation Speed Controller.

quests.title: Straw
quests.subtitle: A Quantum of Solace
desc: Who knew a Blaze could get thirsty? They’re certainly not interested in Water, but other combustible fluids seem to hit the spot just fine.
Giving the Blaze a Straw allows them to accept liquid fuels instead. Check the uses on the Straw or Blaze Burner to see what fuels are valid.

quests.title: Rolling Mill
quests.subtitle: Keep them ingots rollin'
desc: The Rolling Mill is well suited for rolling out some clean rods or extruding wires suitable for electronics use. These may be used manually, or inline with conveyor belts as part of a larger factory.

quests.title: Tesla Coil
quests.subtitle: Assault and Battery
desc: A high-powered electrical device capable of charging objects wirelessly by induced currents, the Tesla Coil can be quite useful in any factory.

When placed above a Belt or Depot and provided sufficient power, the Tesla coil will impart a charge into items on the Belt or Depot. This works not only with crafting recipes, but also for charging equipment like tools and batteries.
The Coil may be deployed for more destructive purposes as well by placing it and providing a Redstone Signal in addition to the power. In this mode, it will damage nearby entities

quests.title: Elevator Pulley
desc: A more advanced form of the Rope Pulley which allows for intelligent floor control as an elevator. The elevator may be called from any floor and can be sent to any floor without stopping between.

quests.title: Mechanical Roller
desc: Placed in front of a rail-based contraption, Mechanical Rollers may be used to flatten terrain or fill gaps below the contraption.
This can be put to great use with a contraption that is designed to lay down track over a great distance.

quests.title: Welcome!
desc: Welcome to Enigmatica 9, we're glad to have you! :D
Quests are divided into two types:
● Discovery
● Learning Mods
You can learn more about each type below.

quests.title: Discovering Enigmatica
desc: The Discovery questline's purpose is to show what's available in the pack.
These chapters are a great place to start if you're new to modded Minecraft or if you're in the need for inspiration.
It currently has the following chapters:
● Adventure
● Building
● Equipment
● Redstone and Logic
● Storage
● Villagers

quests.title: Learning Mods
desc: The Learning Mods chapters are designed to help you get started with large content mods and are broken up into Tech and Magic sections. They will explain roughly how to progress and how to work with the blocks and concepts present in the mod.
These chapters cover a lot of ground, but they don’t cover everything. So, be sure to explore the manuals for those mods that have them.

quests.title: Modded for Dummies
quests.subtitle: Hey, listen!
desc: If you're new to modded Minecraft, it can be a bit daunting to figure out what's what.
That's why we made a book, to sum up the basics and give you a solid baseline to begin your modded journey!

quests.title: Eccentric Tome
quests.subtitle: Don't Panic
desc: A vast repository of knowledge in the palm of your hands. This tome comes pre-populated with the manuals for each mod so they’re always at the ready.
● Right-Click to open the menu and choose a
book. Once chosen, the Eccentric Tome
transforms and becomes that book, for all
intents and purposes.
● Left-Click the air to revert it back to the
Eccentric Tome.
● When transformed, Sneak and press Throw to
remove a given book.
● Craft the Tome with a book to merge them once
more.
Lost your book? Just craft a new one, it’ll come pre-filled with manuals.

quests.title: Witch's Vestments
quests.subtitle: Rags to Witches
desc: The vestments of a Witch go beyond mere mundane protection. Wearing them sends a message to other Witches to stand down while also offering hefty protection against the dark arts.

quests.title: Getting Started: Cauldron Crafting
quests.subtitle: What a Brew-tiful Sight
desc: The Cauldron itself is a time-honored tradition among Witches, used for general cooking, potion making, and more advanced magics alike, it is a versatile tool for any practitioner.

Fluids may be piped in through any form of pipe or delivered by hand with buckets or bottles. Similarly, they may be piped out, though in the case of potions it is likely easiest to remove them manually by Right-Clicking with a bottle.
Items may also be piped in through any sort of automation, as well as dropped in from above.

quests.title: Hexerei
desc: Learn the arts of Witchcraft as you explore what Hexerei has to offer, from cute friends to flying broomsticks, this mod will leave you feeling like a true Witch.

quests.title: Warhammer
quests.subtitle: Payback's a Witch
desc: Sharing a home with trolls will teach a Witch a thing or two, like the value of a heavy object to smash some heads in. Works great for tenderizing steaks too!

quests.title: Drying Rack
quests.subtitle: High and Dry
desc: With a fine selection of herbs in hand, and a small garden prepared, the real magic of Witchcraft may begin.
When it comes to Herbs and cooking, fresh is most certainly best. But sometimes certain properties only manifest once a plant has been dried. Hang a Drying Rack or two around to get started.
