Items may be hung manually with a Right-Click and removed again with a Sneak Right-Click. They may also be inserted via Hopper or other automation and the Drying Rack will conveniently prevent them from being pulled off before the process has finished. Each Rack holds up to nine items at a time.

item.name: Drying Rack / Mahogany Drying Rack / Willow Drying Rack / Witch Hazel Drying Rack

quests.title: Dried Sage Bundle
quests.subtitle: Turning Over a New Leaf
desc: Dried Sage has a number of curative properties, but perhaps more surprising is its ability to ward an area against monster incursions. Perfect for the Witch looking to relax and make a few brews at home without being bothered.

Place Dried Sage on the Plate and light it with a Flint and Steel. The area will be filled with gentle smoke that will prevent mobs from spawning. Right-Clicking the Plate with an empty hand will toggle through its various modes, allowing one to disable the cloud visuals entirely if desired.
Dried Sage may be inserted via Hopper or other automation, and the plate may be lit by a Deployer, allowing the Sage Burning Plate to be fully automated.

quests.title: Candle
quests.subtitle: ... And Now You're Mine
desc: Far beyond simple light sources, a true Witch knows how to infuse Candles with potent magic, causing nearby plants to Grow rapidly, turn the weather from stormy to clear skies, or even imbue nearby monsters with effects such as Poison or Slowness.
Candles have a limited duration and must be periodically replaced. Up to four candles may be placed in a single block space, however, and each one lit individually.
Finally, Candles may be dyed by combining them with dyes in a Crafting Table.

quests.title: Dipper
quests.subtitle: I Put a Spell On You ...
desc: The Dipper is an apparatus that sits atop the Cauldron. With the Cauldron filled with Tallow and up to three String placed in the Dipper, it will set about dipping the string to make Candles all on its own.
String may be fed into the Dipper by way of Hopper or other automation. Some form of filter will need to be used to prevent extracting the string too early, however.
Note: When melting items for Tallow, the Cauldron must have water in it.

quests.title: Witch's Broom
quests.subtitle: Gonna Take My Broom to the Old Swamp Road
desc: Easily the most important tool in any Witch’s arsenal, the Broom allows for both fast and precise flight to avoid critters while out harvesting herbs or to simply get up on that roof to safely fix the smoldering hole left by that lightning bolt.
Some care and maintenance are required when working with Brooms, as their Brushes will not endure forever. Though, they may be enchanted with Unbreaking to help them last a bit longer.
To ride the Broom, Right-Click to place it in the world, then again to hop on. It controls similarly to a boat, though it can change altitude as well.
When not riding it, Sneak Right-Click the Broom to access its menu, where upgrades may be installed, or Brushes swapped out.
At the tip, the Broom may be adorned with simple decorations by hanging them from a Broom Chain, or with more functional Tips that allow the Broom to pass through Lava or Water safely.
Link the Broom to a Broom Whistle to be able to recall the Broom more easily. The Broom must be relatively nearby for this to work.

item.name: Witch Hazel Broom / Mahogany Broom / Willow Broom / Archwood Broom

quests.title: Satchels
quests.subtitle: Gonna Fly Till I Can't No More
desc: Brooms may also be equipped with Satchels that come in various sizes and are the perfect place to store spare parts, potions, or anything one might need for longer excursions.

item.name: Small Satchel / Medium Satchel / Large Satchel

quests.title: Ender Satchel
quests.subtitle: For Better or For Warts
desc: A magical pouch bound to one’s Ender Chest, making it the perfect addition for any forgetful Witches who commonly lose their brooms. At least they won’t lose the contents!

quests.title: Replacer Satchel
quests.subtitle: No Rest for the Wicca'd
desc: No simple storage bag, the Replacer Satchel will automatically swap out Brushes as they wear out, allowing one to fly for longer without interruption.

quests.title: Getting Started: Herb Lore
quests.subtitle: Sage Advice
desc: The wise Witch knows the properties of every plant in their domain, and there are none more knowledgeable than those who call the Swamps their home. Locate a swamp and attempt to forage up some samples for a personal herb garden.

The ancient practice of Dowsing has been used for everything from finding ground water and gems to gravesites and malign spirits. Hexerei’s Dowsing Rod is perfectly attuned to lead the bearer to nearby Swamps and Jungles, with the leaves changing from vibrant green when pointed the correct way, to dull brown when facing away from the target.
A Nature’s Compass is also a viable tool for locating Swamps. And for the less adventurous Witches, a stop at a nearby Market Stall is likely sufficient.

item.name: Sage Seeds / Mandrake Plant / Mugwort Bush / Yellow Dock Bush …

quests.title: Tools and Utility
quests.subtitle: Witch Upon a Star
desc: Dressing for the part is optional, of course, but style should never be overlooked.
Follow along to discover some of the very useful tools in a Witch’s arsenal.

quests.title: Blood Sigil
quests.subtitle: Life's a Witch and Then You Die
desc: Blood is a powerful magical reagent, and a wise Witch is careful of allowing another magic user access to theirs.
To obtain Blood for the purpose of crafting, place a Blood Sigil within the upper left slot of the Cauldron, then hop on in. Each jump will result in a small amount of blood entering the Cauldron.
Of course, nowhere is it stated that the blood must be one’s own. Try dropping a villager in to see what happens. Better still, see if the process can be automated…

quests.title: Crows
quests.subtitle: For the Birds
desc: Witches are often depicted as befriending animals, from cats and mice to snakes and lizards. The Witches of these swamps, however, have a special affinity for the native Crows.

Being a particularly intelligent species of bird, Crows are capable of handling numerous tasks on behalf of their Witch friends. Mix up some of their favorite seeds to offer as a gift to befriend. Either toss the Seed Mixture on the ground nearby or offer the seeds by hand.
Crows are very social critters, and as such will have no issues with having more of their kind around, tame as many as desired!
Once tamed, Sneak Right-Click on them to open a menu where they may be set to a task or equipped with trinkets, hats, or weapons such as a Warhammer!

When commanding a murder of crows, a Crow Flute becomes an indispensable tool. Sneak Right-Click the Flute to access the menu. To begin, click the Select button and then proceed by Right-Clicking each Crow to be commanded by the Flute. Consider crafting a new Flute for every set of Crows to be commanded to prevent mix-ups with commands.
With a Flute, multiple Crows may be selected and commanded to perform their actions, either Harvesting nearby crops, Gathering nearby items, or Pickpocketing nearby Villagers.
Flutes are also the only way to direct a Crow to Perch at a specific location. Perching on a Coffer, for instance, allows a Gathering Crow to automatically deposit its items into the Coffer.
A note on Pickpocketing: Crows have a fixed list of items they’ll choose from any given profession, and the list is not based on the available trades of that villager.

quests.title: Pestle and Mortar
quests.subtitle: Keeping It Grounded
desc: A common sight in apothecaries and kitchens of old, the humble Pestle and Mortar have been used for ages to grind and mix ingredients.
Items may be placed in the Pestle and Mortar by hand via Right-Click, and the finished product may be retrieved similarly.
In addition, items may be piped in via automation and the Pestle and Mortar will hold onto them until finished, only allowing the final product to be extracted.

quests.title: Coffer
quests.subtitle: Do You Be-leaf in Magic?
desc: While it also serves as an easily crafted Shulker Box, the Coffer primarily adds utility to Crows in Harvest mode. Depending on how the Crow button in the GUI is toggled, the Crow will either deposit everything it finds, or only deposit items that already exist in the Coffer, allowing it to act as a filter.
A Coffer may be quickly picked up with a single Left-Click.

quests.title: Witch's Vestments
quests.subtitle: Rags to Witches
desc: The vestments of a Witch go beyond mere mundane protection. Wearing them sends a message to other Witches to stand down while also offering hefty protection against the dark arts.

quests.title: Getting Started: Cauldron Crafting
quests.subtitle: What a Brew-tiful Sight
desc: The Cauldron itself is a time-honored tradition among Witches, used for general cooking, potion making, and more advanced magics alike, it is a versatile tool for any practitioner.

Fluids may be piped in through any form of pipe or delivered by hand with buckets or bottles. Similarly, they may be piped out, though in the case of potions it is likely easiest to remove them manually by Right-Clicking with a bottle.
Items may also be piped in through any sort of automation, as well as dropped in from above.

quests.title: Hexerei
desc: Learn the arts of Witchcraft as you explore what Hexerei has to offer, from cute friends to flying broomsticks, this mod will leave you feeling like a true Witch.

quests.title: Warhammer
quests.subtitle: Payback's a Witch
desc: Sharing a home with trolls will teach a Witch a thing or two, like the value of a heavy object to smash some heads in. Works great for tenderizing steaks too!

quests.title: Drying Rack
quests.subtitle: High and Dry
desc: With a fine selection of herbs in hand, and a small garden prepared, the real magic of Witchcraft may begin.
When it comes to Herbs and cooking, fresh is most certainly best. But sometimes certain properties only manifest once a plant has been dried. Hang a Drying Rack or two around to get started.

Items may be hung manually with a Right-Click and removed again with a Sneak Right-Click. They may also be inserted via Hopper or other automation and the Drying Rack will conveniently prevent them from being pulled off before the process has finished. Each Rack holds up to nine items at a time.

item.name: Drying Rack / Mahogany Drying Rack / Willow Drying Rack / Witch Hazel Drying Rack

quests.title: Dried Sage Bundle
quests.subtitle: Turning Over a New Leaf
desc: Dried Sage has a number of curative properties, but perhaps more surprising is its ability to ward an area against monster incursions. Perfect for the Witch looking to relax and make a few brews at home without being bothered.

Place Dried Sage on the Plate and light it with a Flint and Steel. The area will be filled with gentle smoke that will prevent mobs from spawning. Right-Clicking the Plate with an empty hand will toggle through its various modes, allowing one to disable the cloud visuals entirely if desired.
Dried Sage may be inserted via Hopper or other automation, and the plate may be lit by a Deployer, allowing the Sage Burning Plate to be fully automated.

quests.title: Candle
quests.subtitle: ... And Now You're Mine
desc: Far beyond simple light sources, a true Witch knows how to infuse Candles with potent magic, causing nearby plants to Grow rapidly, turn the weather from stormy to clear skies, or even imbue nearby monsters with effects such as Poison or Slowness.
Candles have a limited duration and must be periodically replaced. Up to four candles may be placed in a single block space, however, and each one lit individually.
Finally, Candles may be dyed by combining them with dyes in a Crafting Table.

quests.title: Dipper
quests.subtitle: I Put a Spell On You ...
desc: The Dipper is an apparatus that sits atop the Cauldron. With the Cauldron filled with Tallow and up to three String placed in the Dipper, it will set about dipping the string to make Candles all on its own.
String may be fed into the Dipper by way of Hopper or other automation. Some form of filter will need to be used to prevent extracting the string too early, however.
Note: When melting items for Tallow, the Cauldron must have water in it.

quests.title: Witch's Broom
quests.subtitle: Gonna Take My Broom to the Old Swamp Road
desc: Easily the most important tool in any Witch’s arsenal, the Broom allows for both fast and precise flight to avoid critters while out harvesting herbs or to simply get up on that roof to safely fix the smoldering hole left by that lightning bolt.
Some care and maintenance are required when working with Brooms, as their Brushes will not endure forever. Though, they may be enchanted with Unbreaking to help them last a bit longer.
To ride the Broom, Right-Click to place it in the world, then again to hop on. It controls similarly to a boat, though it can change altitude as well.
When not riding it, Sneak Right-Click the Broom to access its menu, where upgrades may be installed, or Brushes swapped out.
At the tip, the Broom may be adorned with simple decorations by hanging them from a Broom Chain, or with more functional Tips that allow the Broom to pass through Lava or Water safely.
Link the Broom to a Broom Whistle to be able to recall the Broom more easily. The Broom must be relatively nearby for this to work.

item.name: Witch Hazel Broom / Mahogany Broom / Willow Broom / Archwood Broom

quests.title: Satchels
quests.subtitle: Gonna Fly Till I Can't No More
desc: Brooms may also be equipped with Satchels that come in various sizes and are the perfect place to store spare parts, potions, or anything one might need for longer excursions.

item.name: Small Satchel / Medium Satchel / Large Satchel

quests.title: Ender Satchel
quests.subtitle: For Better or For Warts
desc: A magical pouch bound to one’s Ender Chest, making it the perfect addition for any forgetful Witches who commonly lose their brooms. At least they won’t lose the contents!

quests.title: Replacer Satchel
quests.subtitle: No Rest for the Wicca'd
desc: No simple storage bag, the Replacer Satchel will automatically swap out Brushes as they wear out, allowing one to fly for longer without interruption.

quests.title: Getting Started: Herb Lore
quests.subtitle: Sage Advice
desc: The wise Witch knows the properties of every plant in their domain, and there are none more knowledgeable than those who call the Swamps their home. Locate a swamp and attempt to forage up some samples for a personal herb garden.

The ancient practice of Dowsing has been used for everything from finding ground water and gems to gravesites and malign spirits. Hexerei’s Dowsing Rod is perfectly attuned to lead the bearer to nearby Swamps and Jungles, with the leaves changing from vibrant green when pointed the correct way, to dull brown when facing away from the target.
A Nature’s Compass is also a viable tool for locating Swamps. And for the less adventurous Witches, a stop at a nearby Market Stall is likely sufficient.

item.name: Sage Seeds / Mandrake Plant / Mugwort Bush / Yellow Dock Bush …

quests.title: Tools and Utility
quests.subtitle: Witch Upon a Star
desc: Dressing for the part is optional, of course, but style should never be overlooked.
Follow along to discover some of the very useful tools in a Witch’s arsenal.

quests.title: Blood Sigil
quests.subtitle: Life's a Witch and Then You Die
desc: Blood is a powerful magical reagent, and a wise Witch is careful of allowing another magic user access to theirs.
To obtain Blood for the purpose of crafting, place a Blood Sigil within the upper left slot of the Cauldron, then hop on in. Each jump will result in a small amount of blood entering the Cauldron.
Of course, nowhere is it stated that the blood must be one’s own. Try dropping a villager in to see what happens. Better still, see if the process can be automated…

quests.title: Crows
quests.subtitle: For the Birds
desc: Witches are often depicted as befriending animals, from cats and mice to snakes and lizards. The Witches of these swamps, however, have a special affinity for the native Crows.

Being a particularly intelligent species of bird, Crows are capable of handling numerous tasks on behalf of their Witch friends. Mix up some of their favorite seeds to offer as a gift to befriend. Either toss the Seed Mixture on the ground nearby or offer the seeds by hand.
Crows are very social critters, and as such will have no issues with having more of their kind around, tame as many as desired!
Once tamed, Sneak Right-Click on them to open a menu where they may be set to a task or equipped with trinkets, hats, or weapons such as a Warhammer!

When commanding a murder of crows, a Crow Flute becomes an indispensable tool. Sneak Right-Click the Flute to access the menu. To begin, click the Select button and then proceed by Right-Clicking each Crow to be commanded by the Flute. Consider crafting a new Flute for every set of Crows to be commanded to prevent mix-ups with commands.
With a Flute, multiple Crows may be selected and commanded to perform their actions, either Harvesting nearby crops, Gathering nearby items, or Pickpocketing nearby Villagers.
Flutes are also the only way to direct a Crow to Perch at a specific location. Perching on a Coffer, for instance, allows a Gathering Crow to automatically deposit its items into the Coffer.
A note on Pickpocketing: Crows have a fixed list of items they’ll choose from any given profession, and the list is not based on the available trades of that villager.

quests.title: Pestle and Mortar
quests.subtitle: Keeping It Grounded
desc: A common sight in apothecaries and kitchens of old, the humble Pestle and Mortar have been used for ages to grind and mix ingredients.
Items may be placed in the Pestle and Mortar by hand via Right-Click, and the finished product may be retrieved similarly.
In addition, items may be piped in via automation and the Pestle and Mortar will hold onto them until finished, only allowing the final product to be extracted.

quests.title: Coffer
quests.subtitle: Do You Be-leaf in Magic?
desc: While it also serves as an easily crafted Shulker Box, the Coffer primarily adds utility to Crows in Harvest mode. Depending on how the Crow button in the GUI is toggled, the Crow will either deposit everything it finds, or only deposit items that already exist in the Coffer, allowing it to act as a filter.
A Coffer may be quickly picked up with a single Left-Click.

quests.title: Visit The End
desc: Visit The End

quests.title: Impossible
desc: Just used for hiding existing quests for items in mods that haven't ported yet

quests.title: Immersive Engineering
desc: Immersive Engineering is a versatile tech mod with a focus on large multiblock structures and logistics, all while looking like it came out of a 19th century factory.
The Engineer’s Handbook does a wonderful job of covering things, so be sure to check it out from time to time.

quests.title: Getting Started: Logistics and Storage
desc: Factory building wouldn’t be complete without proper logistics to route items, fluid, and power to the machines that need them. As such, Immersive Engineering offers a robust suite of tools to assist in the effort.
Before delving too deep, however, a few tools need introduction, as they’ll be required going forward.
The trusty Engineer's Hammer is used primarily to form multiblock machines and rotate applicable blocks. They’re also useful for banging out metal plates in a pinch.
Engineer’s Wire Cutters are essential to several crafts but are perhaps most useful for quickly disconnecting live hanging wires safely.
The Engineer’s Screwdriver is handy for making precise changes to Redstone connectors among other things.
All these tools and more can be stored for easy access in an Engineer’s Toolbox.

quests.title: Coke Oven
desc: Critical to the creation of Steel, the Coke Oven is primarily used for processing Coal into Coal Coke and Creosote, two materials that will be used extensively throughout Immersive Engineering.
Items and fluids may be piped in and out automatically.
The Engineer’s Manual shows how this structure is constructed. Right-Click the block highlighted in Red in the manual with an Engineer’s Hammer to form the structure.

quests.title: Windmill
desc: Once used for pumping water or grinding grains, now Windmills harness the breeze to generate electricity instead; putting it to use for far more varied tasks.

Always place the Kinetic Dynamo first, and then the Windmill on the face with the black circle. Windmill Sails may be Right-Clicked onto it to help it catch more wind and thus spin faster. Placing it higher in the air has a similar effect.

quests.title: Basic Wiring
desc: Wires are used to transmit FE and come in three different tiers, each providing different input and output rates, as well as maximum transfer rates. Refer to the Engineer’s Manual for exact rates of each tier.

Connectors are used to set an input or output point and should be placed accordingly. Wires may be Right-Clicked onto them, with a single wire capable of stretching multiple blocks. A single wire may only be stretched so far, however.

Relays may be used to extend the reach of a wire. They won’t transmit power into the block they’re placed on but do allow multiple wire connections. Use them whenever a power line needs to run long distances or to split/combine power lines.
Be mindful around live wires, as they will zap anyone unlucky enough to step into them.
Note: Wires will transmit power through unloaded chunks so long as the start and end points are loaded, making them very useful for long distance power runs.

item.name: LV Wire Coil / MV Wire Coil / HV Wire Coil
LV Wire Connector / MV Wire Connector / HV Wire Connector
LV Wire Relay / MV Wire Relay / HV Wire Relay

quests.title: Insulated Wiring
desc: Note: Wires will transmit power through unloaded chunks so long as the start and end points are loaded, making them very useful for long distance power runs.
Insulating wires prevents them from shocking entities that walk through them, making them ideal for connections close to machines where one might need to move around.
HV Wires may not be insulated, however, and are therefore best used as long-distance power transmission lines, with Transformers being used to bring MV or LV down to a given location.

item.name: Insulated LV Wire Coil / Insulated MV Wire Coil

quests.title: Accumulators
desc: Accumulators act as power storage on a network.
Right-Click a side with an Engineer’s Hammer to toggle between Input (blue), Output (orange), and off.

item.name: LV Accumulator / MV Accumulator / HV Accumulator

quests.title: Engineer's Workbench
desc: Engineers will spend a good deal of time at their workbenches, tinkering with tools and carefully forming delicate parts.
The Engineer’s Workbench provides a space for modifying tools from the mod, and doubles as a crafting bench for items that require an Engineer’s Blueprint.

quests.title: Water Wheel
desc: Though the form of energy they produce has evolved over time, water wheels themselves are quite ancient. Rather than turning a millstone directly, however, these days they’re connected to a Dynamo to produce electrical energy instead.

Always place the Kinetic Dynamo first, and then the Water Wheel on the face with the black circle. Up to three Water Wheels may be chained into the same Dynamo. Once set up, get it spinning by running water over or under the Water Wheels.

quests.title: Conveyor Belt
desc: Getting items from processing to storage need not be a manual effort and Conveyor Belts will handle the task quite adequately.
Much like Rails, Conveyor Belts may slope up or down. They may even be waterlogged if necessary, and Right-Clicking them with a dye will change the color of the wall.
They come in multiple varieties, such as the decorative ‘covered’ belts, but also the more practical:
Dropping Conveyors will insert into inventories below them, or simply drop items on the ground beneath them. They may be disabled with a Redstone signal.
Vertical Conveyors allow for compact vertical movement of items without having to climb up a sloped run of normal Conveyor Belts.
Splitting Conveyors will simply alternate sending each stack they receive to one side or the other. They will not split a stack of items on the belt.

Extracting Conveyors will pull from the attached inventory. They may have their extraction rate adjusted with a Screwdriver and the Extraction point may be adjusted with a Hammer, allowing input from the side of the belt, rather than in line with the flow of the belt. They’re also Redstone sensitive, with a high signal disabling them entirely.

quests.title: Crusher
desc: An all-purpose crushing machine commonly used for processing ores and other bulk items.

Items may be dropped into the open top, where they’ll be absorbed and processed in the order they were received. They may also be piped into the top to avoid dropping items in the world, however briefly.
When complete, it will automatically output items to a belt or inventory in front of the machine.
Beware, the grinding blades can do a lot of damage, easily killing mobs and quickly destroying any items that fall in that don’t have a recipe.

quests.title: Metal Press
desc: A staple of any machine room, the Metal Press may be used to efficiently produce plates, gears, wires, and other stamped products.

Right-Click an appropriate Mold onto the central piston to set up the machine. Molds may be swapped out at any time, though it’s often more convenient to build multiple presses that are each dedicated to a type.
Items are fed into the mill via the built-in conveyor belts and the resulting items will carry on along the belt.

quests.title: Improved Blast Furnace
desc: A powerful furnace that helps maintain the specific heat requirements for smelting Steel.
Both fuel and input items go into the top, while the results come out the front and back. It may be sped up significantly by adding Blast Furnace Preheaters to the sides and powering them.
Outputs will be automatically inserted into adjacent inventories or onto adjacent Conveyor Belts.
Note: The Crude Blast Furnace is disabled for Enigmatica 9.

quests.title: Arc Furnace
desc: Thanks to the intense heat generated within by electricity arcing between electrodes, the Arc Furnace makes short work of alloying and other metalworking tasks. It draws a fair amount of energy to do so, however.

Items are input through the two slots in the top, with each corresponding to one of the two inventories in the GUI. Items are automatically output from the front and rear slots, with slag coming out the rear exclusively.
While the electrodes must be inserted manually, they do tend to last a very long time, and may even be monitored via a Comparator to alert nearby engineers when the electrodes are getting worn out.

quests.title: External Heater
desc: The External Heater is a simple machine that, when powered, will heat adjacent furnaces. This allows the furnaces to smelt more quickly, without using fuel.

quests.title: Thermoelectric Generator
desc: Though the effect is quite small, a heat differential can be harnessed for a reliable source of energy that won’t break down as it relies on no moving parts.

quests.title: Sawmill
desc: A large mill for efficiently processing logs into planks. Without a blade installed, it will only strip bark from logs. However, with a blade installed it will also cut those stripped logs down into planks.

Items are fed into the mill via the built-in conveyor belts and the resulting blocks will carry on along the belt, while any by-products such as sawdust will be inserted into a conveyor or inventory in the front.
Sawblades have limited durability and must be periodically replaced. A new blade may be installed by Right-Clicking it anywhere on the machine.

quests.title: Industrial Squeezer
desc: Large Squeezers such as this have been used widely to extract fluids from materials or to compact dry goods into a more solid form. It’s an invaluable tool for any Engineer.

quests.title: Diesel Generator
desc: Sometimes the best way to get things done is to blow it up.
Well, in a manner of speaking, anyway.
Diesel Generators are notoriously loud, what with all that internal combustion happening, but they’re also reliable, effective, and don’t care too much about what’s burning inside them.
The Diesel Generator accepts all the same fuels as the Thermal Compression Dynamo at roughly the same rates.

It does not always burn clean, however, and it is possible to have an unburnable amount of fuel remaining inside the tank, preventing a different fuel from entering and working. It is therefore recommended to either dedicate the generator to a single fuel or break and re-form the multi-block whenever the fuel changes.

quests.title: Excavator
desc: Once a node has been located, an Excavator should be built atop it. Resources will be scooped up and automatically output out the back of the machine. Be mindful to provide enough storage or some of it may well be lost!
There are a lot of different types of mineral veins, so be sure to check in the Engineer’s Manual under “Overview and Resources” for a full list of Mineral Deposits and where to find them!

quests.title: Mineral Veins
desc: As described in the "Minerals" section of the Engineer’s Manual, massive mineral veins exist below bedrock that are inaccessible without the proper equipment.

The first step towards tapping these veins is locating them with Survey Tools and a Core Sample Drill. Survey Tools will help triangulate the minerals in a large area, while the Core Sample Drill will get an exact read on what’s available.
Use the Survey Tools to find a node and get close to the center, then the Drill to home in on the center where the minerals are at their richest.

quests.title: Garden Cloche
quests.subtitle: Getting Clocher
desc: The Garden Cloche takes power, water, and optionally fertilizer to grow plants at an accelerated rate.

quests.title: Engineered Lighting
desc: They don’t take much energy to run, but they’re well worth the effort. Powered Lanterns will supress mob spawning in an area out to about 32-blocks even though they only light the same area as a normal Lantern. Wires attach directly to them, and they effectively double as Wire Relays.

Floodlights will brighten up a much larger area and may be angled up or down with an Engineer’s Hammer to get them shining on exactly the right spot. Like Powered Lanterns, wires are attached directly to them without the need of a Wire Connector.

quests.title: Workbench Automation
desc: The Automated Workbench is a powered multiblock that may be configured to automatically process a given type of Engineer's Workbench recipe. Handy!
Supply it with the appropriate Blueprint, select the item it should craft, and provide the materials, it’ll take care of the rest.

quests.title: Refinery
desc: Through management of heat and careful exploitation of density differentials, Refineries break down fluids into other useful materials. These Refineries can handle a few different transformations.

quests.title: Assembler
desc: A large crafting machine, the Assembler is capable of sequentially processing up to three recipes. It also boasts three internal fluid tanks that may be drawn from to substitute for filled buckets used in recipes.

quests.title: Mixer
desc: Through vigorous agitation, the Mixer dissolves solids into fluids. Though often used for such mundane tasks as mixing concrete, they’re also quite good at making potions.

quests.title: Bottling Machine
desc: More than simply filling buckets, the Bottling Machine may be used to craft with a number of fluids, such as etching Copper or forming Duroplast.

quests.title: Item Batcher
desc: Item Batcher is an advanced filter block made specifically for use with conveyor belts and creating batches of items for machines.

For example, if one were interested in being as efficient with fuel as possible, an Item Batcher could be configured to only output a single Coal whenever it has eight Raw Beef, thus ensuring that the coal will be fully used in cooking all eight Steaks.
It has applications in crafting as well, to ensure a machine is getting the exact ratio of items it needs to complete a craft. No more, no less.
Attaching a Redstone Interface Connector to a side allows the Batcher to communicate the status of its filters to a Redstone Wire network as well.
Refer to the Engineer’s Manual for more information and other use cases.

quests.title: Item Router
desc: The Item Router is an advanced item sorter made to work with Conveyor Belts.
Items inserted on a side will be output into any inventory or belt on the side matching the filter. If an item doesn't match any filter, it will be redirected to a non-filtered side.
Item Routers support filtering by item type as well as by NBT, Damage, and Tag.

quests.title: Item Silo
desc: Simple bulk item storage. Items are input through the top and extracted through the bottom.
Applying a Redstone signal to the bottom block will allow it to output automatically.

quests.title: Fluid Tank
desc: Simple bulk fluid storage. Fluids are input through the top and extracted through the bottom.
Applying a Redstone signal to the bottom block will allow it to output automatically.

quests.title: Fermenter
desc: Fermentation has been going on in one form or another for millennia. Once upon a time fruits may have been left to ferment naturally over the course of days, now through industrial magic the process takes considerably less time.

quests.title: Fluid Pipe
desc: Simple Fluid Pipes to get fluids moving around the factory. These pipes do not pull from attached inventories on their own. For anything that doesn’t automatically push fluid outputs, a Fluid Pump will be required.

Even for those times when a pump isn’t required, using one greatly increases the flow rate of Fluid Pipes. Power is required and an Engineer’s Hammer will be needed to set sides to Input (blue) or Output (orange). It also requires a Redstone signal to turn on.
The pipes themselves may be covered with Steel or Treated Wood Scaffolding blocks, as well as dyed by Right-Clicking with a dye piece. Dyed pipes will not connect to pipes of another color.

quests.title: Fluid Outlet
desc: When an area needs to be flooded, large or small, a Fluid Outlet makes the perfect tool for the job. Simply place it and pipe fluids into it via any means; it will begin placing that fluid in the area below it, filling from bottom to top.

quests.title: Fluid Router
desc: The Fluid Router is an advanced item sorter made to work with Fluid Pipes.
Fluids inserted on a side will be output into any tank or Fluid Pipe on the side matching the filter. If a fluid doesn't match any filter, it will be redirected to a non-filtered side.

quests.title: Buzzsaw
quests.subtitle: Goes Brrr
desc: A handheld saw perfect for chopping down trees or chopping through zombies.

This tool runs on biodiesel, though the internal tank is on the smaller side. Consider carrying a tank with you for refueling in the field. Simply place it in the input slot of the tank to fill it up.
Place it in an Engineer’s Workbench to add or remove augments.

quests.title: Spellbound Revolver
quests.subtitle: First comes smiles, then lies. Last is gunfire.
desc: A trusty side-arm suitable for any Gunslinger.
Place it in an Engineer’s Workbench to add or remove augments.

quests.title: Mining Drill
quests.subtitle: Workin' in a coal mine. Oops, about to slip down.
desc: A handheld tunnel bore capable of quickly digging through the toughest rocks.

This tool runs on biodiesel, though the internal tank is on the smaller side. Consider carrying a tank with you for refueling in the field. Simply place it in the input slot of the tank to fill it up.
Place it in an Engineer’s Workbench to add or remove augments.

quests.title: Railgun
quests.subtitle: See the TURTLE, ain't he keen?
desc: Capable of launching projectiles at immense velocities and ripping through targets with impunity, the Railgun is a fierce weapon.
Suitable ammunition includes Iron and Steel Rods, as well as Graphite Electrodes and many others.
Place it in an Engineer’s Workbench to add or remove augments.

quests.title: Revolver Speedloader
quests.subtitle: When the shooting starts, we kill what moves.
desc: The Speedloader will automatically reload the Revolver when it runs out of ammo, making it a great way to continue the fight.
To refill it on the go, simply right click and place your cartridges in it. However, it can also be filled in a 3x3 crafting grid by surrounding it with ammo.

It is possible to automate refilling Speed Loaders inside of an Immersive Engineering Assembler. With a little ingenuity, it’s more than possible to automatically pull empty Speedloaders from one’s inventory, fill them, and send them back.

quests.title: Bayonet
quests.subtitle: The man in black fled across the desert...
desc: For those times when the beasts get too close, or the ammo runs dry.

quests.title: Advanced Heatsinks
quests.subtitle: The wheel turns and the world moves on.
desc: Heatsinks allow the Railgun to recharge faster for more rapid-fire destruction.

quests.title: Precision Scope
quests.subtitle: All things serve the beam.
desc: The Middle Mouse button will enable the scope when installed and scrolling will adjust the magnification level. Great for picking off a target at a distance.

quests.title: Accumulator Backpack
quests.subtitle: Pain is a tool, after all. Sometimes it's the best tool.
desc: The Railgun, mighty as it is, holds relatively little energy. A Capacitor Backpack is an excellent way to extend the battery life.
While it can go in a Curios slot, the Capacitor Backpack is perhaps better combined with a chest armor in a crafting grid.

quests.title: Ammo Cartridges
quests.subtitle: ...and the gunslinger followed.
desc: Casull Cartridges are the cheapest, most basic ammo; however, they still pack quite a punch.
Armor-Piercing Cartridges will quickly dispatch a well armored foe and Silver Cartridges are potent against the Undead.

For controlling large crowds, consider something a little more potent, like Buckshot or Dragon’s Breath Cartridges which fire a short-range conical burst. And if your aim is simply terrible, consider the Wolfpack Cartridge, which bursts on impact launching homing shrapnel in all directions, quickly dispatching anything they encounter.
Explore your options and read more in the Engineer’s Manual.

quests.title: Rockcutter Sawblade
quests.subtitle: A Clean Job
desc: An exceptional cutting implement that can cleanly carve out blocks of Stone, Ice, or Glass, effectively acting as a tool with Silk Touch.

quests.title: Pressurized Air Tank
quests.subtitle: Don't Burst It
desc: The Mining Drill’s engine is not normally capable of operating under water. However, with the addition of a Pressurized Air Tank it can be kept running at full speed.

quests.title: Skyseeker's Drill Head
quests.subtitle: Diggy Diggy Hole
desc: Drill heads do wear out over time, though they can be removed from the drill and repaired in an Anvil.
Upgrading to a steel drill head not only increases the durability, but also allows mining Obsidian without wasting your precious shiny blue rocks.
Up to three Additional Augers may be added to a drill, each one speeding up the mining speed and even improving the damage dealt to anything unlucky enough to be standing in front of it.

quests.title: Advanced Lubrication System
desc: Adding some lubricant to a Drill or Saw destined for rugged digging and cutting tough material can greatly extend the lifetime of the tool.

quests.title: Blade Quiver
quests.subtitle: So Wait, Instead of Arrows...
desc: The Blade Quiver may be attached to the Buzzsaw in the Engineer’s Workbench, holds additional blades, and allows you to swap between them on-the-fly in the field. Sneak + Scroll Wheel to change blades.

quests.title: Transformers
desc: Transformers allow stepping down from a higher tier to a lower tier.

For example, one might have a single HV line running through an area where several machines need power. Rather than running dangerous HV lines down directly to each machine, a Transformer could be used to step down to MV, allowing an insulated wire to be run to each machine instead.

quests.title: Lightning Rod
desc: Nothing says “Mad Scientist” like harnessing lightning for energy.

Lightning Rods require a structure of Steel Fences to be built atop them as well, to channel the actual lightning. These structures tend to be large but may be shared by more than one base. Between natural thunderstorms and other means of manipulating the weather, these can generate quite an enormous amount of energy.

Note: For technical reasons, Lightning Rods don’t generate energy when struck by lightning, quite the opposite, in fact. When conditions are right, they’ll simply generate their energy and summon a lightning bolt down as a visual indicator.

quests.title: Getting Started: Material Processing
desc: Bricks, Treated Wood, and Steel; these are what an Immersive Factory is built from, and the focus of early efforts in the mod.

quests.title: Getting Started: Power Generation
desc: Hear that hum? That’s the sound of industry waiting to happen. It’s time to unleash its potential.

quests.title: Tools and Utility
desc: From high-powered lights and excavation tools to revolvers and railguns, Immersive Engineering offers a tool for nearly any job.

quests.title: Large Tank
desc: An extended Fuel Tank that works in the Mining Drill and Buzzsaw. Well worth the cost.

quests.title: Heavy Machinery
desc: With better materials come larger, more capable machines. Prepare to get dirty!

quests.title: Redstone Wiring
desc: Redstone Wiring represents an advancement in Redstone technology, allowing a dedicated Engineer to build complex logic circuits that are less prone to the failings of traditional Redstone Dust. A color-coded channel system also allows a single small network to interact with multiple independent machines.
Redstone Wires may be stretched between Redstone Wire Connectors, Probe Connectors, or Interface Connectors. These carry the Redstone signal without the signal decaying.
Redstone Wire Connectors act as Input and Output points for a signal and may be placed directly on a block. They must have their mode and color channel set by using a Screwdriver on them.

Redstone Probe Connectors act very much like Comparators with a few extra built-in features. Most Immersive Engineering machines will output special comparator signals that may also be read by this Connector. Refer to the Engineer’s Manual for specifics about each machine.
Redstone Interface Connectors are used in conjunction with special blocks like Item Batchers and Logic Units, allowing the signals used by those blocks to be read.

quests.title: Engineer's Circuit Table
desc: Logic Circuits themselves are crafted in the Engineer’s Circuit Table.
This workbench requires power, which is input from the back, as well as some quantity of Circuit Backplanes, Lead Wire, and Vacuum Tubes. Different logic operations will require different quantities.

Circuits are programmed with an operator as well as Input and Output colors. When ready, the completed circuit is withdrawn from the right side of the GUI. Circuits may have their Inputs and Outputs reprogrammed by placing them back in the upper slot, but the operator is locked in upon first creation.

quests.title: Logic Unit
desc: The Logic Unit represents a compact and potentially very complex Redstone Logic computer. Up to ten Logic Circuits must be programmed and placed within and a Redstone Interface Connector attached to the outside.

Whenever the inbound signal changes, the Unit will cycle through each of the installed circuits once, performing each operation, allowing multiple logic gates to be applied to a signal, or even multiple color codes to be used as Input and Output signals.

quests.title: Immersive Engineering
desc: Immersive Engineering is a versatile tech mod with a focus on large multiblock structures and logistics, all while looking like it came out of a 19th century factory.
The Engineer’s Handbook does a wonderful job of covering things, so be sure to check it out from time to time.

quests.title: Getting Started: Logistics and Storage
desc: Factory building wouldn’t be complete without proper logistics to route items, fluid, and power to the machines that need them. As such, Immersive Engineering offers a robust suite of tools to assist in the effort.
Before delving too deep, however, a few tools need introduction, as they’ll be required going forward.
The trusty Engineer's Hammer is used primarily to form multiblock machines and rotate applicable blocks. They’re also useful for banging out metal plates in a pinch.
Engineer’s Wire Cutters are essential to several crafts but are perhaps most useful for quickly disconnecting live hanging wires safely.
The Engineer’s Screwdriver is handy for making precise changes to Redstone connectors among other things.
All these tools and more can be stored for easy access in an Engineer’s Toolbox.

quests.title: Engineer's Workbench
desc: Engineers will spend a good deal of time at their workbenches, tinkering with tools and carefully forming delicate parts.
The Engineer’s Workbench provides a space for modifying tools from the mod.

quests.title: Conveyor Belt
desc: Getting items from processing to storage need not be a manual effort and Conveyor Belts will handle the task quite adequately.
Much like Rails, Conveyor Belts may slope up or down. They may even be waterlogged if necessary, and Right-Clicking them with a dye will change the color of the wall.
They come in multiple varieties, such as the decorative ‘covered’ belts, but also the more practical:
Dropping Conveyors will insert into inventories below them, or simply drop items on the ground beneath them. They may be disabled with a Redstone signal.
Vertical Conveyors allow for compact vertical movement of items without having to climb up a sloped run of normal Conveyor Belts.
Splitting Conveyors will simply alternate sending each stack they receive to one side or the other. They will not split a stack of items on the belt.

Extracting Conveyors will pull from the attached inventory. They may have their extraction rate adjusted with a Screwdriver and the Extraction point may be adjusted with a Hammer, allowing input from the side of the belt, rather than in line with the flow of the belt. They’re also Redstone sensitive, with a high signal disabling them entirely.

quests.title: Crusher
desc: An all-purpose crushing machine commonly used for processing ores and other bulk items.

Items may be dropped into the open top, where they’ll be absorbed and processed in the order they were received. They may also be piped into the top to avoid dropping items in the world, however briefly.
When complete, it will automatically output items to a belt or inventory in front of the machine.
Beware, the grinding blades can do a lot of damage, easily killing mobs and quickly destroying any items that fall in that don’t have a recipe.

quests.title: Metal Press
desc: A staple of any machine room, the Metal Press may be used to efficiently produce plates, gears, wires, and other stamped products.

Right-Click an appropriate Mold onto the central piston to set up the machine. Molds may be swapped out at any time, though it’s often more convenient to build multiple presses that are each dedicated to a type.
Items are fed into the mill via the built-in conveyor belts and the resulting items will carry on along the belt.

quests.title: Improved Blast Furnace
desc: A powerful furnace that helps maintain the specific heat requirements for smelting certain materials.
Both fuel and input items go into the top, while the results come out the front and back. It may be sped up significantly by adding Blast Furnace Preheaters to the sides and powering them.
Outputs will be automatically inserted into adjacent inventories or onto adjacent Conveyor Belts.
Note: The Crude Blast Furnace is disabled for Enigmatica 9.

quests.title: External Heater
desc: The External Heater is a simple machine that, when powered, will heat adjacent furnaces. This allows the furnaces to smelt more quickly, without using fuel.

quests.title: Sawmill
desc: A large mill for efficiently processing logs into planks. Without a blade installed, it will only strip bark from logs. However, with a blade installed it will also cut those stripped logs down into planks.

Items are fed into the mill via the built-in conveyor belts and the resulting blocks will carry on along the belt, while any by-products such as sawdust will be inserted into a conveyor or inventory in the front.

quests.title: Industrial Squeezer
desc: Large Squeezers such as this have been used widely to extract fluids from materials or to compact dry goods into a more solid form. It’s an invaluable tool for any Engineer.

quests.title: Refinery
desc: Through management of heat and careful exploitation of density differentials, Refineries break down fluids into other useful materials. These Refineries can handle a few different transformations.

quests.title: Assembler
desc: A large crafting machine, the Assembler is capable of sequentially processing up to three recipes. It also boasts three internal fluid tanks that may be drawn from to substitute for filled buckets used in recipes.

quests.title: Mixer
desc: Through vigorous agitation, the Mixer dissolves solids into fluids. Though often used for such mundane tasks as mixing concrete, they’re also quite good at making potions.

quests.title: Bottling Machine
desc: More than simply filling buckets, the Bottling Machine may be used to craft with a number of fluids, such as etching Copper or forming Duroplast.

quests.title: Item Batcher
desc: Item Batcher is an advanced filter block made specifically for use with conveyor belts and creating batches of items for machines.

For example, if one were interested in being as efficient with fuel as possible, an Item Batcher could be configured to only output a single Coal whenever it has eight Raw Beef, thus ensuring that the coal will be fully used in cooking all eight Steaks.
It has applications in crafting as well, to ensure a machine is getting the exact ratio of items it needs to complete a craft. No more, no less.
Attaching a Redstone Interface Connector to a side allows the Batcher to communicate the status of its filters to a Redstone Wire network as well.
Refer to the Engineer’s Manual for more information and other use cases.

quests.title: Item Router
desc: The Item Router is an advanced item sorter made to work with Conveyor Belts.
Items inserted on a side will be output into any inventory or belt on the side matching the filter. If an item doesn't match any filter, it will be redirected to a non-filtered side.
Item Routers support filtering by item type as well as by NBT, Damage, and Tag.

quests.title: Item Silo
desc: Simple bulk item storage. Items are input through the top and extracted through the bottom.
Applying a Redstone signal to the bottom block will allow it to output automatically.

quests.title: Fluid Tank
desc: Simple bulk fluid storage. Fluids are input through the top and extracted through the bottom.
Applying a Redstone signal to the bottom block will allow it to output automatically.

quests.title: Fermenter
desc: Fermentation has been going on in one form or another for millennia. Once upon a time fruits may have been left to ferment naturally over the course of days, now through industrial magic the process takes considerably less time.

quests.title: Fluid Pipe
desc: Simple Fluid Pipes to get fluids moving around the factory. These pipes do not pull from attached inventories on their own. For anything that doesn’t automatically push fluid outputs, a Fluid Pump will be required.

Even for those times when a pump isn’t required, using one greatly increases the flow rate of Fluid Pipes. Power is required and an Engineer’s Hammer will be needed to set sides to Input (blue) or Output (orange). It also requires a Redstone signal to turn on.
The pipes themselves may be covered with Steel or Treated Wood Scaffolding blocks, as well as dyed by Right-Clicking with a dye piece. Dyed pipes will not connect to pipes of another color.

quests.title: Fluid Outlet
desc: When an area needs to be flooded, large or small, a Fluid Outlet makes the perfect tool for the job. Simply place it and pipe fluids into it via any means; it will begin placing that fluid in the area below it, filling from bottom to top.

quests.title: Fluid Router
desc: The Fluid Router is an advanced item sorter made to work with Fluid Pipes.
Fluids inserted on a side will be output into any tank or Fluid Pipe on the side matching the filter. If a fluid doesn't match any filter, it will be redirected to a non-filtered side.

quests.title: Buzzsaw
quests.subtitle: Goes Brrr
desc: A handheld saw perfect for chopping down trees or chopping through zombies.

This tool runs on biodiesel, though the internal tank is on the smaller side. Consider carrying a tank with you for refueling in the field. Simply place it in the input slot of the tank to fill it up.
Place it in an Engineer’s Workbench to add or remove augments.

quests.title: Spellbound Revolver
quests.subtitle: First comes smiles, then lies. Last is gunfire.
desc: A trusty side-arm suitable for any Gunslinger.
Place it in an Engineer’s Workbench to add or remove augments.

quests.title: Mining Drill
quests.subtitle: Workin' in a coal mine. Oops, about to slip down.
desc: A handheld tunnel bore capable of quickly digging through the toughest rocks.

This tool runs on biodiesel, though the internal tank is on the smaller side. Consider carrying a tank with you for refueling in the field. Simply place it in the input slot of the tank to fill it up.
Place it in an Engineer’s Workbench to add or remove augments.

quests.title: Railgun
quests.subtitle: See the TURTLE, ain't he keen?
desc: Capable of launching projectiles at immense velocities and ripping through targets with impunity, the Railgun is a fierce weapon.
Suitable ammunition includes Iron and Steel Rods, as well as Graphite Electrodes and many others.
Place it in an Engineer’s Workbench to add or remove augments.

quests.title: Revolver Speedloader
quests.subtitle: When the shooting starts, we kill what moves.
desc: The Speedloader will automatically reload the Revolver when it runs out of ammo, making it a great way to continue the fight.
To refill it on the go, simply right click and place your cartridges in it. However, it can also be filled in a 3x3 crafting grid by surrounding it with ammo.

It is possible to automate refilling Speed Loaders inside of an Immersive Engineering Assembler. With a little ingenuity, it’s more than possible to automatically pull empty Speedloaders from one’s inventory, fill them, and send them back.

quests.title: Bayonet
quests.subtitle: The man in black fled across the desert...
desc: For those times when the beasts get too close, or the ammo runs dry.

quests.title: Advanced Heatsinks
quests.subtitle: The wheel turns and the world moves on.
desc: Heatsinks allow the Railgun to recharge faster for more rapid-fire destruction.

quests.title: Precision Scope
quests.subtitle: All things serve the beam.
desc: The Middle Mouse button will enable the scope when installed and scrolling will adjust the magnification level. Great for picking off a target at a distance.

quests.title: Ammo Cartridges
quests.subtitle: ...and the gunslinger followed.
desc: Casull Cartridges are the cheapest, most basic ammo; however, they still pack quite a punch.
Armor-Piercing Cartridges will quickly dispatch a well armored foe and Silver Cartridges are potent against the Undead.

For controlling large crowds, consider something a little more potent, like Buckshot or Dragon’s Breath Cartridges which fire a short-range conical burst. And if your aim is simply terrible, consider the Wolfpack Cartridge, which bursts on impact launching homing shrapnel in all directions, quickly dispatching anything they encounter.
Explore your options and read more in the Engineer’s Manual.

quests.title: Rockcutter Sawblade
quests.subtitle: A Clean Job
desc: An exceptional cutting implement that can cleanly carve out blocks of Stone, Ice, or Glass, effectively acting as a tool with Silk Touch.

quests.title: Pressurized Air Tank
quests.subtitle: Don't Burst It
desc: The Mining Drill’s engine is not normally capable of operating under water. However, with the addition of a Pressurized Air Tank it can be kept running at full speed.

quests.title: Skyseeker's Drill Head
quests.subtitle: Diggy Diggy Hole
desc: Drill heads do wear out over time, though they can be removed from the drill and repaired in an Anvil.
Upgrading to a steel drill head not only increases the durability, but also allows mining Obsidian without wasting your precious shiny blue rocks.
Up to three Additional Augers may be added to a drill, each one speeding up the mining speed and even improving the damage dealt to anything unlucky enough to be standing in front of it.

quests.subtitle: So Wait, Instead of Arrows...
desc: The Blade Quiver may be attached to the Buzzsaw in the Engineer’s Workbench, holds additional blades, and allows you to swap between them on-the-fly in the field. Sneak + Scroll Wheel to change blades.

desc: From high-powered lights and excavation tools to revolvers and railguns, Immersive Engineering offers a tool for nearly any job.

quests.title: Large Tank
desc: An extended Fuel Tank that works in the Mining Drill and Buzzsaw. Well worth the cost.

quests.title: Heavy Machinery
desc: With better materials come larger, more capable machines. Prepare to get dirty!

item.name: Quasi-Compact Artificing Block / Adept Artificing Block / Novice Artificing Block

This workbench requires power, which is input from the back, as well as some quantity of Runic Proto-Boards, Lead Wire, and Vacuum Tubes. Different logic operations will require different quantities.
Circuits are programmed with an operator as well as Input and Output colors.
