quests.title: Industrial Foregoing
desc: Industrial Foregoing provides a wide range of machines to automate various farming related tasks. From growing plants and breeding animals, to duplicating mobs and drilling for resources.

quests.title: Fluid Extractor
quests.subtitle: A Matter of Time
desc: The Fluid Extractor slowly drains the fluids from blocks placed in front of it, such as logs. Power is optional but will speed up the machine dramatically. This is the primary source of Latex used to make Rubber, a vital resource used throughout the mod.

quests.title: Latex Processing Unit
quests.subtitle: Tacking into the Wind
desc: By providing water, latex, and some energy, the Latex Processing Unit can reduce liquid latex down into Tiny Dry Rubber, which may then be processed further into Plastic.

quests.title: Mob Slaughter Factory
quests.subtitle: Choose Your Pain
desc: The Mob Slaughter Factory kills mobs and animals in its area of effect.
Entities slain in this way do not drop anything but are conveniently converted into Liquid Meat and Pink Slime, liquids with a variety of unique uses.

quests.title: Dissolution Chamber
quests.subtitle: Extreme Measures
desc: Dissolving solids in liquids is certainly a common task, in the home as much as in industry.
The Dissolution Chamber takes this process somewhat further, by dissolving the materials together and then systematically rebuilding something entirely new from the soup.

quests.title: Addons
quests.subtitle: In the Cards
desc: Machine Addons break down into four categories: speed, efficiency, processing, and range.
Speed: Increases the operating speed of the machine
Efficiency: Reduces the energy requirements of the machine
Processing: Allows the machine to perform multiple operations per process
Range: Increases the working area of the machine
Not all machines can accept all addons.

quests.title: Mob Crusher
quests.subtitle: The Butcher's Knife Cares Not for the Lamb's Cry
desc: A machine that rapidly disintegrates creatures in the area, storing their drops and Essence internally.
It will not harm Baby Animals or Players, however, and may optionally consume the Essence it would normally produce to apply Looting to the kill.

quests.title: Enchantment Manipulation
quests.subtitle: Magic to Make the Sanest Man Go Mad
desc: By supplying these machines with energy and Essence, they can assist in automating several Enchanting related tasks.
The Enchantment Factory will randomly enchant Books and equipment.
The Enchantment Applicator will apply Enchanted Books to items without increasing their repair cost.
The Enchantment Extractor will remove a random enchantment from an item, preserving both the item and the enchantment by transferring it to a Book.

quests.title: Material StoneWork Factory
quests.subtitle: Rocks and Shoals
desc: This machine is a one-stop shop for cobblestone processing.
It can generate cobblestone from lava and water, then perform up to four sequential operations, either Smelting, Crushing, 2x2 Crafting, or 3x3 Crafting, to produce a variety of final outputs.
For example, Cobble could be crushed to Gravel, then Sand, and finally smelted into Glass.

quests.title: Bioreactor
quests.subtitle: Ties of Blood and Water
desc: The Bioreactor can process up to nine different types of plant-based items at once to produce Biofuel; the more slots that are filled, the higher the efficiency.
Biofuel can be used to make power with the Biofuel Generator or to run Infinity tools.

quests.title: Infinity Drill
desc: A drill capable of mining out very large areas, perfect for extended mining sessions.
Sneak Right-Click to set its options.
Right-Click on a tank of Biofuel to fill it.

quests.title: Plant Fertilizer
quests.subtitle: Second Chances
desc: By automatically applying Fertilizer or Bone Meal, the Plant Fertilizer drastically speeds up crop growth in its working area.

quests.title: Conveyor Belt
quests.subtitle: Crossover
desc: Conveyor belts move entities atop them whether that’s a mob or an item that has been dropped on it. Several types of upgrades are available such as for extracting or inserting into inventories or teleporting things short distances.
Sneaking while standing on them will prevent the player from being carried along.

quests.title: Mycelial Reactor
quests.subtitle: The War Without, The War Within
desc: Sixteen different Mycelial Generators exist, consuming everything from pink matter and gunpowder, to enchanted items and food. They don’t produce much energy on their own, but when all sixteen are running they’ll trigger a Mycelial Reactor to begin operating as well, generating a whopping 25 million FE/t.

In order to work, the Generators and Reactor must be placed by the same player. Only one set per player will work. The Reactor itself will continue to operate so long as all the Generators are producing power.

quests.title: Infinity Backpack
desc: A backpack with very deep pockets. It’s capable of holding an enormous number of items and has a built-in magnet to pick up items and XP. It can also stock-keep items in the player’s inventory, such as keeping arrows or building blocks stocked from its own storage.
When filled with Liquid Meat, it will automatically feed the player.

quests.title: Infinity Trident
desc: A more powerful trident capable of damaging many mobs wherever it lands. It has built in Loyalty, Riptide, and Channelling enchantments that may be toggled as desired.
Sneak Right-Click to set its options.
Right-Click on a tank of Biofuel to fill it.

quests.title: Infinity Saw
desc: A powerful cutting tool which will rapidly remove logs in the area it is used, starting from the top of the tree it’s used on.
Sneak Right-Click to set its options.
Right-Click on a tank of Biofuel to fill it.

quests.title: Infinity Hammer
quests.subtitle: I'm Still Worthy!
desc: A heavy melee weapon that smashes anything in the area. It comes with a built in Beheading enchantment that may be toggled on and off.
Sneak Right-Click to set its options.
Right-Click on a tank of Biofuel to fill it.

quests.title: Black Hole Units
desc: A block capable of storing big amounts of an item, you can insert or extract items by interacting with the front.

item.name: Common Black Hole Unit / Pity Black Hole Unit / Simple Black Hole Unit / Advanced Black Hole Unit …

quests.title: Black Hole Tanks
desc: A block capable of storing big amounts of a fluid.

item.name: Common Black Hole Tank / Pity Black Hole Tank / Simple Black Hole Tank / Advanced Black Hole Tank …

quests.title: Black Hole Controller
desc: A block that can contain up to sixteen Black Hole Units or Tanks and make their contents accessible to automation.

quests.title: Mechanical Dirt
quests.subtitle: A Blight Upon the Land
desc: By electrifying this questionable substance known as Liquid Meat, Mechanical Dirt can rapidly generate mobs native to the local biome. Light requirements are respected, so mobs won’t spawn on it if the room is too bright.
Energy and Liquid Meat are distributed to all adjacent Mechanical Dirt blocks, allowing a single connection for each to operate a large grid of Mechanical Dirt.

quests.title: Mob Duplicator
quests.subtitle: Dolly 2.0
desc: By energizing Essence in the presence of a captured mob, the Mob Duplicator will begin pumping out clones of that mob ready for culling.
It can only hold one mob at a time, but the Mob Imprisonment Tool can be easily swapped out on-demand with any sort of pipe and a little bit of Redstone logic.

quests.title: Getting Started: Latex Processing
desc: Plastic is a critical resource for many endeavors in Industrial Foregoing. Processing it down from Latex will take some time, however, so setting up some basic automation is going to be helpful in the long run.

quests.title: Getting Started: Mob Processing
desc: For more advanced machinery, fluids such as Liquid Meat, Pink Slime, and Ether Gas will be required. These may be obtained by processing mobs through various methods.

quests.title: Getting Started: Farm Management
desc: Industrial Foregoing comes with a variety of machines to help simplify crop farming.

quests.title: Storage and Logistics
desc: While it focuses more on mob and material processing, Industrial Foregoing also offers a number of tools for storing and moving items and fluids.

quests.title: Tools and Utility
desc: Far from just machines, Industrial Foregoing has a number of utility tools to cover many needs.

quests.title: Transporters
quests.subtitle: The Darkness and the Light
desc: Transporters are small modules that can be used to, well, transport items or fluids between adjacent inventories. Their range is limited, but they can be very fast. And since more than one can go in a single block space, they can be used for easily splitting and sorting machine outputs to other inventories.
Speed Addons will make Transporters operatate more quickly, while Efficiency Addons will allow them to move more per operation.

item.name: Item Transporter / Fluid Transporter / World Transporter

quests.title: Sewer
quests.subtitle: What You Leave Behind
desc: An excellent addition to any passive animal farm, the Sewer will slowly generate liquid Sewage from the animals in its working area.
The Sewer may also gather XP orbs and will convert them directly into Essence.

quests.title: Sewage Composter
quests.subtitle: A Matter of Perspective
desc: A simple device for making that Sewage into something a little more useful: Fertilizer.

quests.title: Plant Gatherer
quests.subtitle: Reaping the Rewards
desc: The Plant Gatherer will rapidly harvest all crops in its working area, extending out in front of the machine. When harvesting, it will remove the entire crop, so coupling it with a Plant Sower is key.
As it harvests crops, it will also produce a small amount of Sludge which will need to be processed.
Providing it with a small amount of Ether Gas will allow it to replant on harvest automatically.

quests.title: Plant Sower
quests.subtitle: Sow Many Plants, Sow Little Time
desc: A handy device for replanting crops in an area. It plants seeds in an area above it, allowing it to be hidden out of sight underground.

Each input slot may be locked to a specific seed type by first placing a seed in the slot, then clicking the lock button. Each slot then corresponds to one of the colored slots on the left of the interface and to the colored dots on the top of the machine. This indicates in which area the seeds will be placed, with a single Sower easily handling up to nine unique crop plots.

quests.title: Hydroponic Bed
desc: Hydroponics have been used to facilitate the growth of a variety of plants since their inception, growing stronger more nutrient rich foods.
The Hydroponic Bed acts as any farmland, allowing most crops to be planted atop it. However, with a bit of power and water, it will speed up the crop growth dramatically.
By providing a small amount of Ether Gas, it will even automatically harvest the crop its growing.

quests.title: Spores Recreator
quests.subtitle: The Red Angel
desc: It’s well known that growing mushrooms can be a tricky affair as maintaining proper growing conditions requires a fair amount of effort.

The Spores Recreator assists by maintaining those conditions internally, providing optimal growing conditions for mushrooms of all types. A small amount of Water is required for normal mushrooms, while some Lava is required for mushrooms native to the Nether.

quests.title: Sludge Refiner
quests.subtitle: The Plot Thickens...
desc: By refining Sludge produced by a Plant Gatherer, a number of blocks may be produced, such as Clay, Sand, and Soul Sand.

quests.title: Advanced Material Processing
desc: It isn’t all just mob mashing… well, maybe it is? Industrial Foregoing offers a… unique take on ore processing, as well as machines to assist with extraction of said ores and other materials.

quests.title: Washing Factory
quests.subtitle: Wrongs Darker Than Death or Night
desc: The meat of mobs is a truly magical substance. Not only can it be electrified to make more mobs, but when sealed up with ores for long enough, can help to soften up the rock, increasing the yields from the ore.
Once Washed in Meat, the resulting concoction is passed through a Fermentation Station and finally a Sieving Machine that helps remove the metals from the rest.

quests.title: Industrial Foregoing
desc: Industrial Foregoing provides a wide range of machines to automate various farming related tasks. From growing plants and breeding animals, to duplicating mobs and drilling for resources.

quests.title: Dissolution Chamber
quests.subtitle: Extreme Measures
desc: Dissolving solids in liquids is certainly a common task, in the home as much as in industry.
The Dissolution Chamber takes this process somewhat further, by dissolving the materials together and then systematically rebuilding something entirely new from the soup.

quests.title: Addons
quests.subtitle: In the Cards
desc: Machine Addons break down into four categories: speed, efficiency, processing, and range.
Speed: Increases the operating speed of the machine
Efficiency: Reduces the energy requirements of the machine
Processing: Allows the machine to perform multiple operations per process
Range: Increases the working area of the machine
Not all machines can accept all addons.

quests.title: Material StoneWork Factory
quests.subtitle: Rocks and Shoals
desc: This machine is a one-stop shop for cobblestone processing.
It can generate cobblestone from lava and water, then perform up to four sequential operations, either Smelting, Crushing, 2x2 Crafting, or 3x3 Crafting, to produce a variety of final outputs.
For example, Cobble could be crushed to Gravel, then Sand, and finally smelted into Glass.

quests.title: Infinity Drill
desc: A drill capable of mining out very large areas, perfect for extended mining sessions.
Sneak Right-Click to set its options.
Right-Click on a tank of Abyssaline to fill it.

quests.title: Plant Fertilizer
quests.subtitle: Second Chances
desc: By automatically applying Fertilizer or Bone Meal, the Plant Fertilizer drastically speeds up crop growth in its working area.

quests.title: Infinity Trident
desc: A more powerful trident capable of damaging many mobs wherever it lands. It has built in Loyalty, Riptide, and Channelling enchantments that may be toggled as desired.
Sneak Right-Click to set its options.
Right-Click on a tank of Abyssaline to fill it.

quests.title: Infinity Hammer
quests.subtitle: I'm Still Worthy!
desc: The perfect tool for clearing vast tracts of land of any form of tree. This saw operates unlike most tools in that it works its way down from the top of the tree.
Sneak Right-Click to set its options.
Right-Click on a tank of Abyssaline to fill it.

quests.title: Mechanical Dirt
quests.subtitle: A Blight Upon the Land
desc: By electrifying this questionable substance known as Liquid Meat, Mechanical Dirt can rapidly generate mobs native to the local biome. Light requirements are respected, so mobs won’t spawn on it if the room is too bright.
Energy and Liquid Meat are distributed to all adjacent Mechanical Dirt blocks, allowing a single connection for each to operate a large grid of Mechanical Dirt.

quests.title: Getting Started: Farm Management
desc: Industrial Foregoing comes with a variety of machines to help simplify crop farming.

quests.title: Tools and Utility
desc: Far from just machines, Industrial Foregoing has a number of utility tools to cover many needs.

quests.title: Transporters
quests.subtitle: The Darkness and the Light
desc: Transporters are small modules that can be used to, well, transport items or fluids between adjacent inventories. Their range is limited, but they can be very fast. And since more than one can go in a single block space, they can be used for easily splitting and sorting machine outputs to other inventories.
Speed Addons will make Transporters operatate more quickly, while Efficiency Addons will allow them to move more per operation.

quests.title: Sewer
quests.subtitle: What You Leave Behind
desc: An excellent addition to any passive animal farm, the Sewer will slowly generate liquid Sewage from the animals in its working area.
The Sewer may also gather XP orbs and will convert them directly into Essence.

quests.title: Sewage Composter
quests.subtitle: A Matter of Perspective
desc: A simple device for making that Sewage into something a little more useful: Fertilizer.

quests.title: Plant Gatherer
quests.subtitle: Reaping the Rewards
desc: The Plant Gatherer will rapidly harvest all crops in its working area, extending out in front of the machine. When harvesting, it will remove the entire crop, so coupling it with a Plant Sower is key.
As it harvests crops, it will also produce a small amount of Sludge which will need to be processed.
Providing it with a small amount of Ether Gas will allow it to replant on harvest automatically.

quests.title: Plant Sower
quests.subtitle: Sow Many Plants, Sow Little Time
desc: A handy device for replanting crops in an area. It plants seeds in an area above it, allowing it to be hidden out of sight underground.

Each input slot may be locked to a specific seed type by first placing a seed in the slot, then clicking the lock button. Each slot then corresponds to one of the colored slots on the left of the interface and to the colored dots on the top of the machine. This indicates in which area the seeds will be placed, with a single Sower easily handling up to nine unique crop plots.

quests.title: Hydroponic Bed
desc: Hydroponics have been used to facilitate the growth of a variety of plants since their inception, growing stronger more nutrient rich foods.
The Hydroponic Bed acts as any farmland, allowing most crops to be planted atop it. However, with a bit of power and water, it will speed up the crop growth dramatically.
By providing a small amount of Ether Gas, it will even automatically harvest the crop its growing.

quests.title: Sludge Refiner
quests.subtitle: The Plot Thickens...
desc: By refining Sludge produced by a Plant Gatherer, a number of blocks may be produced, such as Clay, Sand, and Soul Sand.

quests.title: Infinity Nuke
desc: The ultimate weapon, capable of destroying anything and anyone in a vast area.
You’ve been warned.
Sneak Right-Click to set its options.
Right-Click on a tank of Abyssaline to fill it.
To detonate:
1. Place it somewhere far from
anything important.
2. Right-Click it to arm it. The casing
will close.
3. Light it with a Flint and Steel.
4. Run.

quests.title: Infinity Saw
desc: The perfect tool for clearing vast tracts of land of any form of tree. This saw operates unlike most tools in that it breaks blocks from the top of the tree down towards wherever it is being used. It clears wood and leaves in an area centered on where it is used, whether those trees are connected to the one being sawed or not.
Sneak Right-Click to set its options.
Right-Click on a tank of Abyssaline to fill it.

quests.title: Mekanism
desc: A Sci-Fi themed technology mod with an emphasis on the extreme, Mekanism focuses on creating efficiencies, whether in the form of increased output from ores to advanced fusion reactors to power your base.

Its systems do aim towards a certain amount of realism with certain concessions along the way for better game play. Within the context of the mod, the player will need to master power generation, manage heat and radiation, all while seeking the most efficient path.
Beyond these quests, there is no in game guide to Mekanism. However a very thorough official wiki can be found here:
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com"}}

quests.title: Getting Started: Material Processing
desc: As noted, Mekanism maintains a strong focus on efficiencies throughout the mod. As machines are upgraded and more systems put in place, they become more efficient, more productive, and cheaper to run.
Focusing on being efficient from the very start will ultimately pay off in the long run.

quests.title: Advanced Power Generation
desc: That little Gas-Burning Generator is probably doing OK up to this point. One could be excused for thinking it's enough.
Certain high-tier crafts will require substances currently out of our reach, and obtaining them is going to require extreme amounts of energy.

quests.title: Heat Generator
quests.subtitle: Argent Crucible
desc: The Heat Generator is a multi-function device that will be useful early on as a source of power.

To begin, surround the Heat Generator with lava, flowing or otherwise. The block itself may also be 'lava-logged' just as you'd water-log stairs or slabs. The more faces that are in contact with lava, the faster it produces energy.

Solid fuel may also be fed into the device, where it is converted to lava and 'burned' for energy. Combining both the passive and active generation methods will produce more power than either method on its own.

quests.title: Wind Generator
quests.subtitle: 100% Cancer-Free
desc: Lava has a tendency to set things on fire, which some would deem undesirable. As a step up from the Heat Generator, there's the Wind Generator.
Even at sea-level this will out-produce the heat generator's passive mode, however placing it higher in the world allows it to generate even more.

quests.title: Gas-Burning Generator
quests.subtitle: Frightening Efficiency
desc: The Gas-Burning Generator primarily burns Ethylene to produce energy, however it can also be used to burn excess Hydrogen. Hydrogen itself produces no net gain in power, instead serving as a useful energy storage medium.

quests.title: Induction Matrix
quests.subtitle: There Is No Spoon
desc: For times when more extensive energy storage is required, the Induction Matrix is the answer.
This modular multiblock structure can hold truly astonishing amounts of energy at its largest size of 18x18x18. Even a small one, however, will outperform an equivalent number of Energy Cubes.

The structure must be a rectangular prism with walls built of Induction Casing or Structural Glass. Induction Providers and Cells can be placed in any configuration desired. Empty spaces are fine, and different tiers may be mixed.
Providers only affect the I/O speed. Typically, not many are required. Cells, on the other hand, provide the storage capacity of the Matrix, and will typically make up the bulk of the insides.
At least two Induction Ports will be required to make full use of the Matrix, one configured for Input and the other for Output. Sneak + Right-Click with a Configurator to change the mode.
It’s worth noting that the current fill level of an Induction Matrix may be read with a Comparator on an Induction Port; very useful for turning power production down or off when it is nearly full.
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki: Induction Matrix","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com/wiki/Induction_Matrix"}}

item.name: Basic Induction Cell / Advanced Induction Cell / Elite Induction Cell / Ultimate Induction Cell
Basic Induction Provider / Advanced Induction Provider / Elite Induction Provider / Ultimate Induction Provider

quests.title: Getting Started: Power Generation
desc: It is possible to bootstrap power production by feeding Redstone dust directly into the power slot in Mekanism machines.
This would be wasteful and inefficient, however. There are far more efficient ways to proceed.

quests.title: Metallurgic Infuser
quests.subtitle: Advanced Metallurgy
desc: Once some basic power infrastructure is settled, the next most important machine will be the Metallurgic Infuser.

Take notice of the color coding in Mekanism GUIs, as they’ll indicate where materials go. The Yellow box on the left is where the infusion matter goes. It’ll be absorbed into an internal buffer and then consumed during the actual craft.

These colors also correspond to the colors in the Side Config panel. By default, this machine expects the infusion material to be inserted from the bottom of the machine. That’s all configurable, however, so set them however they’re most convenient.

Automation Note: Since the two required input materials use two different channels, red and yellow, there’s no way to feed both items in from the same face. As a result, it’s often easiest to make multiple machines, each dedicated to their own infusion material.

item.name: Metallurgic Infuser / Basic Infusing Factory / Advanced Infusing Factory / Elite Infusing Factory …

quests.title: Enrichment Chamber
quests.subtitle: Put One In The Chamber
desc: Alloys will be needed commonly for more advanced machinery. They can be quite costly to make, however, as infusion materials don’t go very far.
They can be stretched quite a bit further by enriching them in an Enrichment Chamber, however.
For example, a single Redstone will make a single Infused Alloy, however a single Enriched Redstone will make eight Alloys. It is therefore well worth the effort to enrich these items.

item.name: Enrichment Chamber / Basic Enriching Factory / Advanced Enriching Factory / Elite Enriching Factory …

quests.title: Crusher
quests.subtitle: Follow Me, Don't Follow Me
desc: Smashing things is an age-old method of getting one thing out of another. We’re well beyond the days of just smashing things with a rock, but the results are similar.
A variety of crushed materials are used throughout Mekanism, so a Crusher will be invaluable moving forward.

item.name: Crusher / Basic Crushing Factory / Advanced Crushing Factory / Elite Crushing Factory …

quests.title: Pressurized Reaction Chamber
quests.subtitle: Pushing Down On Me, Pressing Down On You
desc: Certain chemical reactions only occur at greater pressures and the PRC can be used to facilitate them.

quests.title: Osmium Compressor
quests.subtitle: Organic Blend
desc: Obsidian and Glowstone by themselves are brittle materials, despite their interesting properties. By refining them and bonding them with a substrate such as Osmium, they create alloys that are easier to work with while maintaining their unique nature.

item.name: Osmium Compressor / Basic Compressing Factory / Advanced Compressing Factory / Elite Compressing Factory …

quests.title: Thermal Evaporation Plant
quests.subtitle: Reduce By Half, Simmer Gently
desc: Before getting too deep into nuclear physics, a little ground-work will be needed. The Thermal Evaporation Plant will feature heavily in the coming processes so understanding it is going to be vital.

Gather the requested materials and build a Thermal Evaporation Plant. The structure will have a 4x4 base in a rectangular prism shape. The sides may also be made of Structural Glass and it can be extended vertically up to 18 blocks tall.

The Evaporation Plant functions with heat, which can be provided through a variety of means. The easiest will be to hook a Resistive Heater up to one of the Valves and give it power. Note that the amount of power used by the Resistive Heater can be set in the GUI. Experiment to find the right balance of power.
Water or other fluids may then be piped in to one of the other Valves. As the Water heats, it will be converted to Brine which may then be piped out of the third Valve.
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki: Thermal Evaporation Plant","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com/wiki/Thermal_Evaporation_Plant"}}

quests.title: Electrolytic Separator
quests.subtitle: Keep 'Em Separated
desc: Electrolysis is most commonly used to separate Water into its component parts of Hydrogen and Oxygen, though it does find itself in use in many other industrial processes.

Note that while Energy and Speed upgrades have no impact on the amount of Hydrogen that’s produced for a given amount of FE, they do still speed up the machine and both are required to run this machine at its fastest.

quests.title: Fuel Rod Assembly
quests.subtitle: Nuclear Launch Detected
desc: The Fuel Rod Assembly is what actually holds the fissile material during the reaction. Having more allows the reactor to burn fuel faster.
One assembly consists of a Control Rod Assembly at the top of a column of Fuel Assemblies. Assemblies must not touch, so arranging them in a checkerboard is ideal.

The materials gathered up to this point are enough to build a 5x5x9 reactor with glass top and sides, which is quite a respectable starting reactor. Use the Configurator to set the Reactor Ports appropriately.
Tip: Place an Input Valve near the top of the structure, in line with the vents for the turbine, to allow for simpler routing of Mechanical Pipes.
Similarly, the Coolant Output is best placed lower in the structure, again in line with the Turbine's Input Valve, to simplify routing of Pressurized Tubes.
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki: Fission Reactor","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com/wiki/Fission_Reactor"}}

quests.title: Fission Reactor Casing
quests.subtitle: Limiting Exposure
desc: The first step in actually constructing a fission reactor is building a safe place to put it. Something that keeps all that radiation at bay.

The Fission reactor itself can be quite large, up to 18x18x18 if one so desires. Though it is wise to keep the entire structure contained within a single chunk. There's no sense starting off that large, however, so we'll focus on something a little more reasonable with a 5x5 base and 9 blocks tall.
The Configurator may be used to toggle the ports between "Input Only", "Output Waste", and "Output Coolant". Be sure to set these accordingly.
Note: F3 + G will show the chunk boundaries. Try to plan out your reactor accordingly.

quests.title: Safety Precautions
quests.subtitle: Getting Out In Front
desc: History has shown us time and time again that a Safety-First approach is the only sane way to work with something as dangerous as nuclear physics. Three Mile Island may have been a disaster, but the fact that nobody died is a testament to the importance of safety protocols.
With that said, it's worth the effort to build some safety systems into a Mekanism fission reactor as well. The wiki has an excellent entry on circuit breakers here:

{"text":"Mekanism Wiki: Circuit Breaker","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com/wiki/Fission_Reactor#:~:text=for%20sodium%20cooling.-,Circuit%20Breaker,-Every%20reactor%20should"}}

The reactor may go super-critical and explode if it overheats, the leading cause of which is that it has run out of coolant. Therefore, the circuit breaker should trigger on High Temperature. It may also be prudent to build a second circuit breaker for Excess Waste to prevent venting radiation into the surrounding environment.

quests.title: Radioactive Waste Barrel
quests.subtitle: HLW Disposal
desc: Burning Fissile Fuel naturally creates waste. Proper handling and storage of this waste is critical. Waste may only be transported via Mekanism's Pressurized Tubes and can only be stored in Radioactive Waste Barrels, or machines that accept waste for reprocessing.
Furthermore, breaking or picking up any machine or Waste Barrel containing waste will automatically dump the radiation into the environment, so some care must be taken to avoid incidents.
Lastly, waste stored in such barrels will slowly and safely dissipate. So if the intent is to process it further, the safest course of action is to simply pipe it straight into machines.

quests.title: Supercritical Phase Shifter
quests.subtitle: I've Giv'n Her All We've Got, Captain
desc: You had a stockpile of Uranium, right? Yeah. You're going to need a lot to build this structure, which is used for generating Antimatter from Nuclear Waste.
Two ports with Supercharged Coils will accept power input. The other two ports will be used for inputting waste and outputting antimatter.
Adding more Ports with Supercharged Ports attached to them will allow the machine to run faster, assuming of course that sufficient power and waste can be supplied.
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki: Supercritical Phase Shifter","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com/wiki/Supercritical_Phase_Shifter"}}

quests.title: Fusion Reactor
quests.subtitle: Star in a Box
desc: Fusion, the power of the stars, without which no heavier elements would exist.

The Mekanism Wiki will assist in building the odd shape of this structure, however building the fuel supply chain is up to you. Be sure to use Reactor glass on all sides to dramatically reduce the cost of building this structure.

There are a few important things to keep in mind with a Fusion Reactor. First and foremost, this is a safe energy supply that, unlike a Fission Reactor, will never melt down or cause any adverse effects.
● When fueling the Reactor, pipe in Deuterium and Tritium separately.

● The Reactor generates very little FE directly. To get the most out of it, run water through to convert to steam. Then run the steam through an Industrial Turbine. Like the Fission Reactor, keeping up with the water requirements will likely require recycling the Steam back to Water in the Turbine.
● Piping in D-T Fuel in addition to the direct Deuterium and Tritium feeds will drastically increase the heat of the reactor, causing it to generate steam far more quickly.
● Connecting the Fusion Reactor to a Thermoelectric Boiler is another great way of boosting the total steam production, and therefore power production.
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki: Fusion Reactor","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com/wiki/Fusion_Reactor"}}

quests.title: Industrial Turbine
quests.subtitle: Bursting at the Seams
desc: The Fission Reactor doesn't produce useful energy on its own. Rather, the steam it generates must be run through an Industrial Turbine in order to generate FE. The Turbine is also critical for recycling steam into water to return to the Fission Reactor for cooling. Without this reprocessing loop, it is exceptionally difficult to provide enough coolant to keep the Reactor running.

The Turbine itself is a complex multiblock with various rules governing where and how the parts go together. Refer to the Wiki for help in building the turbine. The materials gathered so far are enough to build a 5x5x9 Turbine with glass sides.

The Reactor will automatically output Steam from a Coolant Output Port. The steam must be passed into one of the Turbine Ports via Pressurized Tube and Water then automatically outputs from any of the Vents at the top of the structure and can be passed back to an input port on the Reactor.
Power can than be extracted from another Turbine Port.

WARNING: If the Turbine's power buffer fills up it will stop running, steam and water flow will halt, and the attached Reactor's heat will rapidly rise to dangerous levels resulting in a potential meltdown situation.
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki: Industrial Turbine","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com/wiki/Industrial_Turbine"}}

quests.title: Aetheric Transmutation Chamber
quests.subtitle: Indistinguishable from Magic
desc: Alchemists of yore were correct in believing that elemental substances could be transmuted.
What they failed to understand was the vast amount of energy that would be required to do so.

quests.title: QIO Drive Array
quests.subtitle: Bigger on the Inside
desc: QIO Storage is an extra-dimensional, high-capacity storage medium. The system allows for remote access through a handheld terminal as well as wireless import, export, and Redstone Capabilities.
It’s also fully compatible with Applied Energistics 2. Simply place a configured QIO Dashboard on an ME Storage Bus to grant AE2 full access to the entire contents of the QIO system.

item.name: QIO Drive / Hyper-Dense QIO Drive / Time-Dilating QIO Drive / Supermassive QIO Drive

quests.title: QIO Dashboard
quests.subtitle: Remote Viewing
desc: Dashboards may be placed anywhere and allow for manual insertion into and extraction from the network.
As previously mentioned, they can also be used to grant AE2 access to a QIO Network via an attached ME Storage Bus.

quests.title: QIO Importing and Exporting
quests.subtitle: Garbage In, Garbage Out
desc: Storing items in a QIO Drive Array would be rather daft if there were no way of getting things in or out automatically.
The QIO Importers and Exporters facilitate this, allowing the system to work as a wireless item transfer and storage system.
The Redstone Adapter simply outputs a signal when a certain threshold of an item has been reached within the QIO drive space, allowing a simple way of disabling machinery that no longer needs to run.

quests.title: Laser Amplification
quests.subtitle: This One Goes to Eleven
desc: In order to actually kickstart a Fusion Reactor, a highly focused and energetic burst of energy is required.
Laser Amplifiers will collect up to five laser beams and combine them into a single powerful beam. Amplifiers may also be chained together, with one amplifier feeding into another.

The final amplifier in the chain should be pointed at the Laser Focus Matrix in the Fusion Reactor and should be set to be Redstone Pulse mode. Once it has accumulated enough energy, providing a redstone pulse will release it all in an instant.
A filled Hohlraum must be present in the Fusion Reactor as well.

quests.title: Don't Panic
quests.subtitle: There's a Frood Who Really Knows Where His Towel Is
desc: Accidents happen.
Grab a fish and complete this quest in the case that you've irreversibly irradiated your entire base.
Redeemable once only.

quests.title: Thermoelectric Boiler
quests.subtitle: It's Gettin' Hot In Here
desc: Water Cooling is a great place to start, but it has its limits. Sodium may be used instead to dissipate even more heat, allowing the reactor to run at higher burn rates.
In order to make use of Sodium, however, a new multiblock is required: The Thermoelectric Boiler.
● Sodium is heated to Superheated Sodium in the Fission Reactor.
● Superheated Sodium is passed into the Boiler where it heats water to steam.
● The Boiler outputs cooled Sodium, which is recycled through the Fission Reactor.
● The Steam is passed through the turbine, producing FE and water which is recycled through the Boiler.

The Boiler itself may be nearly any size, up to 18x18x18, however a small one is very capable of dissipating a lot of heat. The quest requires materials for a 5x9x5 boiler. When scaling up, it’s more likely that the Turbine will need to be expanded than the Boiler.
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki: Thermoelectric Boiler","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com/wiki/Thermoelectric_Boiler"}}

quests.title: Gauge Dropper
quests.subtitle: Better Than a Stick in the Eye
desc: It’s bound to happen. With pipes and cables running everywhere, who knows what’s going to get into that machine when it’s plonked down. Water? Hydrogen? And once things are in, often times it’s not clear how to get them out.

This is where the Gauge Dropper comes in. This small tool will help extract unwanted inputs from various machines. Clicking on an input inside the GUI of a machine with the Dropper will extract a small amount of the input, allowing it to be easily transported to another machine. Sneak + Left-Click will instead void the material.
Similarly, Sneak + Right-Clicking the air with the gauge dropper will void whatever is currently stored.

quests.title: Tier Installers
quests.subtitle: Yo Dawg, Heard You Liked Machines...
desc: There are limits to the number of speed upgrades that can go in machines. After that, expanding sideways is the only option to speeding things up. Thankfully, Tier Installers make this somewhat easier than simply tossing down nine more machines full of upgrades. Remember, it’s all about being efficient!

Each Tier Installer will add a number of input and output slots to the machine, allowing it to run that many items in parallel. Each slot shares the other Upgrades in the machine, reducing the number of Upgrades that would need to be crafted.
To apply a Tier Installer, simply Sneak + Right-Click on a machine place in-world. Tiers must be installed in order, no skipping tiers!

item.name: Basic Tier Installer / Advanced Tier Installer / Elite Tier Installer / Ultimate Tier Installer

quests.title: Precision Sawmill
quests.subtitle: Your Arm's Off!
desc: Making planks with hand tools is so last century, and incredibly wasteful. Obtain more for the effort and recover some of the loss by finding uses for the leftover saw dust.

item.name: Precision Sawmill / Basic Sawing Factory / Advanced Sawing Factory / Elite Sawing Factory …

quests.title: Teleporter
quests.subtitle: Guests are reminded that Platform One forbids the use of weapons, teleportation, and religion.
desc: Got somewhere to be and no time to get there? Well, start walking. And next time, bring a teleporter to set up when you get there to avoid going the long way again.
Teleporter Frames are Optional.

quests.title: Getting Started: Logistics and Storage
desc: Mekanism deals in Energy, Fluid, Gas, Item, and Heat transfer, and has a matching pipe to assist in the transfer of each.
Configuring them is done with the Configurator, which itself has several modes. Use Sneak + Scroll Wheel to change the current mode.
When in Wrench mode, a Sneak + Right Click will immediately pick up any Mekanism machine or pipe.
When in any of the ‘Configurate’ modes, the Configurator will toggle different aspects of the pipe. See the following sections for more information.

quests.title: Diversion Transporter
desc: While Logistical Transporters themselves may not be configured to be Redstone sensitive, that doesn’t mean the option is completely gone. Replace a section of pipe with a Diversion Transporter, which allows each face to be individually configured for Redstone control.

quests.title: Logistical Sorter
desc: A Logistical Transporter can be set to pull from any inventory, but this will effectively route items in a Nearest-First order. To get a little fancier, the Logistical Sorter may be used.
Sorters are placed against any inventory and mark the extraction point for items. They cannot be used in the middle or at the end of a section of pipes.

The Sorter must first be configured with one or more filters. For example, click ‘New Filter’, then ‘ItemStack’. On the left there will be two boxes. The one on top can have an item dragged in. Clicking the one on the bottom will set a color channel. These colors match the colors available when configuring Logistical Transporters, and indeed will tell the items where to go.

Continuing with the example, assume a blue filter is set for Stone and a green filter is set for Granite. As the Sorter pulls either Stone or Granite, those items will be framed in blue or green, respectively. As they travel through the pipe, if they have the option of going down a blue or green section of pipe, they will prefer to do so.

Conveniently, this same system is used by other Mekanism Machines. Each has a Transporter Config where a color can be assigned to a side for routing inputs, and a color can be set for all outputs leaving the machine. So, a Smelting Factory might be assigned yellow to receive Cobblestone, and assign blue to its outputs, routing the resulting Stone to the blue line from the previous example.
The system is far more complicated than can truly be covered here, but with a little patience it isn’t difficult to figure out.

quests.title: Quantum Entangloporter
desc: It isn’t always convenient to lay out pipes for hundreds of blocks, especially since the rules of Minecraft dictate that all those blocks would need to be loaded to transport items.

For convenience’s sake, many mods offer some form of long-range wireless transport. For Mekanism, this takes the form of the Quantum Entangloporter. This block can transport all the same things as the various pipes, the exception being radioactive materials.
Each Entangloporter must be bound to a channel, which may be created within the block itself. Place one in each location, choose a channel, then pipe in and out as desired.
Entangloporters have no range limitations and work across dimensions. They can be given an Anchor upgrade as well to force load the chunk they are in.

quests.title: Energized Smelter
desc: A high-temperature furnace that’ll get things cooked up in no time at all.

item.name: Energized Smelter / Basic Smelting Factory / Advanced Smelting Factory / Elite Smelting Factory …

quests.title: Purification Chamber
desc: Advanced machinery that uses Oxygen to purify materials, the Purification Chamber is frequently used in parts of larger processing chains.
Be sure to install Gas Upgrades in these machines to reduce their overall Oxygen use, or it may be difficult to keep up with demands.

item.name: Purification Chamber / Basic Purifying Factory / Advanced Purifying Factory / Elite Purifying Factory …

quests.title: Chemical Injection Chamber
desc: By placing objects under great pressure, they may be infused with other materials.

The Chemical Injection Chamber, while often found as a step in larger processing chains, is also a very handy tool for automating more tedious tasks, such as setting concrete or getting those Copper Stairs to just the right level of oxidation before using them in a roof.
Remember to install Gas Upgrades to make the gas inputs more efficient!

item.name: Chemical Injection Chamber / Basic Injecting Factory / Advanced Injecting Factory / Elite Injecting Factory …

quests.title: Combiner
desc: Unsurprisingly, smashing things together to make new things is also an age-old tradition. The Combiner may be used to simplify obtaining a number of decorative blocks.

item.name: Combiner / Basic Combining Factory / Advanced Combining Factory / Elite Combining Factory …

quests.title: MekaSuit Helmet
quests.subtitle: The Only Thing They Fear... Is You.
desc: All pieces may be upgraded to enhance the energy shield and add radiation shielding.
Other Notable Upgrades:
Helmet
● Auto Feeding
● Night Vision
● Solar Charging
● Underwater Breathing
● Magic Damage Protection
● Status Effect Protection
Bodyarmor
● Creative Flight
● Elytra Flight
● Radiation Tracking
● Energy Distribution
Pants
● Run Speed Enhancement
Boots
● Jump Height Enhancement
● Magnet Upgrade

quests.title: Energy Cubes
desc: Energy Cubes act as basic energy storage and may be placed in line with power cables to provide a larger buffer for peak usage.
All Mekanism machines will also accept them in their energy slot to power a machine off grid.
Finally, Energy Cubes themselves have slots for the purpose of charging most energy using items, or even discharging other batteries.

item.name: Basic Energy Cube / Advanced Energy Cube / Elite Energy Cube / Ultimate Energy Cube

quests.title: Heat Pipes
desc: Logistics Pipes work differently than other pipes as they cannot be made Redstone Sensitive. A Sneak + Right Click with a Configurator in a ‘Configurate’ mode will instead toggle the color filter of a section of pipes, which assists in filtering where items are sent by Mekanism machines.
All these pipes may be upgraded in-world by Right-Clicking them with the appropriate tier of Alloy. This will upgrade the nearest 8 pipe segments on the same network.
Clicking repeatedly in the same spot is a good way to get a long network fully upgraded without needing to tear everything up and re-configure the pipes.

item.name: Basic Thermodynamic Conductor / Advanced Thermodynamic Conductor / Elite Thermodynamic Conductor / Ultimate Thermodynamic Conductor

quests.title: Item Pipes
desc: Logistics Pipes work differently than other pipes as they cannot be made Redstone Sensitive. A Sneak + Right Click with a Configurator in a ‘Configurate’ mode will instead toggle the color filter of a section of pipes, which assists in filtering where items are sent by Mekanism machines.
All these pipes may be upgraded in-world by Right-Clicking them with the appropriate tier of Alloy. This will upgrade the nearest 8 pipe segments on the same network.
Clicking repeatedly in the same spot is a good way to get a long network fully upgraded without needing to tear everything up and re-configure the pipes.

item.name: Basic Logistical Transporter / Advanced Logistical Transporter / Elite Logistical Transporter / Ultimate Logistical Transporter

item.name: Basic Pressurized Tube / Advanced Pressurized Tube / Elite Pressurized Tube / Ultimate Pressurized Tube

quests.title: Fluid Pipes
desc: With a Configurator in any of the ‘Configurate’ modes, a Right-Click on a section of pipe will toggle Redstone Sensitivity, allowing the pipe to be disabled with a Redstone signal, while a Sneak + Right-Click will toggle the pipe’s mode, either Push, Pull, or None (disabled).
All these pipes may be upgraded in-world by Right-Clicking them with the appropriate tier of Alloy. This will upgrade the nearest 8 pipe segments on the same network.
Clicking repeatedly in the same spot is a good way to get a long network fully upgraded without needing to tear everything up and re-configure the pipes.

Note: Each pipe tier has a limited Pump Rate when set to Pull. However, if left unconfigured, they’ll allow much greater volumes to be pushed into them. The throughput of a section of pipes is calculated as Capacity * number of pipe segments.

item.name: Basic Mechanical Pipe / Advanced Mechanical Pipe / Elite Mechanical Pipe / Ultimate Mechanical Pipe

quests.title: Energy Pipes
desc: Logistics Pipes work differently than other pipes as they cannot be made Redstone Sensitive. A Sneak + Right Click with a Configurator in a ‘Configurate’ mode will instead toggle the color filter of a section of pipes, which assists in filtering where items are sent by Mekanism machines.
All these pipes may be upgraded in-world by Right-Clicking them with the appropriate tier of Alloy. This will upgrade the nearest 8 pipe segments on the same network.
Clicking repeatedly in the same spot is a good way to get a long network fully upgraded without needing to tear everything up and re-configure the pipes.

item.name: Basic Universal Cable / Advanced Universal Cable / Elite Universal Cable / Ultimate Universal Cable

quests.title: Chemical Tanks
desc: Basic Chemical storage, these will hold any non-radioactive gas, slurry, infusion type, or pigment.
They can be directly inserted into machines to provide their materials or be configured to auto output to adjacent machines.
They’ll also function as an over-flow trash by setting them to “Dump Excess”.

item.name: Basic Chemical Tank / Advanced Chemical Tank / Elite Chemical Tank / Ultimate Chemical Tank

quests.title: Fluid Tanks
desc: Basic Fluid storage, these can auto-output to the bottom by Sneak + Right-Clicking the bottom face with a Configurator.

item.name: Basic Fluid Tank / Advanced Fluid Tank / Elite Fluid Tank / Ultimate Fluid Tank

quests.title: Formulaic Assemblicator
desc: While often overlooked, the Formulaic Assemblicator is a capable auto-crafter.

quests.title: Dynamic Tank
desc: Large scale Gas or Fluid storage, Dynamic Tanks may be any size from 3x3x3 to 18x18x18. Structural Glass may be used in place of Dynamic Tank blocks anywhere but the edges and corners.

quests.title: Solar
desc: Though they won’t produce anything at night, Solar Panels are an excellent way to get a small amount of power to remote places.

quests.title: Nutritional Liquifier
desc: All your essential vitamins, minerals, and amino acids, neatly condensed into a convenient chewy paste. Yum.

quests.title: Pigment Mixer
desc: This suite of blocks allows for high-efficiency production and application of dyes.

quests.title: Tools and Utility
desc: Beyond machines and logistics, Mekanism offers a number of very useful tools, armor, and utility devices.

quests.title: Meka-Tool
quests.subtitle: Rip and Tear
desc: A powerful all in one tool capable of accepting several upgrades.
Notable Upgrades
● Attack Amplification Unit
● Excavation Escalation Unit
● Vein Mining Unit
● Silk Touch Unit
● Teleportation Unit
● Farming Unit

quests.title: Atomic Disassembler
quests.subtitle: Don't Leave That Plasma Cutter Running
desc: A basic multi-tool with built in vein mining and excellent attack damage.

quests.title: Getting Started: Material Processing
desc: As noted, Mekanism maintains a strong focus on efficiencies throughout the mod. As machines are upgraded and more systems put in place, they become more efficient, more productive, and cheaper to run.
Focusing on being efficient from the very start will ultimately pay off in the long run.

quests.title: Metallurgic Infuser
quests.subtitle: Advanced Metallurgy
desc: Once some basic power infrastructure is settled, the next most important machine will be the Metallurgic Infuser.

Take notice of the color coding in Mekanism GUIs, as they’ll indicate where materials go. The Yellow box on the left is where the infusion matter goes. It’ll be absorbed into an internal buffer and then consumed during the actual craft.

These colors also correspond to the colors in the Side Config panel. By default, this machine expects the infusion material to be inserted from the bottom of the machine. That’s all configurable, however, so set them however they’re most convenient.

Automation Note: Since the two required input materials use two different channels, red and yellow, there’s no way to feed both items in from the same face. As a result, it’s often easiest to make multiple machines, each dedicated to their own infusion material.

item.name: Metallurgic Infuser / Basic Infusing Factory / Advanced Infusing Factory / Elite Infusing Factory …

quests.title: Enrichment Chamber
quests.subtitle: Put One In The Chamber
desc: Alloys will be needed commonly for more advanced machinery. They can be quite costly to make, however, as infusion materials don’t go very far.
They can be stretched quite a bit further by enriching them in an Enrichment Chamber, however.
For example, a single Redstone will make a single Infused Alloy, however a single Enriched Redstone will make eight Alloys. It is therefore well worth the effort to enrich these items.

item.name: Enrichment Chamber / Basic Enriching Factory / Advanced Enriching Factory / Elite Enriching Factory …

quests.title: Pressurized Reaction Chamber
quests.subtitle: Pushing Down On Me, Pressing Down On You
desc: Certain chemical reactions only occur at greater pressures and the PRC can be used to facilitate them.

quests.title: Supercritical Phase Shifter
quests.subtitle: I've Giv'n Her All We've Got, Captain
desc: By infusing Pandemonium with incredible amounts of magical energies, it may be refined into a material with potent transmutational properties: Aetherium.
Two ports with Supercharged Coils will accept power input. The other two ports will be used for inputting waste and outputting antimatter.
Adding more Ports with Supercharged Ports attached to them will allow the machine to run faster, assuming of course that sufficient power and waste can be supplied.
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki: Supercritical Phase Shifter","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com/wiki/Supercritical_Phase_Shifter"}}

quests.title: Aetheric Transmutation Chamber
quests.subtitle: Indistinguishable from Magic
desc: Alchemists of yore were correct in believing that elemental substances could be transmuted.
What they failed to understand was the vast amount of energy that would be required to do so.

quests.title: Gauge Dropper
quests.subtitle: Better Than a Stick in the Eye
desc: It’s bound to happen. With pipes and cables running everywhere, who knows what’s going to get into that machine when it’s plonked down. Water? Hydrogen? And once things are in, often times it’s not clear how to get them out.

This is where the Gauge Dropper comes in. This small tool will help extract unwanted inputs from various machines. Clicking on an input inside the GUI of a machine with the Dropper will extract a small amount of the input, allowing it to be easily transported to another machine. Sneak + Left-Click will instead void the material.
Similarly, Sneak + Right-Clicking the air with the gauge dropper will void whatever is currently stored.

quests.title: Tier Installers
quests.subtitle: Yo Dawg, Heard You Liked Machines...
desc: There are limits to the number of speed upgrades that can go in machines. After that, expanding sideways is the only option to speeding things up. Thankfully, Tier Installers make this somewhat easier than simply tossing down nine more machines full of upgrades. Remember, it’s all about being efficient!

Each Tier Installer will add a number of input and output slots to the machine, allowing it to run that many items in parallel. Each slot shares the other Upgrades in the machine, reducing the number of Upgrades that would need to be crafted.
To apply a Tier Installer, simply Sneak + Right-Click on a machine place in-world. Tiers must be installed in order, no skipping tiers!

item.name: Basic Tier Installer / Advanced Tier Installer / Elite Tier Installer / Ultimate Tier Installer

quests.title: Teleporter
quests.subtitle: Guests are reminded that Platform One forbids the use of weapons, teleportation, and religion.
desc: Got somewhere to be and no time to get there? Well, start walking. And next time, bring a teleporter to set up when you get there to avoid going the long way again.
Teleporter Frames are Optional.

quests.title: Getting Started: Logistics and Storage
desc: Mekanism deals in Energy, Fluid, Gas, Item, and Heat transfer, and has a matching pipe to assist in the transfer of each.
Configuring them is done with the Configurator, which itself has several modes. Use Sneak + Scroll Wheel to change the current mode.
When in Wrench mode, a Sneak + Right Click will immediately pick up any Mekanism machine or pipe.
When in any of the ‘Configurate’ modes, the Configurator will toggle different aspects of the pipe. See the following sections for more information.

quests.title: Mekanism
desc: A Sci-Fi themed technology mod with an emphasis on the extreme, Mekanism focuses on creating efficiencies, whether in the form of increased output from ores to advanced fusion reactors to power your base.

Its systems do aim towards a certain amount of realism with certain concessions along the way for better game play. Within the context of the mod, the player will need to master power generation, manage heat and radiation, all while seeking the most efficient path.
Beyond these quests, there is no in game guide to Mekanism. However a very thorough official wiki can be found here:
{"text":"Mekanism Wiki","color":"blue","underlined":"true","clickEvent":{"action":"open_url","value":"https://wiki.aidancbrady.com"}}

quests.title: Nature's Aura
desc: Nature's Aura is a druidic themed magi-tech mod that uses the omnipresent 'aura' to derive its power.
Be warned, Aura is a limited resource which must be managed and replenished lest the natural order be disturbed. Draining too much can cause dire consequences.

These quests will guide you through the mod, but be sure to refer back to the manual regularly for extra information. Chapters will unlock as you complete these quests and their associated achievements.

quests.title: Ritual of the Forest
quests.subtitle: Tire-toi une bûche
desc: The Ritual of the Forest is the basis for all magic to come. A tree is sacrificed in the center to provide the energy for the ritual.
The items around the outside of the recipe should each be placed into a Wooden Stand; the order is of no consequence and items may be placed manually or by automation.
Once the reagents are ready, place and grow the required sapling. The Gold Powder will be consumed along with the items and tree when the ritual completes.
Refer to the Book of Natural Aura for specific instructions on building the ritual.

quests.title: Getting Started: Rituals
quests.subtitle: The threads that bind us
desc: To begin upon the naturalist's path, Brilliant Fiber should be woven into the leaves of trees. There, they’ll transform the leaves to a beautiful golden hue.
Craft one or more Brilliant Fibers and Right-Click them onto any leaves. The effect will spread to nearby leaves, so with careful management, crafting more Brilliant Fibers should not be necessary.
Golden Leaf will drop whenever the fully transformed leaves are broken. Place fresh leaves near the remaining transformed leaves to begin converting them as well.

quests.title: Offering Table
quests.subtitle: Just nod if you can hear me
desc: Upon reaching a high enough skill level, Naturalists may commune directly with the gods, asking boons in exchange for offerings. Do be mindful, however, as the gods are petty at times, no matter what the offering.
Place the offerings in the bowl and then toss down a Spirit of Calling to complete the ritual. The bowl will hold multiple items, with only a single Spirit required for the full batch.

quests.title: Harnessing Aura: Automation
quests.subtitle: The duality of life and death
desc: The Natural Altar is the heart of two ritual practices; one to infuse life into objects and another to infuse death.
Refer to the Book of Natural Aura's section on the Natural Altar and the Crimson Altar for a preview of the required structure.

quests.title: Getting Started: Generating Aura
quests.subtitle: Give And Take
desc: The earliest Naturalists are said to have discovered Aura by observing these Ancient Trees. They found their roots grew deep, drawing Aura up from the depths and dispersing it into the environment.
Upon realizing the Aura could be renewed, they set about devising ever more elaborate ways to use and replenish it. Those who pushed it too far, however, paid dearly.
The trees grown from Ancient Saplings serve two primary purposes:
First, they’ll help replenish Aura in the area they’re planted, albeit slowly. As they do, the leaves will die and decay.  Worry not, more effective methods of replenishing the Aura exist.
Second, the wood is particularly useful when it comes to the arcane as it is steeped in the magical energies of Aura. It makes a fine base for many an arcane implement.

quests.title: Transmutation Catalyst
quests.subtitle: To obtain, something equal must be lost
desc: The Transmutation Catalyst augments the Natural and Crimson Altars to allow them to perform further transformations.
Place it on any of the four short pillars surrounding the Altar itself to activate it.

quests.title: Crumbling Catalyst
quests.subtitle: For ivy climbs the crumbling hall
desc: The Crumbling Catalyst augments the Natural and Crimson Altars to allow them to perform further transformations.
Place it on any of the four short pillars surrounding the Altar itself to activate it.

quests.title: Creational Catalyst
quests.subtitle: An explosion of life to match the primordial age
desc: Each Aura generating device is limited to the extent it can replenish Aura. It is possible, however, to push this boundary and flood an area with an over-abundance of Aura.
Place the Creational Catalyst beneath any Aura Generator to remove its generation cap and attain such lushness as has not been observed since the early days of creation.

quests.title: Mystical Magnifier
quests.subtitle: Relax, I'll need some information first
desc: Many devices have a specific range that can only be seen by Right-Clicking on them with a Mystical Magnifier. It's a valuable tool to any natural botanist.

quests.title: Environmental Eye
quests.subtitle: It's still magic even if you know how it's done
desc: Untrained eyes may notice the more overt signs of Aura in an area, subtle glowing lights and lush plant growth.
The Environmental Eye further hones the Naturalist’s vision to grant deeper insights into the Aura infusing the landscape.
Finding an area with higher-than-normal Aura at this stage may be helpful, as some Aura will be consumed in order to create the apparatuses needed to help renew it.

quests.title: Harnessing Aura: Tools of the Trade
quests.subtitle: Geo-caching 101
desc: A portable source of Aura that can be be put to good use with a variety of tools.
Refer to the Book of Natural Aura's section on Natural Tools for potential uses.
Note: These may not fill completely when worn. To get a full charge, or to even automate filling them, they may be placed in a Natural Altar to their maximum capacity.

quests.title: Environmental Ocular
quests.subtitle: Open your eyes, then open your eyes again
desc: An advanced version of the Natural Eye which grants its owner the ability to see ever more precise details of the Aura around them.

quests.title: Aura Trove
quests.subtitle: Thy cup runneth over
desc: Higher capacity than the Aura Cache.
Refer to the Book of Natural Aura's section on Natural Tools for potential uses.
Note: These may not fill completely when worn. To get a full charge, or to even automate filling them, they may be placed in a Natural Altar to their maximum capacity.

quests.title: Shifting Sundial
quests.subtitle: From dusk, to dawn
desc: The most powerful of Naturalists have found that when combined with a rare catalyst, the passage of time itself may be manipulated.
This process will rapidly advance time at a great cost of Aura. Be wary not to allow Aura to drop too far!

quests.title: Corporeal Eye
quests.subtitle: A line in the sand
desc: A simple apparatus that helps contain livestock and other animals. Creatures within the range of this block will be unable to step beyond its boundaries.
No Aura is consumed to produce this effect.
The range depends upon strength of the redstone signal it is provided.

quests.title: Altar of Birthing
quests.subtitle: Crossing the threshold
desc: A ritual that harnesses the powers of creation itself, allowing its user to bring forth new life from the barest traces of material.
Once built, simply throw down the reagents atop the altar. If there's enough Aura, the ritual will proceed automatically.
Refer to the Book of Natural Aura for specific instructions on building the ritual.

quests.title: Imperceptible Builder
quests.subtitle: Constructive interference
desc: The Imperceptible Builder assists in complicated automation tasks, taking blocks from nearby inventories and placing them down.
Specify where it should place blocks by placing an example in an Item Frame on the Builder itself.
Refer to the Book of Natural Aura for specific instructions.

quests.title: Aura Field Creators
quests.subtitle: Destructive interference
desc: When two Aura Field Creators are linked together, they form a destructive zone between them that rapidly breaks blocks at the cost of some Aura.
To link them, simply Right-Click one, and then the other. Supply a Redstone signal to either of them to enable the system. They'll begin drawing Aura and breaking blocks after a short delay.
An Item Frame can be used to alter their behavior as well:

Note: The Aura Field Creator will use any tool provided in the frame including any enchants or special break properties of the tool. Shears shear leaves, shovels collect snow, Fortune and Silk Touch are respected.

quests.title: Extraneous Firestarter
quests.subtitle: Maxwell's demon, hard at work
desc: When placed upon a Furnace, Blast Furnace, or Smoker, the Extraneous Firestarter will draw in nearby Aura, converting it into heat for smelting and cooking.

While this process is much quicker than burning Coal or other combustible materials, it does come with the drawback that it can drain Aura into dangerous levels. Multiple may even be installed to enhance the effect.

quests.title: Ender Crate
quests.subtitle: Abaddon's gate
desc: The entire Aura field appears to be connected in some fashion, even across dimensions. Though the measurable effects tend to be more localized, some brilliant Naturalist was able to deduce a way to use the subtle ripples in the weave to transfer matter unimaginable distance.

Ender Crates can be assigned to a channel in an Anvil by simultaneously renaming them and combining them with an Eye of Ender. More Crates can be assigned to the same channel at any time by giving them the same name.
Similarly, Ender Oculars may be assigned a channel to allow personal access to the same inventory. Perfect for dropping off the spoils of exploration while far from home.
A small amount of Aura is used every time an item is moved in or out of the crate. Therefore, it is vital that Aura is generated on both sides of the connection.

quests.title: Hopper Enhancement
quests.subtitle: It reaches out nothing answers and it reaches out
desc: When placed atop an Adept’s Hopper or a Vanilla Hopper, the Hopper Enhancement allows the collection of blocks up to seven blocks away. A very useful tool to have in any automated apparatus.
If used with an Adept’s Hopper, any filter set will be respected by the Hopper Enhancement.

quests.title: Adept Hopper
quests.subtitle: Filtering through the morass
desc: One of the few Natural devices that do not consume Aura to function, Adept’s Hoppers are a filterable hopper that moves items slightly faster than a vanilla hopper.
Place an Item Frame on the side and insert any item or block in the frame to set the filter.

quests.title: Esoteric Ecology
quests.subtitle: Do. Or do not. There is no try.
desc: Over the ages, Naturalists have come up with numerous ways to replenish Aura. Some require more advanced knowledge than others, and each has its own requirements and complications.

In most cases, they involve closing the circle, returning the energies imbued in some living entity back to the latent Aura field. Though a few creative methods have been discovered that involve more arcane energies.
Each has been detailed at length in the Book of Natural Aura.

item.name: Canopy Diminisher / Herbivorous Absorber / Swamp Homi / Offshoot Observer …

quests.title: Effect Powders
quests.subtitle: Dust in the wind
desc: Lush Aura has a variety of side effects which may or may not be desirable at any given time. Powders exist to control when and where these effects occur.
● Barrens - Prevent the formation of grass on Netherrack.
● Bountiful Core - Stone and Netherrack are converted to ore with the appropriate Aura type.
● Steady Growth - The growth of crops, plants, and flowers will no longer be boosted by Aura.
● Fertility - Passive Animals will breed when able.
● No Storage - Your Aura Cache or Trove will not charge in the area.

quests.title: Winter's Calling
quests.subtitle: She sounds like she's in a flurry
desc: When Aura is drawn through this device, it causes the heat in the area to rapidly disperse, dropping localized temperatures and causing snow and ice to form.

quests.title: Eyes in the Dark
quests.subtitle: The eyes have it
desc: Just as Ender Eyes may assist in the location of Strongholds, these assist in the location of other important structures.
● Eye of the Pillager will locate Pillager Outposts.
● Eye of the Blaze will locate Nether Fortresses.
● Eye of the Shulker will locate End Cities.

item.name: Eye of the Pillager / Eye of the Blaze / Eye of the Shulker

quests.title: Redstone Aura Vaporizer
desc: A closed system which prevents any loss of Aura, this small device serves as an excellent timer, releasing a Redstone pulse whenever the Aura within fully evaporates and re-condenses. The more Aura, the longer this process takes.
Right-Click the Aura Vaporizer with bottled Aura to define the time of the clock. Right-Click with an empty hand to retrieve whatever has been previously installed.
Each bottle of sunlight equates to one second of time. One bottle of ghosts, one minute. One bottle of darkness, one hour.

quests.title: Everlasting Spring
desc: While true that Water is easily obtained through other means, an Everlasting Spring provides a convenient place to connect a pipe to supply other machinery.
The Spring provides water at the cost of a small amount of Aura.

quests.title: Lamp of Sanctuary
desc: Keeping hostile creatures away from sensitive contraptions can be quite vital. The last thing anyone needs is a surprise Creeper visit.
For a miniscule upkeep cost, the Lamp of Sanctuary will inhibit natural mob spawns in its area of influence, the range of which is determined by the strength of the Redstone signal it is receiving.

quests.title: Item Distributor
desc: Quite the simple device, but powerful, nonetheless. The Item distributor moves items from the inventory above it and evenly distributes them to the inventories adjacent.

quests.title: Eir's Token
desc: A true marvel for anyone who’s spent any time toiling in the earth to extract resources. With Eir’s Token attached to a tool, it will simply stop working rather than break at low durability.

quests.title: Ring of Last Chance
desc: When held anywhere in one’s inventory, the Ring of Last Chance prevents a killing blow, shattering itself rather than allow its bearer to slip off this mortal coil.

desc: Botanist’s equipment offers several unique benefits to its user beyond the basic uses for armor and tools of each type.
● All pieces may be repaired with Aura simply by sneaking with an Aura Cache or Aura Trove equipped.
● Botanist’s Pickaxe: May be used to infuse materials with Aura by Right-Clicking.
● Botanist’s Handaxe: Cleaves through leaves very rapidly.
● Botanist’s Shovel: Converts Dirt to Grass and creates 3x3 Dirt Paths in Grass.
● Botanist’s Hoe: Randomly produces seeds when tilling Farmland.
● Botanist’s Blade: Inflicts Slow on its target.
● Botanist’s Armor: When wearing a full set, inflicts Withering on attacking enemies.
