By installing such a card into a Module in Emitting mode, several features become available. For example, by making use of the color channels, it can function as an AND gate, OR gate, compare against another channel or against a constant value, and much more. By chaining them together, some truly compact Redstone logic can be made.

quests.title: Module Expansion Crystal
quests.subtitle: Raspberry Pi
desc: Module Expansion Crystals are used to add extra functionality to various Tube Modules. Simply Right-Click it on any Tube Module to add new features
● Regulator Tube Module: Precise control of regulated pressure.
● Pressure Gauge Tube Module: Precise control of the Redstone signal.
● Air Grate Module: Adds a filter for what will be affected by it.
● Redstone Module: Adds a host of logic features such as AND and OR gates, clocks, Comparator functionality, and much more.

For example, the Redstone control of a Compressor can be greatly compacted by applying a Module Expansion Card to the Pressure Gauge. Set this to output a signal only when the Gauge is below 4.9 bar (or 19.9 bar for advanced), then use a short section of Redstone modules to bring that signal directly to the Compressor. This eliminates the need for the long loop of Redstone suggested earlier.

quests.title: Simple Drones
quests.subtitle: Flying Circus
desc: Logistics Drones are handy little helpers in places where you don’t want to run a full air infrastructure. Experiment with some logistics frames and deploy a logistics drone to move the items for you.

item.name: Drone / Logistics Drone / Harvesting Drone / Guard Drone …

quests.title: Charging Station
quests.subtitle: In-Flight Refueling
desc: The Charging Station is the primary way of charging Pneumatic items such as the Pneumatic Wrench, Jackhammer or Armor. It serves double duty as the means of inserting upgrades into those items as well.
By inserting a Dispenser Upgrade in the Charging Station, it will charge entities above it, recharging Drones or any equipment on a player.
Nearby drones will automatically seek out such a Charging Station when they’re low on Air.

quests.title: Item Life Upgrade
quests.subtitle: In Her Time of Need
desc: Install one or more Item Life Upgrades in a Drone to help them stay in working order. They can occasionally take damage from environmental hazards and these upgrades will cause them to self-repair at the cost of some Air.

quests.title: Standby Upgrade
quests.subtitle: She's All Alone, All Alone
desc: Installing a Standby Upgrade in a non-programmable Drone will let it go to sleep when there’s no work to be done. Programmable drones may be programmed to do the same without the need of an upgrade.

quests.title: Range Upgrade
quests.subtitle: He's Going the Distance
desc: Install a few Range Upgrades in a non-programmable drone to increase the area it covers.

quests.title: Speed Upgrade
quests.subtitle: He's Going for Speed
desc: Speed things up with a few of these in a Drone. Many other blocks benefit from them as well.

quests.title: Programmable Drones
quests.subtitle: Doin’ It My Way
desc: Programmable Drones are the pinnacle of PNC:R’s automation capabilities and the options are near limitless as they can interact with blocks and entities, wield weapons and tools, and perform their actions based on complex conditions.
Take a dive into this visual programming language and see what you can come up with! If you’re short of ideas, try some of these:
● Automate Powah’s Energizing Orb
● Automate Botania’s Runic Altar
● Automate PNC:R’s Biodiesel
● Create a slime farm using milk buckets and green dye
● Create a transportation network using drones to pick you up and teleport you

quests.title: Remote
quests.subtitle: Always At Arms Reach
desc: Remotes are programmable interface devices that work by manipulating global variables. You can use these for remote redstone when combined with a Universal Sensor, or they can be used to control programmable drones.

quests.title: Amadron Tablet
quests.subtitle: Prime Delivery
desc: The pinnacle of stay-at-home shopping. Click a button and your order is there before you know it.
Begin by binding the Tablet to a chest by Sneak + Right-Clicking the inventory with it. It may additionally be bound to a tank, if desired.

Place any payment items in the chest, then complete the order from the Tablet itself. Once submitted, a Drone will appear to extract the payment from the chest. A short time later, a second drone will appear to deposit the purchase in the chest. When purchasing fluids, they’ll be sent to the bound tank instead.

quests.title: Assembly Table
quests.subtitle: Some Assembly Required
desc: The Assembly Table is a multiblock machine capable of more advanced crafting.
Each piece has limitations on where it can be placed. Refer to the PNC:R manual for the exact placement rules.
A simple layout can be done in a 2x3 space, however:
IO, Controller, IO
Drill, Table, Laser
Note: The Drill \& Laser program allows the Assembly Table to craft recipes that require only a drill or laser. In most cases there’s no reason to use the individual programs.

quests.title: Fluid Tanks
quests.subtitle: Stacking the Odds
desc: Portable Fluid Storage. Also capable of filling buckets and other tanks for automation purposes.
Stack them vertically and Right-Click with a Pneumatic Wrench to form a multiblock tank.

quests.title: Arcane Compressor
quests.subtitle: Super Laminar Flow
desc: Advanced Compressors may reach up to 20 bar of pressure, powering some of the most Pressure hungry machines. However, this comes at the cost of needing to be kept cool to run efficiently.

While cooling these compressors with something like a Vortex Tube certainly works, it’s far from ideal as Vortex Tubes consume enormous amounts of Air to cool anything down. A very large percentage of Air made by the compressor would be going right back into cooling.

Instead, consider cooling these with Heat Sinks and Air Grates. Three Heat Sinks in direct contact with the Compressor, and several Air Grates set up such that each is blowing at all three Heat Sinks can keep a high-speed Compressor running very cool and at a minor fraction of Air compared to Vortex Tube cooling.

quests.title: Vacuum Pump
quests.subtitle: Full Reverse!
desc: Though most things will require high pressure to operate, some machines will require a vacuum to do what they do. The Vacuum Pump may be used for just this purpose.
Run pressure into the side of the machine with a green plus sign, then run a Tube out of the side with the red minus sign. Anything down the line will be put under vacuum.

Tip: Having a second Pressure Chamber under permanent vacuum can be enormously helpful as the Vacuum Chamber can be used to transfer Enchantments from items to books. Likewise, the books may be re-applied to items in a regular Pressure Chamber for a minor expenditure of Air.

quests.title: Vacuum Trap
quests.subtitle: Who Ya Gonna Call?
desc: Your gateway to custom spawning.
Not every mob is readily available from natural spawners. Thankfully, there is a way of recreating the magic of the Spawner Core: The Vacuum Trap.

The process begins similarly to the Spawner Extractor, hook the Vacuum Trap up to a Vacuum Pump and pull out all of the air. Volume upgrades are recommended and a Spawner Core is required. Sneak + Right-Click the charged Trap with a Pneumatic Wrench to pick it up. Now place it down near most any mob and Sneak + Right-Click it with an empty hand to open it. Nearby mobs will be sucked in and be added to the Core.
Multiple mob types can be stored in a Core, making mixed spawners possible.
A Spawner Core with only one mob in it is still valid for use in a Pressurized Spawner; very useful for hard to capture or rare mobs.
The Trap works more efficiently if it has Memory Essence in the internal tank, meaning it takes fewer mobs to completely fill it.
Random mobs may be released from a core by Sneak + Right-Clicking it on the ground, allowing easier transportation of mobs even before the Pressurized Spawner is available.

quests.title: Tools and Utility
quests.subtitle: You Can Touch, You Can Play
desc: Beyond machines and logistics, PNC:R offers a number of very useful tools, armor, and utility devices.

item.name: Pressure Tube / Reinforced Pressure Tube / Advanced Pressure Tube

quests.title: Heat Sink
desc: Heat Sinks will passively increase the rate at which Heat is transferred into the air, helping to cool things back down to ambient temperatures quickly and efficiently.

Heat Sinks in the area of effect of an active Air Grate will operate even faster. This is one of the most efficient ways to cool machines, when the Air Grates are regulated down to just enough pressure to operate.

When connected to a pressure line in a vacuum, the Air Grate also doubles as an item collector, pulling items and other entities towards it. Items pulled all the way to it will be inserted into any adjacent inventories.

quests.title: Pneumatic Helmet
quests.subtitle: Send Your Armies But They'll Never Be Enough, My Shell's Too Tough
desc: All pieces may be upgraded to enhance their armor, self-repair, or gilded to prevent Piglin attacks.
Other Notable Upgrades:
Helmet
● Night Vision
● Entity and Block Tracking
● Entity and Block Hacking
● S.C.U.B.A. Gear
Chestplate
● Magnet Upgrade
● Auto Tool Charging
● Block Launcher
● Elytra
Leggings
● Run Speed
● Jump Height
Boots
● Built in Step Assist
● Built in Fall Damage Negation
● Swim Speed
● Creative Flight

quests.title: Pneumatic Jackhammer
quests.subtitle: Swiss-Army… Hammer
desc: A versatile multi-tool capable of clearing large areas with ease. Sneak Right-Click to access the GUI where Drill Bits and Enchanted Books can be installed as well as changing the drill mode.
Accepts Fortune or Silk Touch books.

quests.title: Sentry Turret
quests.subtitle: Stand and Deliver
desc: A smart turret that can be filtered to attack only certain creatures. For instance, only adult animals.

quests.title: Minigun
quests.subtitle: Leveling the Playing Field
desc: A modern solution to monster slaying. Pet friendly too!
Add a Security Upgrade to prevent it from harming tamed creatures and fellow players.

quests.title: Micromissiles
quests.subtitle: Target Acquired
desc: Bats. The greatest enemy of them all. Now behold, their doom is in your hands.

Micromissiles are target seeking explosives. They do no damage to the terrain and can be configured for varying degrees of explosive damage, travel speed, and turn speed. Sneak Right-Click to configure.

quests.title: Crop Support
quests.subtitle: Reach for the sky!
desc: Crop Supports promote healthy plant growth, increasing how quickly they grow.

quests.title: Elevators
quests.subtitle: Uplifting News
desc: The perfect addition to any vertical base of operations, PNC:R Elevators feature an easy to use Elevator Caller which will take the user directly to the requested floor.

Each Elevator Base has a limit to how high it can go but stacking them atop each other will increase that height additively. Elevator Frames must be placed on top of the Base up to the maximum desired height.
For more information, refer to the PNC:R manual.

quests.title: Air Cannon
desc: While capable of doing damage with launched TNT or Arrows, perhaps more interestingly, the Air Cannon can be used for transporting items, mobs, or simply tossing things on the ground for in-world crafting with a flair.

quests.title: Transfer Gadget
desc: When placed on the side of an inventory or a tank, the Transfer Gadget facilitates the transfer of items and fluids into any adjacent tank. It is a bit slow, but has the benefit of not requiring a block space.

quests.title: Aerial Interface
quests.subtitle: It's Over! I Have the High Ground!
desc: The Aerial Interface is a powerful personal automation tool. Its sides may be configured to expose the player inventory to automation, allowing for automatic restocking of ammo and other items remotely.

Since it treats the player’s inventory as any other, it also permits remotely charging any Pneumatic equipment. For example, configure a side to access the armor slots, then point a tube with a Charging Module at that side. This will keep Pneumatic Armor always topped off.
In addition to this, with a Dispenser Upgrade installed it can automatically feed the player, or interface with their XP, allowing it to be piped in and out as Memory Essence.

quests.title: Filters
desc: Frames themselves have robust filtering options built in, but they don’t cover all use cases.

In order to filter by tags, a Tag Filter must be created in a Tag Workbench and inserted into the filter in place of an item. Place an item in the left-hand slot and some paper into the slot to the left of the Book icon. A list of tags will appear under the item which may be selected and sent to the right-hand side.
Once the Book icon Is pressed, all tags on the right will be encoded into the Tag Filter. A single Tag Filter may contain tags from multiple item types.
A Classify Filter may also be used for filtering broad categories of items. For instance, all furnace fuel, all unstackable items, all enchanted items, or anything that may be cooked in a furnace.

quests.title: Thermostat Module
desc: A very handy tube module to have, the Thermostat Module will read the temperature of the block it is facing, outputting a Redstone signal along the tube that may be used to control a Vortex Tube or any other contraption.
This allows for a very simple, and very compact way of meeting specific heat thresholds for crafting!

quests.title: Spellbound Air Blower
desc: The Spellbound Air Blower takes the Air Blower to the next level, processing four times faster than the base Encased Fan. It uses special meshes and PNC’s Heat mechanics to replace the Water, Lava, Soul Fire, or Fire used by the Encased Fan.
Meshes are installed by Right-Clicking them on the front of the Blower, while Heat should be supplied to the body of the Blower.

For Splashing recipes, it will use a Water Soaked Mesh. Ambient temperatures should normally suffice for this to work. Too cold and the Mesh may freeze. Too hot and it will be converted back into the Woven Mesh it was made from.
For Smoking recipes, no mesh is required, however the Blower will need to be heated to around 110C. With a Dense Mesh installed, however, it only needs to be heated to about 55C.

For Blasting recipes, the temperature needs to reach approximately 330C, however just like with Smoking, this temperature requirement can be significantly lowered by installing a Dense Mesh. This allows it to begin Blasting at only 110C.
Finally, Haunting Recipes require a Haunted Mesh and a temperature of approximately 110C.

quests.title: Air Blower
desc: An air powered device that mimics Create’s Encased Fan, the Air Blower uses a small amount of Air to process recipes twice as fast as the Encased Fan, making it a very handy upgrade when speed is of the utmost importance.

quests.title: Zephyr Engine
desc: The Zephyr Engine is a compact means of converting Compressed Air into Rotational Force. These Engines may be chained together, thereby adding their effects together to reach higher Stress capacities.

quests.title: Powah!
desc: As the name implies, Powah! is all about generating, storing, and transmitting power through various means.
In addition, it offers a few unique mechanics and a variety of new materials to go along with its various tiers. Read along to discover more.

quests.title: Getting Started: Logistics and Storage
desc: An energy generating mod would hardly be complete without some ways to transmit and store it. Powah comes with everything from personal batteries to charge held items to cables and in world storage cells.

quests.title: Furnator
desc: Operating on all sorts of basic Furnace fuel, Furnators generate respectable energy starting out and are a great way to obtain a little extra power from materials that might otherwise be considered waste.

Each tier of Furnator will generate the same amount of energy per fuel, they’ll just do so quicker. So, while a Nitro Furnator can generate some decent energy, it will consume fuel very quickly to do so.

quests.title: Energy Cables
desc: Simple cables to get energy from one place to another without fuss.
The portion of a cable that connects to a machine may be Right-Clicked to adjust it or make it Redstone sensitive.

item.name: Energy Cable (Basic) / Energy Cable (Hardened) / Energy Cable (Blazing) / Energy Cable (Niotic) …

quests.title: Magmator
desc: A sort of geothermal generator, the Magmator generates energy from hot fluids such as Lava.

Each tier of Magmator will generate the same amount of energy per bucket of fuel, they’ll just do so quicker. So, while a Nitro Magmator can generate some decent energy, it will consume fuel very quickly to do so.

quests.title: Thermo Generator
desc: A thermoelectric generator that requires a heat differential to generate energy. The Thermo Generator should be placed on a hot block of some sort and coolant should be piped into it.
The heat source itself will never be consumed, but the coolant is used up slowly over time.
Check Uses on the Thermo Generator in JEI to see all available heat sources and coolants.

item.name: Thermo Generator (Basic) / Thermo Generator (Hardened) / Thermo Generator (Blazing) / Thermo Generator (Niotic) …

quests.title: Solar Panel
desc: Only operating half of the day, Solar Panels still make an excellent power source for certain applications

item.name: Solar Panel (Basic) / Solar Panel (Hardened) / Solar Panel (Blazing) / Solar Panel (Niotic) …

quests.title: Lens of Ender
desc: When applied to a Solar Panel, a Lens of Ender will allow it to see the sun even while deep underground. It still won’t operate at night, but at least it can be brought inside or hidden.

quests.title: Uraninite
desc: Powerful fuel for use in Reactors, though its high cost to craft means lower tier Reactors may operate at a net loss.

quests.title: Reactor
desc: Reactors are large multiblock generators that consume multiple inputs to operate efficiently.

First, and most importantly is the actual fuel, Uraninite. Each piece represents 100mb in the fuel gauge and the Reactor performs best when the fuel gauge is full. Dropping a single piece of fuel in, versus filling the gauge will result in dramatically lower output per fuel, so try to keep it full while running.

Next comes coolant. Running the reactor generates heat that must be dissipated. To do this, the reactor needs both Solid and Liquid coolants. Checking Uses on a Reactor Block in JEI will show what counts for each. The Liquid Coolants are not consumed, but the Solid Coolants are.
Finally, the Reactor accepts two regulator materials, Carbon which helps the Reactor run more efficiently, and Redstone which will allow it to produce more energy per tick, though less efficiently.
The Carbon gauge accepts the same inputs as a Furnace or Furnator; Charcoal is likely the easiest to supply endlessly.
Building a Reactor is as simple as holding a stack of 36 blocks and placing one. The rest of them will place automatically.

quests.title: Getting Started: Energizing
desc: Powah introduces just a few types of machines, but multiple tiers of each. Obtaining higher tiers requires more powerful materials which are made with the Energizing Orb.

The Orb may be operated by hand or via automation, accepting items from any sort of pipe or conveyance. Once items are inserted, they may not be removed via automation until the craft completes, simplifying automated crafting considerably. Items may be removed by hand at any time, however.

Energy for the craft requires Energizing Rods placed around the Orb. These must be placed on some form of energy cable or battery. The rods themselves may be up to six blocks from the Orb and do not require line of sight; they’ll happily shoot their lasers through any block.
Rods will automatically link to the nearest Orb when placed but may be re-linked to another Orb manually with a Wrench. Sneak Right-Click the Wrench in the air to change it to Link mode.
As energy costs increase for higher tier materials, higher tier Rods are recommended to increase the energy delivery rate, though it’s also viable to simply add more Rods.

item.name: Energizing Rod (Basic) / Energizing Rod (Hardened) / Energizing Rod (Blazing) / Energizing Rod (Niotic) …

quests.title: Energy Cell
desc: Simple tiered energy storage that doubles as an item charger.
Each side may be configured separately and the whole Cell may be made Redstone sensitive.

item.name: Energy Cell (Basic) / Energy Cell (Hardened) / Energy Cell (Blazing) / Energy Cell (Niotic) …

quests.title: Ender Cell
desc: Ender Cells are the basis for cross dimensional and wireless power transfer.

Each Cell may be linked to one of up to twelve channels per player, with each channel having separate storage capacities. When first initialized, a channel will have no energy capacity of its own and Batteries or Energy Cells must be added to it. With the Interface open, Shift Right-Click Cells or Batteries to add them to the selected Channel. Each will add its full capacity as well as transfer any stored energy into the Channel.
This is a perfect way to recycle and condense any extra energy storage lying around.

item.name: Ender Cell (Basic) / Ender Cell (Hardened) / Ender Cell (Blazing) / Ender Cell (Niotic) …

quests.title: Player Transmitter
desc: Carrying around a battery is an excellent way to keep powered equipment charged on the go, but what if we could regain that inventory slot? The Player Transmitter allows precisely that by remotely charging any items in the owner’s inventory.
To set the owner, craft a Binding Card and Right-Click the card in the air. Doing so will bind the card to that player. The card may then be inserted into the Player Transmitter to configure it.

item.name: Player Transmitter (Basic) / Player Transmitter (Hardened) / Player Transmitter (Blazing) / Player Transmitter (Niotic) …

quests.title: Ender Gate
desc: Only one Ender Cell is truly required per channel. More can certainly be used, but they’re considerably more expensive than the alternative, Ender Gates.
Like Ender Cells, Ender Gates may be linked to a Channel in their interface. They can be used both for input and output to and from the Ender Network.
Unlike an Ender Cell, however, more storage may not be added to the Ender Network from a Gate. This may only be done at a Cell.

item.name: Ender Gate (Basic) / Ender Gate (Hardened) / Ender Gate (Blazing) / Ender Gate (Niotic) …

quests.title: Dimensional Binding Card
desc: An ordinary Binding Card will only work within the same dimension as the Player Transmitter. By upgrading it to a Dimensional Card, however, the Player can enjoy wireless charging from anywhere.

quests.title: Energized Steel
desc: After the Basic tier comes Hardened, the first tier requiring energized materials.

quests.title: Blazing Crystal
desc: The first of several crystalline materials required by Powah, Blazing Crystals retain enormous heat and double as a decent heat source for Thermo Generators.

quests.title: Niotic Crystal
desc: As costs increase, so to do the rewards, with Niotic tier machines operating much more quickly.

quests.title: Spirited Crystal
desc: The penultimate tier of materials, Spirited is quite powerful in its own right. But with the right materials we can go further still.

quests.title: Nitro Crystal
desc: Using incredibly rare materials to craft, Nitro represents the highest tier of Powah.

quests.title: Energy Hoppers
desc: Energy Hoppers effectively convert a simple chest into a mass charging inventory. Simply place it against a chest or other inventory; any powered items inside will be charged up in short order.

item.name: Energy Hopper (Basic) / Energy Hopper (Hardened) / Energy Hopper (Blazing) / Energy Hopper (Niotic) …

quests.title: Energy Discharger
desc: Energy Dischargers will rapidly drain the energy stored in Batteries, allowing it to be fed into machines. While perhaps less useful when compared to Ender Cells, they still allow for long range and rapid transport of energy by shipping Batteries around.

item.name: Energy Discharger (Basic) / Energy Discharger (Hardened) / Energy Discharger (Blazing) / Energy Discharger (Niotic) …

quests.title: Getting Started: Power Generation
desc: Powah offers five different generators, each situationally useful. Consider the application wisely when choosing which to use.

quests.title: Spirit
desc: Spirit is a small mod with one primary focus: spawning mobs.

quests.title: Soul Steel Tools
desc: In addition to harvesting extra souls when used to kill mobs, Soul Steel tools may also be empowered with the souls contained within a Soul Crystal. They may also be repaired by dropping them in Soul Fire.
The weapon will automatically pull from a Soul Crystal in one’s inventory when empowered, applying extra damage or special effects on hit. Be warned; this does consume souls from the Soul Crystal.
A tool may be empowered or depowered at any time by pressing its keybind.
{@pagebreak}
&nBee&r
● Applies poison on hit
&nBlaze&r
● Sets blocks and mobs ablaze
&nCat&r
● Applies speed on hit
&nCave Spider&r
● Applies poison on hit
&nChicken&r
● Applies slow falling on hit
{@pagebreak}
&nCreeper&r
● Explodes on impact
&nDolphin&r
● Applies dolphin's grace on hit
&nGhast&r
● Sets mobs and blocks ablaze
● Explodes on impact
&nGlow Squid&r
● Applies glowing on impact
&nIron Golem&r
● Provides 2 additional damage on hit
● Provides 1 additional level of
knockback on hit
{@pagebreak}
&nPufferfish&r
● Applies poison on hit
&nRabbit&r
● Applies jump boost on hit
&nRavager&r
● Provides 4 additional damage on hit
● Provides 2 additional levels of
knockback on hit
&nShulker&r
● Applies levitation on hit
&nSquid&r
● Applies blindness on hit
{@pagebreak}
&nTurtle&r
● Applies slowness on hit
● Applies resistance on hit
&nWarden&r
● Provides 5 additional damage on hit
● Provides 2 additional levels of
knockback on hit
● Applies darkness on hit
&nWither&r
● Applies wither on hit
● Explodes on impact
&nWither Skeleton&r
● Applies wither on hit

item.name: Soul Steel Sword / Soul Steel Shovel / Soul Steel Axe / Soul Steel Hoe …

quests.title: Getting Started: Soul Engulfing
desc: Soul Engulfing is the primary crafting mechanic introduced by Spirit. It involves building some structure with a Soul Fire burning in the middle, and then dropping an item into the Soul Fire.

For some crafts, this will consume the structure. For others, the structure will not be consumed. In either case, if the structure and materials are valid, the resulting item will be dropped on the ground.
The structure required for each craft, as well as an indication if it will be consumed, is shown in JEI.

quests.title: Soul Cage
desc: A Soul Cage is used to spawn more mobs, simply put. A Soul Crystal with enough souls stored in it may be Right-Clicked on it to set the type.
The more souls contained in the Crystal, the better the Soul Cage will be!

quests.title: Soul Crystal
desc: The Soul Crystal itself is used to store mob souls, with each crystal holding a single type of mob.
Filling the Crystal requires killing mobs with it in one’s inventory. Special weapons must be used as well; either Soul Steel tools or weapons enchanted with Soul Reaper will do nicely.

quests.title: Crystal Pedestal
desc: Crystal Pedestals may be used to help automate filling Soul Crystals.

Place one in a mob farm and provide it with a Soul Crystal. Any time a mob of the correct type is killed by an appropriate weapon within six blocks of it, the souls will be transferred into the Soul Crystal.
Modular Routers with Activator Modules, Create Deployers, and PneumaticCraft Drones are all capable of wielding such a weapon. Just be sure to drop it in Soul Fire every now and then to repair it!

Crystal Pedestals may also be used to combine two Soul Crystals with like souls stored in them. Place one on the Pedestal, then Right-Click it with the other to transfer into the Crystal on the Pedestal.

quests.title: Pedestal
desc: Pedestals are decorative blocks used to display items. Right-Click an item onto it to display.

quests.title: Soul Pedestal
desc: Soul Pedestals may be used to display mob souls for a more macabre sort of decoration. Right-Click with a Soul Crystal to display the contained mob.
Soul Crystal Shards and Soul Crystals will display an actual mob entity, while Crude Soul Crystals will only display a generic, though very cute, Crude Soul.
Any displayed soul may be converted to a Crude Soul by Right-Clicking with a Soul Steel Wand.

quests.title: Storage
desc: Finding a place to store stuff is always a bit complicated, and keeping organized can be quite a task at times. Thankfully, a few mods exist to assist in this endeavor. The following quests will help you discover these mods.
Note: Most blocks that are useful as a storage block have been Tagged for search in EMI. Search for the following categories:
● #containers
● #containers/basic
● #containers/bulk
● #containers/bag
● #containers/energy
● #containers/gas
● #containers/liquid

quests.title: Sophisticated Storage
quests.subtitle: A very fancy chest
desc: Extra-large storage in the same space as a chest. Sophisticated Storage adds advanced Chests, Barrels, and Shulker Boxes in with multiple tiers of capacity. They even accept various upgrades to add additional functionality.
Those may be upgraded in place by using the appropriate tier upgrade item on them.

quests.title: Find Me
desc: Forgot where you left your precious diorite? Mouse over some in your inventory or JEI and press Y to locate it in nearby inventories.

quests.title: Plonk
desc: Looking for a handy place to store your hammer at the forge? Tired of rummaging through chest after chest for that gear press? Place them in world instead!
Plonk allows you to place up to four stacks of items in any block space. Simply hold the item, point at a block, and press P to place. Right click to pick the items back up.

quests.title: Storage Controller
desc: The Functional Storage Controller acts as a central hub for automation. Any linked drawers are accessible through it by things such as pipes, hoppers, or an ME Storage Bus.
Drawers need not be in contact with the Controller, nor each other. They simply need to be selected and bound to the Controller by way of a Linking Tool.
To begin, select a Drawer Controller by Right-Clicking it with a Linking Tool. The selected Controller is highlighted while the Linking Tool is in hand.
The tool itself has several linking modes and linking actions that may be swapped at any time:
● Toggle between the Single and Multiple linking modes by Sneak + Right Clicking the air.
● Toggle between the Add and Remove linking actions by Right Clicking the air.

Once in the desired mode, simply Right Click the target drawer to bind or unbind it. If in Multiple Linking Mode, Right Click a Start and End drawer. Every drawer in the selected area will be linked at once. Every drawer linked to the selected Controller will be highlighted as well while the Linking Tool is in hand.

quests.title: Upgraded Storage
quests.subtitle: Bedazzled Chests
desc: Each tier of storage offers both more upgrade slots and more storage slots.

item.name: Basic to Iron Tier Upgrade / Iron to Gold Tier Upgrade / Gold to Diamond Tier Upgrade / Diamond to Netherite Tier Upgrade

quests.title: Functional Storage
quests.subtitle: Drawing a line in the sand
desc: Looking for a place to store those ten thousand Iron Ingots? Look no further. Functional Drawers has drawers that hold a very large quantity of a given item. They offer a number of useful upgrades as well to assist in both Storage and Automation endeavors.
A Configuration Tool may be used to lock a drawer, hide or show the stored item and quantity, or disable rendering for any installed upgrades.
● Toggle between modes by Sneak + Right Clicking in the air.
● Right Click a drawer to change settings in chosen mode.

quests.title: Storage Upgrades
desc: Thirty-two stacks aren't enough? There is a solution!
Each drawer has four upgrade slots that may be used to enhance storage, stacking up to truly monumental capacities.

item.name: Copper Upgrade / Gold Upgrade / Diamond Upgrade / Netherite Upgrade

quests.title: Iron Downgrade
desc: Bigger is not always better. A storage downgrade can be useful for light stock-keeping situations.

quests.title: Void Upgrade
desc: Excess items will be automatically voided.

quests.title: Backpack
desc: Sophisticated backpacks is the backpack mod you never knew you were missing.
The backpacks themselves may be worn in a curio slot and accessed via keybind, as well as be placed in world and interacted with via pipes or hoppers.
Beyond these already excellent features, they can also host a number of very useful upgrades.

quests.title: Magnet Upgrade
desc: A filterable upgrade that pulls items from afar, straight into your backpack.

quests.title: Everlasting Upgrade
desc: Never lose your precious goods again!

quests.title: Pickup Upgrade
desc: A filterable upgrade that lets items pass directly into the backpack when picked up by the player.

quests.title: Feeding Upgrade
quests.subtitle: You're Not You When You're Hungry
desc: Need a snack? Let your backpack provide.

quests.title: Personal Shrinking Device
desc: The Personal Shrinking Device can shrink one right out of sight and into the nooks and crannies of special machines.
Build your own contraption within them to suit your needs, complete with custom input and output sides.
Simply Right-Click a Compact Machine with the Personal Shrinking Device to warp inside.

quests.title: Compact Machines
quests.subtitle: One, cut a hole in a box
desc: Gather the materials for your first Compact Machine!
Compact Machines range in size from 3x3x3 to 13x13x13 blocks of internal space.
Choose the size that best fits your needs and build away!

item.name: Compact Machine (Tiny) / Compact Machine (Small) / Compact Machine (Normal) / Compact Machine (Large) …

quests.title: Tunnels
quests.subtitle: Two, stick your junk in that box
desc: Placed on the walls inside Compact Machines, Tunnels permit a connection to the outside world.

For example, place a Tunnel on a wall and right click it until it reports it is configured to the up position, then place a chest against it. Warp back outside and place a Hopper on the top of the machine and feed in a few items. They’ll be whisked away into that chest inside. Use this concept to feed items into or out of the machine, as necessary.
Of course, many other options exist for getting stuff in and out as well.

quests.title: Upgraded Backpacks
quests.subtitle: Haversack, will travel
desc: Each tier of backpack offers both more upgrade slots and more storage slots.

item.name: Iron Backpack / Gold Backpack / Diamond Backpack / Netherite Backpack

quests.title: Dimensional Storage
quests.subtitle: Wouldn't you think my collection's complete?
desc: Got more gadgets and gizmos than one cavern can hold? More whozits and whatzits than you know what to do with? Then its time to shove it in another dimension and hire someone to sort it for you. Just read the fine print of any contracts you sign.
Occultism offers extensive storage capabilities with cross-dimensional access both manually and via automation such as pipes, hoppers, or an ME Storage Bus.
Check out the Occultism chapter for more details on the process.

quests.title: Collector Upgrade
desc: A Collector Upgrade allows the drawer to pick up items from the world.
Set the pickup direction in the drawer’s GUI.

quests.title: Pusher Upgrade
desc: Puller and Pusher upgrades allow the drawer to pull items from or push items to adjacent inventories.
Set the direction in the drawer’s GUI.

quests.title: Ender Drawer
quests.subtitle: Getting your drawers in a knot
desc: Ender drawers, as the name might imply, allow their contents to be accessed from multiple locations.

Each drawer is given a unique frequency when placed which may be copied by Left Clicking it with a Linking Tool. Right Clicking another Ender Drawer copies the frequency to it, effectively making the two drawers act as one.

quests.title: Compacting Drawer
desc: Compacting drawers automatically change form of item stored.
From block to ingots, ingots to nuggets. Vice versa and everything at once.

quests.title: Armory Cabinet
quests.subtitle: Oh my god Becky, look at that trunk
desc: A hoarder’s dream come true. Now nothing from that mob farm will go to waste!
The Armory Cabinet will hold a very substantial amount of armor, weapons, tools, and other un-stackable items.
The block has no manual interface, items must be accessed through automation.

quests.title: Applied Energetics 2
quests.subtitle: Digital Age for Experts
desc: Far more than a simple storage solution, Applied Energetics 2 offers a full range of automation and cross dimensional transport capabilities.
Check out the dedicated AE2 chapter for more information.

quests.title: Stack Upgrades
desc: Stack upgrades allow each slot to hold more than usual, with their effect stacking with each other as well. A single Tier 1 upgrade will double a slot to 128, and another Tier 1 upgrade will double that again to 256!

item.name: Stack Upgrade Tier 1 / Stack Upgrade Tier 2 / Stack Upgrade Tier 3 / Stack Upgrade Tier 4

quests.title: Functional Upgrades
desc: Add some extra features to your backpack, like the ability to smelt, craft, or use a stonecutter without leaving the interface.

item.name: Smelting Upgrade / Smoking Upgrade / Blasting Upgrade / Crafting Upgrade …

quests.title: Tank Upgrade
desc: Personal fluid storage with a variety of practical applications.
This upgrade is augmented by Stack Upgrades.

quests.title: Battery Upgrade
desc: Keeping tools charged on the go can be quite a drain. Attach a battery to your backpack to recharge those items on the go.
This upgrade is augmented by Stack Upgrades.

quests.title: Pump Upgrades
desc: When paired with a Tank Upgrade, pumps allow the backpack to pull fluids in from the world. Go for a dive!
The Experience Pump allows the backpack to instead store player XP, even repairing equipped tools and armor enchanted with Mending!

item.name: Pump Upgrade / Advanced Pump Upgrade / Experience Pump Upgrade

quests.title: Stack Upgrades
desc: Stack upgrades allow each slot to hold more than usual, with their effect stacking with each other as well. A single Tier 1 upgrade will double a slot to 128, and another Tier 1 upgrade will double that again to 256!

item.name: Stack Upgrade Tier 1 / Stack Upgrade Tier 2 / Stack Upgrade Tier 3 / Stack Upgrade Tier 4

quests.title: Functional Upgrades
desc: Add some extra features to your storage, like the ability to smelt, craft, or use a stonecutter without leaving the interface.

item.name: Smelting Upgrade / Smoking Upgrade / Blasting Upgrade / Crafting Upgrade …

quests.title: Pickup Upgrade
desc: Any item that comes in direct contact with the storage will be picked up automatically.

quests.title: Magnet Upgrade
desc: Picks up items in the area, inserting them into the storage.

quests.title: Storage Controller
desc: The Sophisticated Storage Controller acts as a central hub for automation. Any linked containers are accessible through it by things such as pipes, hoppers, or an ME Storage Bus.

To connect a Sophisticated Storage container to the Controller, simply place it down next to the Controller. More containers may be added, so long as everything is touching. Chaining in this way works out to 12 blocks from the Controller.

Otherwise, remote containers may be linked with the help of a Storage Link. This will work in much the same way as a Controller in that a single Link can be used to connect a chained series of containers.
First, place a Storage Link against the block in question.
Next, Sneak + Right Click the Controller with a Storage Tool to select it.
Finally, Right Click one or more Storage Links to create the connection. Each successful link will render a line between the Controller and the Storage Link.

quests.title: Block
quests.subtitle: Trading Places
desc: While not really storage on its own, the Entangled Block enables remote access to the block or machine it is bound to, extending the block’s capabilities to the Entangled Block.

What does this mean, exactly? Well, if the target block accepts power, power can now be fed to it through the Entangled Block. Likewise for other things such as Fluids, Items, Mekanism Gases, PNC Air and Heat, and possibly more.
The uses for these blocks are practically endless, from hiding pesky wiring out of sight, to improving throughput to a machine by exposing more faces to insert through.
Bear in mind that the Entangled Block itself is still passive. If the bound machine is set to push items out to an adjacent chest, for instance, the Entangled Block will not do this.

To bind a block to the Entangled Block, Sneak Right-Click the target block with the Entangled Binder. Then simply Right-Click a placed Entangled Block. The target block will render inside of the Entangled Block when properly bound.

quests.title: Nomadic Tents
desc: Let wanderlust take you where the wind blows and bring your home along with you for the journey.
Nomadic Tents provide a small area to keep your essentials. Build a small storage system inside with some basic machinery. Keep your bed there too if you wish; sleeping is allowed!

Craft any sized tent, then Right-Click and Hold on the ground to place the frame. Right-Click each Frame block with a Tent Mallet to form the tent. Using a Golden Tent Mallet will frame out the entire tent instantly!
To pick the tent back up, Right-Click the door once with any Tent Mallet.
To enter or exit the tent, simply Right-Click or walk through the door. Enjoy your cozy new living space!
Note: Normally this mod has Tent Shovels that are used to increase the floor depth of a tent. These have been intentionally disabled, and all tents come with the floor depth maximized by default.
Already have a Mega sized tent but didn’t upgrade the floor layers? Craft it together with a Wooden Shovel to max out the layers.

quests.title: Safety First!
quests.subtitle: Don't Panic!
desc: There’s nothing quite so frustrating as falling into the void and dying due to a bug.
Things happen. Sometimes players get outside of the bounds of a Compact Machine or a Tent and end up in an awkward situation of being unable to get back again.
Enigmatica has implemented special precautions for these situations.
Just jump into the void to be teleported to your spawn point.
Valid Dimensions
● &3Compact Machines&r
● &6Nomadic Tents&r
● &5The End&r

quests.title: Storage Lectern
desc: Keeping things organized through the power of friendship!

Storage Lecterns act as the central access point for a storage system offered by Ars Nouveau. It connects multiple storage blocks together by way of Bookwyrms and offers some limited automation capabilities as well!
Read more about setting it up in the Ars Nouveau quest section.

quests.title: Storage
desc: Finding a place to store stuff is always a bit complicated, and keeping organized can be quite a task at times. Thankfully, a few mods exist to assist in this endeavor. The following quests will help you discover these mods.
Note: Most blocks that are useful as a storage block have been Tagged for search in EMI. Search for the following categories:
● #containers
● #containers/basic
● #containers/bulk
● #containers/bag
● #containers/energy
● #containers/gas
● #containers/liquid

quests.title: Sophisticated Storage
quests.subtitle: A very fancy chest
desc: Extra-large storage in the same space as a chest. Sophisticated Storage adds advanced Chests, Barrels, and Shulker Boxes in with multiple tiers of capacity. They even accept various upgrades to add additional functionality.
Those may be upgraded in place by using the appropriate tier upgrade item on them.

quests.title: Find Me
desc: Forgot where you left your precious diorite? Mouse over some in your inventory or JEI and press Y to locate it in nearby inventories.

quests.title: Plonk
desc: Looking for a handy place to store your hammer at the forge? Tired of rummaging through chest after chest for that gear press? Place them in world instead!
Plonk allows you to place up to four stacks of items in any block space. Simply hold the item, point at a block, and press P to place. Right click to pick the items back up.

quests.title: Storage Controller
desc: The Functional Storage Controller acts as a central hub for automation. Any linked drawers are accessible through it by things such as pipes, hoppers, or an ME Storage Bus.
Drawers need not be in contact with the Controller, nor each other. They simply need to be selected and bound to the Controller by way of a Linking Tool.
To begin, select a Drawer Controller by Right-Clicking it with a Linking Tool. The selected Controller is highlighted while the Linking Tool is in hand.
The tool itself has several linking modes and linking actions that may be swapped at any time:
● Toggle between the Single and Multiple linking modes by Sneak + Right Clicking the air.
● Toggle between the Add and Remove linking actions by Right Clicking the air.

Once in the desired mode, simply Right Click the target drawer to bind or unbind it. If in Multiple Linking Mode, Right Click a Start and End drawer. Every drawer in the selected area will be linked at once. Every drawer linked to the selected Controller will be highlighted as well while the Linking Tool is in hand.

quests.title: Upgraded Storage
quests.subtitle: Bedazzled Chests
desc: Each tier of storage offers both more upgrade slots and more storage slots.

item.name: Basic to Iron Tier Upgrade / Iron to Gold Tier Upgrade / Gold to Diamond Tier Upgrade / Diamond to Netherite Tier Upgrade

quests.title: Thermal Series
desc: The Thermal Series is a suite of mods that has been a staple of Modded Minecraft for years. Time has brought many changes to it, but it's kept its overall theme of slightly magical tech throughout.
The Thermalpedia goes into greater detail on many of the tools and machines in the Thermal Series. Refer to it often to learn more.

quests.title: Dynamo Stirling
quests.subtitle: Power, From the Top
desc: A Stirling Dynamo burns solid fuel to create a heat differential, allowing the engine to spin and generate energy in an easily stored and transferable form.
It’s a very basic form of power, but sufficient to get things going.

quests.title: Device Tree Extractor
quests.subtitle: Trickle-Down Economics
desc: While nothing is without cost, the source of energy isn't always immediately obvious. The Arboreal Extractor uses a combination of gravity and the trees own capillary action to collect the fluids available in the tree.
This is a non-destructive process, but a living tree is required. Supplying some bone meal or other fertilizer can help replenish the tree's reserves faster, thus boosting production.

quests.title: Machine Refinery
quests.subtitle: Whiskey Business
desc: With a little bit of energy input, the Fractionating Still can refine Resin into Tree Oil, a fine renewable fuel that burns more efficiently than coal.

quests.title: Machine Pulverizer
quests.subtitle: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
desc: Some materials are more abundant than they seem at first glance, they're simply locked up in different forms that require a touch more work to release.
A Pulverizer can help extract these extras, such as getting some nickel from iron ore, or silver from lead ore.

quests.title: Aura Forge
quests.subtitle: Support the Resistance!
desc: An advanced furnace used for making alloys directly, as well as many other useful materials, such as hardened glass.

quests.title: Dynamo Compression
quests.subtitle: ICE, ICE, Baby
desc: For a quick early boost in power, consider switching to liquid fuels. Compression Dynamos will output a bit more power per tick compared to Stirling, even without augments.

quests.title: Arcane Furnace
quests.subtitle: Capissen 38 Mark II
desc: A simple furnace, like a standard coal burning furnace except faster and more efficient.

quests.title: Machine Press
quests.subtitle: Bop It, Pull It, Twist It
desc: Precision machining typically means greater efficiencies, either in terms of time spent doing a task or materials used. The MultiServo Press is one such machine that makes pressing plates faster and gears cheaper, as well as opening the door to other processing techniques.

quests.title: Machine Insolator
quests.subtitle: Between the Wasteland and Sky...
desc: Nature does an excellent job of growing plants. It's been at it for a while, after all. But when space is at a premium a Phytogenic Insolator is an excellent alternative to the natural approach.
Water and energy are required. Fertilizer is recommended, though optional.

quests.title: Machine Crafter
quests.subtitle: Insert Tab A Into Slot B
desc: A precision machine that can quickly assemble components, simplifying automation. It features an internal fluid tank as well which can automatically provide liquids to crafts that need them.
Set a recipe, press the green check to validate it, and then supply the ingredients.

quests.title: Lightning Grenade
desc: A handheld 'explosive' that releases the charged energy of elemental Blitz, causing lightning to strike spontaneously.

quests.title: Ice Grenade
desc: A handheld 'explosive' that releases the chilling power of elemental Blizz, freezing water and blanketing the area in snow.

quests.title: Earth Grenade
desc: A handheld 'explosive' that releases the latent power of elemental Basalz, causing the earth to shift and crack.

quests.title: Fire Grenade
desc: A handheld 'explosive' that releases the smoldering energy of elemental Blaze, lighting the surroundings on fire.

quests.title: Exotic Elements
quests.subtitle: Everything changed when the Fire Elementals attacked
desc: Simple metallurgy can only go so far. At a certain point, more exotic materials are required. Seek out the elemental creatures that make their homes in the world's most extreme environments.
● Blaze may be found naturally just about anywhere in the Nether, though Nether Fortresses are certainly a hot spot for them.
● Basalz may similarly be found in the Nether such as in Basalt Deltas. They’ll appear in the Overworld as well in Barren or Mountainous Biomes.
● Blitz may be found in Warm and Dry biomes such as Deserts, Savannas, or Badlands; places with no rainfall.
● Blizz may be found in Cold biomes; anywhere that might see snow fall.

A Nature’s Compass is useful for locating Biomes by their properties. Use the Temperature or Tag sorting options to display a list of Biomes and their Tags. For instance, Frozen Peaks count as a Cold Biome and will spawn Blizz.
If these mobs prove difficult to find, they may be summoned via the Elemental Gate Pearls. Watch out, they’ll come in droves.

quests.title: RF Capacity and Transfer Augments
desc: Better storage or faster discharge?
Consider the application carefully when choosing between these augments.

item.name: Rf Coil Augment / Rf Coil Storage Augment / Rf Coil Xfer Augment

quests.title: Machine and Device Augments
desc: Integral Components represent a generic upgrade that may be installed in any upgradable Thermal Series machine, device, or dynamo. They offer a straight multiplier of most stats, applied after other Augments, so they’re always worth using.
Only one may be used at a time and only the highest tier counts, so be sure to spread them around.

Augments serve many roles, sometimes changing functionality slightly depending on where they’re installed. Not all Augments may be used in every Machine or Device, so be sure to check the Thermalpedia for specifics.

item.name: Upgrade Augment 1 / Upgrade Augment 2 / Upgrade Augment 3

quests.title: Machine Centrifuge
quests.subtitle: Up Against a Wall
desc: Based on the ancient art of spinning things until they fly apart, Centrifuges are a vital part of industry, allowing for efficient separation of materials.
Useful for a variety of purposes, its also the first step in creating a versatile and energy dense liquid fuel.

quests.title: Fluid Cell
quests.subtitle: Can't Help But Feeling a Bit Sloshed
desc: Expandable, upgradable, portable. An excellent first choice for gathering liquids in the field.

quests.title: Energy Cell
quests.subtitle: Feeling Energetic and Quite Positive
desc: Expandable, upgradable, portable. Perfect for a quick charge just about anywhere.

quests.title: Machine Output Augment
desc: A lot of material can be lost in a system that would otherwise be recovered by slowing down to check again.
The Auxiliary Process Sieve trades speed for extra materials in applicable machines.

quests.title: Machine Speed Augment
desc: Sometimes a job just needs to get done now and damn the costs.
Flux Linkage Amplifiers greatly enhance the speed of machines though they reduce energy efficiency in turn.

quests.title: Device Water Gen
quests.subtitle: Sick of Tea? That's like being sick of breathing.
desc: Feeling a bit peckish? How ‘bout a nice cold one, fresh from the tap?
Place water sources on each side to produce infinite water that can be extracted by any fluid pipe. Perfect for automation!

quests.title: Device Rock Gen
quests.subtitle: Igneous is Bliss
desc: A bit of lava, a bit of water. Boom, box of rocks.
The type of stone output by the Igneous Extruder is controlled by the block placed beneath it.

quests.title: Device Collector
quests.subtitle: I laugh at gravity all the time. Hahaha, gravity!
desc: A handy device for picking up that mess those zombies left. Such inconsiderate house-guests.

quests.title: Dynamo Augments
desc: Industrial Engineers often face a trade-off when designing a system, speed versus efficiency. Consider the needs of the application when choosing between these.
Efficiency pays off when energy can be stored for future use. In such a case, installing a few Multi-Cycle Injectors would be wise.
However, sometimes a loss is required to keep up with a steady demand. Auxiliary Reaction Chambers will increase output, but fuel will burn less efficiently.

Dynamos will produce less energy per tick as their internal buffer fills, but they will continue to burn fuel slowly unless turned off. With an Excitation Field Limiter installed, they’ll turn off on their own when full.

quests.title: Arcane Dynamo
quests.subtitle: A Remnant from Another Age
desc: For the ultimate power source from Thermal, things will need to get a little arcane.
The Disenchantment Dynamo burns enchanted books as fuel, converting the powerful magics on these books into more readily used energy.

quests.title: Charge Bench
desc: Perfect for quickly charging a set of tools after a long mining session, the Energetic Infuser can hold up to nine items at a time for charging. Items may be accessed manually or via automation.

quests.title: Tools and Utility
desc: A multi-purpose workbench which may be used to charge items, fill tanks with fluid, and alter the augments of any Thermal machines, devices, or tools.
While the augments in blocks may be swapped out in their own GUI, the Tinker’s Workbench is the only way to install or change augments in hand-held tools.

quests.title: Flux Capacitor
desc: Portable energy storage, Flux Capacitors will keep any handheld tools charged up for continuous use.
Notable Augments:
● Integral Components
● RF Coils

quests.title: Potion Infuser
desc: A portable potion vial that may be used on oneself or on another target. It will inject the target with whatever potion it contains and may be used to automatically re-apply potions to the bearer.
Notable Augments:
● Integral Components
● Expanded Tank Construction
● Alchemical Amplifier
● Alchemical Extender

quests.title: Watering Can
desc: When filled, this Watering Can may be used to water plants in a wide area. Watering plants will greatly enhance growth rates.
Notable Augments:
● Integral Components
● Expanded Tank Construction
● Radial Enhancement

quests.title: Fluid Reservoir
desc: A handheld Fluid Reservoir that will provide its fluids to any other held or worn equipment. On switching modes, it may also be used to pick up or place fluids in the world.
Notable Augments:
● Integral Components
● Expanded Tank Construction

quests.title: Potion Quiver
desc: A magical quiver capable of holding an enormous number of arrows when upgraded which automatically tips any arrows with liquid potions as they’re drawn and shot.
Notable Augments:
● Integral Components
● Expanded Tank Construction
● Alchemical Amplifier
● Alchemical Extender

quests.title: Getting Started: Power Generation
desc: There’s no such thing as a free lunch, as the saying goes; doing work means using energy and the search for energy drives all things. Our first step, therefore, will be to generate some power to begin working with Thermal machines.

quests.title: Device Composter
desc: Good soil can be hard to come by, but with modern composting methods, waste food can be easily converted into compost. From there, a little mixing with other substrates results in some fine soil for planting.

quests.title: Device Soil Infuser
desc: Phyto-Soil is already a marvel of modern farming techniques, but it can be activated with a gentle energetic field to further enhance its growing potential.

The Phyto-Soil Infuser does just this, supplying energy to Phyto-Soil at the same level as the device, as well as to soil one block above or below. The radius of effect may be expanded with Radial Enhancement Augments.

quests.title: Device Fisher
desc: While many find fishing to be a calm, relaxing pastime, others find it well… tedious. To those, the Aquatic Entangler is the answer to obtaining fish and other goodies from the seas.

Place the device facing a pool of water, its working area is out in front of it. Bait isn’t a requirement, but it will certainly help. By default, it captures fish from the Fishing loot table, without the Treasure or Junk tables.
● Junk Nets will capture loot from the standard Junk fishing table, things like Leather Boots, String, and Leather.
● Aqua-Chow will simply increase the rates of catching standard drops from the Fishing table.

● Benthic Aqua-Chow, on the other hand, will capture special treasures, such as Sponge, Prismarine, elusive Nautilus Shells, and even Tridents. Obtaining the best loot requires placing it in Ocean and Deep Ocean biomes.

quests.title: Device Hive Extractor
quests.subtitle: Don't Worry, Bee Happy!
desc: Bees really don’t care much for the more traditional methods of harvesting honey from their hives as it has a tendency towards being somewhat disruptive.
Flow Hives are a more recent invention that allows easy harvesting of honey without disturbing the bees, ensuring they remain healthy and happy, while still being able to enjoy their golden goodness.
Simply place the Hive Hopper below a Beehive to begin!

quests.title: Device Nullifier
quests.subtitle: I know you're not supposed to cry over spilled tea, but... it's just so sad.
desc: Pack overloaded with junk?
The Nullifier is a simple trash can for both items and fluids.

quests.title: Machine Crystallizer
quests.subtitle: You Rock, Let's Facet!
desc: Growing crystals is typically just a matter of getting all the right ingredients into the right environment. Like making a cake, forget one ingredient and the whole thing is ruined.
The Crystallizer handles the majority of this, just give it the raw materials and I’ll get thing growing in no time.

quests.title: Machine Sawmill
desc: With a blade guaranteed for life, this Sawmill will get any cutting job done in no time.

quests.title: Machine Pyrolyzer
quests.subtitle: We Flame to Please
desc: Burning or heating things to change their characteristics is nothing new, of course, but how one goes about it is just as important as the heat itself. In the case of pyrolysis, objects are heated in the absence of oxygen, resulting in an entirely different sort of reaction as compared to simply burning it.
Mostly used for obtaining Coal Coke, the byproducts of its use can also be quite useful.

quests.title: Device Potion Diffuser
quests.subtitle: Sharing tea with a fascinating stranger is one of life's true delights.
desc: When provided Liquid Potions (as made in an Alchemical Imbuer) the Decoctive Diffuser will fill the air with a gentle mist, applying the potion effect to any entities nearby.
If there are no entities nearby, nothing happens, and no potion is spent.

quests.title: Getting Started: Material Processing
desc: Better materials are critical to any industrial endeavor but getting them will require a bit of setup and equipment first.

quests.title: Flux Drill
quests.subtitle: Guaranteed to Satisfy
desc: A powered drill that makes short work of any digging task.
Notable Augments:
● Integral Components
● RF Coils
● Radial Enhancement

quests.title: Flux Saw
quests.subtitle: You Try to Hold Me But I Bust Through
desc: A powered saw that makes short work of any tree.
Notable Augments:
● Integral Components
● RF Coils
● Radial Enhancement

quests.title: Hazmat Suit
quests.subtitle: So Dangerous, You'll Have to Sign a Waiver
desc: Sturdy protection against many of the world's hazards, such as fire and very sharp booshes.

quests.title: Diving Suit
quests.subtitle: You'll Think You're Looking at Aquaman
desc: A technological marvel that allows the wearer to remain productive for longer under water.

quests.title: Flux Magnet
desc: A powered magnet, perfect for keeping your precious items from falling into lava.
Notable Augments:
● Integral Components
● RF Coils
● Radial Enhancement

quests.title: Area Radius Augment
desc: Radial Enhancements generally increase the area a device works in, such as drilling a 3x3 or larger area in the Fluxbore or spreading potion effects further in a Decoctive Diffuser.

quests.title: Agricultural Devices
desc: Though metals and gems from deep in the ground are certainly important, one must not overlook the importance of renewable resources from the land and sea. Thermal offers a number of devices to assist in these agrarian endeavors.

quests.title: Beekeeper Helmet
quests.subtitle: You Realized It's Not My Fault Not a Moment Too Soon
desc: In some parts of the world, when any major events happen within a family, the news is traditionally shared with the bees.
A suit such as this may be prudent to wear when bringing bad news to the hive.

quests.title: Advanced Materials
desc: Alloys and Cured Rubber unlock access to even more interesting machines. Of note, machines for refining better fuels and growing crystals.

quests.title: Machine Brewer
quests.subtitle: Why is it that every time you play with magic water, I get soaked?
desc: An upgrade to the antiquated Brewing Stand, with better heating and larger storage.
Liquid Potions may be used in several devices, such Alchemical Quivers or Decoctive Diffusers.
The fluid may also be bottled in a Fluid Encapsulator if needed.

quests.title: Thermal Series
desc: The Thermal Series is a suite of mods that has been a staple of Modded Minecraft for years. Time has brought many changes to it, but it's kept its overall theme of slightly magical tech throughout.
The Thermalpedia goes into greater detail on many of the tools and machines in the Thermal Series. Refer to it often to learn more.

quests.title: Device Tree Extractor
quests.subtitle: Trickle-Down Economics
desc: While nothing is without cost, the source of energy isn't always immediately obvious. The Arboreal Extractor uses a combination of gravity and the trees own capillary action to collect the fluids available in the tree.
This is a non-destructive process, but a living tree is required. Supplying some bone meal or other fertilizer can help replenish the tree's reserves faster, thus boosting production.

quests.title: Machine Refinery
quests.subtitle: Whiskey Business
desc: With a little bit of energy input, the Fractionating Still can refine Resin into Tree Oil, a fine renewable fuel that burns more efficiently than coal.

quests.title: Machine Pulverizer
quests.subtitle: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
desc: Some materials are more abundant than they seem at first glance, they're simply locked up in different forms that require a touch more work to release.
A Pulverizer can help extract these extras, extracting more material from ores. Be sure to check out the available Catalysts to get the most out of this machine.

quests.title: Aura Forge
quests.subtitle: Support the Resistance!
desc: An advanced furnace used for making alloys directly, as well as many other useful materials, such as hardened glass.

quests.title: Arcane Furnace
quests.subtitle: Capissen 38 Mark II
desc: A simple furnace, like a standard coal burning furnace except faster and more efficient.

quests.title: Machine Press
quests.subtitle: Bop It, Pull It, Twist It
desc: Precision machining typically means greater efficiencies, either in terms of time spent doing a task or materials used. The MultiServo Press is one such machine that makes pressing plates faster and gears cheaper, as well as opening the door to other processing techniques.

quests.title: Machine Crafter
quests.subtitle: Insert Tab A Into Slot B
desc: A precision machine that can quickly assemble components, simplifying automation. It features an internal fluid tank as well which can automatically provide liquids to crafts that need them.
Set a recipe, press the green check to validate it, and then supply the ingredients.

quests.title: Lightning Grenade
desc: A handheld 'explosive' that releases the charged energy of elemental Blitz, causing lightning to strike spontaneously.

quests.title: Ice Grenade
desc: A handheld 'explosive' that releases the chilling power of elemental Blizz, freezing water and blanketing the area in snow.

quests.title: Earth Grenade
desc: A handheld 'explosive' that releases the latent power of elemental Basalz, causing the earth to shift and crack.

quests.title: Fire Grenade
desc: A handheld 'explosive' that releases the smoldering energy of elemental Blaze, lighting the surroundings on fire.

quests.title: Exotic Elements
quests.subtitle: Everything changed when the Fire Elementals attacked
desc: Simple metallurgy can only go so far. At a certain point, more exotic materials are required. Seek out the elemental creatures that make their homes in the world's most extreme environments.
● Blaze may be found naturally just about anywhere in the Nether, though Nether Fortresses are certainly a hot spot for them.
● Basalz may similarly be found in the Nether such as in Basalt Deltas. They’ll appear in the Overworld as well in Barren or Mountainous Biomes.
● Blitz may be found in Warm and Dry biomes such as Deserts, Savannas, or Badlands; places with no rainfall.
● Blizz may be found in Cold biomes; anywhere that might see snow fall.

A Nature’s Compass is useful for locating Biomes by their properties. Use the Temperature or Tag sorting options to display a list of Biomes and their Tags. For instance, Frozen Peaks count as a Cold Biome and will spawn Blizz.
If these mobs prove difficult to find, they may be summoned via the Elemental Gate Pearls. Watch out, they’ll come in droves.

quests.title: RF Capacity and Transfer Augments
desc: Better storage or faster discharge?
Consider the application carefully when choosing between these augments.

item.name: Rf Coil Augment / Rf Coil Storage Augment / Rf Coil Xfer Augment

quests.title: Machine and Device Augments
desc: Integral Components represent a generic upgrade that may be installed in any upgradable Thermal Series machine, device, or dynamo. They offer a straight multiplier of most stats, applied after other Augments, so they’re always worth using.
Only one may be used at a time and only the highest tier counts, so be sure to spread them around.

Augments serve many roles, sometimes changing functionality slightly depending on where they’re installed. Not all Augments may be used in every Machine or Device, so be sure to check the Thermalpedia for specifics.

item.name: Upgrade Augment 1 / Upgrade Augment 2 / Upgrade Augment 3

quests.title: Machine Centrifuge
quests.subtitle: Up Against a Wall
desc: Based on the ancient art of spinning things until they fly apart, Centrifuges are a vital part of industry, allowing for efficient separation of materials.
Useful for a variety of purposes, its also the first step in creating a versatile and energy dense liquid fuel.

quests.title: Fluid Cell
quests.subtitle: Can't Help But Feeling a Bit Sloshed
desc: Expandable, upgradable, portable. An excellent first choice for gathering liquids in the field.

quests.title: Machine Output Augment
desc: A lot of material can be lost in a system that would otherwise be recovered by slowing down to check again.
The Auxiliary Process Sieve trades speed for extra materials in applicable machines.

quests.title: Machine Speed Augment
desc: Sometimes a job just needs to get done now and damn the costs.
Flux Linkage Amplifiers greatly enhance the speed of machines though they reduce energy efficiency in turn.

quests.title: Device Water Gen
quests.subtitle: Sick of Tea? That's like being sick of breathing.
desc: Feeling a bit peckish? How ‘bout a nice cold one, fresh from the tap?
Place water sources on each side to produce infinite water that can be extracted by any fluid pipe. Perfect for automation!

desc: A handy device for picking up that mess those zombies left. Such inconsiderate house-guests.

quests.title: Tools and Armor
desc: Many mods add a variety of very useful tools that can be easy to overlook. These quests won't cover everything, but will serve to highlight some of the more notable options not otherwise covered in other quest chapters.
Note: Most tools and armor have been Tagged for easier search in EMI. Search for the following categories to discover more:
● #armor
● #armor/helm
● #armor/chest
● #armor/leggings
● #armor/boots
● #tools
● #tools/pickaxe
● #tools/shovel
● #tools/axe
● #tools/hoe
● #tools/multi-tool

quests.title: Mining Gadget
quests.subtitle: Frickin' Laser Beams
desc: A powered tool capable of mining blocks from a distance.
Danger: Class 4 Laser Device. Avoid eye or skin exposure.
Notable Upgrades
● Torch Placer
● Area Mining
● Silk Touch
● Fortune
● Filterable Void Upgrade
● Magnet Upgrade

item.name: Mining Gadget MK3 / Mining Gadget MK1 / Mining Gadget MK2

quests.title: Cloud in a Bottle
quests.subtitle: Head in the Clouds
desc: Ever wish you could start building a platform in the sky without having to nerd-pole your way up there?
Well, if you can't fly you may still need that nerd-pole. If you can, however, grab a bottle of cloud to act as a starting point for the platform.

Using a glass bottle between y192 and y196 will get you a Bottled Cloud. Right-Clicking the air again will place the cloud, allowing other blocks to be placed against it. It will disappear after a few moments, but will go back into your bottle on it's own if another block is placed against it in time.

quests.title: Time in a bottle
quests.subtitle: Just to Spend it With You...
desc: Save every day like a treasure and spend them on whatever you like.
Sneak Right-Click most machines to spend stored time on them, speeding them up briefly.

quests.title: Personal Shrinking Device
quests.subtitle: Pym Powered
desc: Smaller, but equally strong? Impossible!
Until now.
With Shrink’s Personal Shrinking Device in hand, shrink to the tiniest of sizes and slip through cracks even a mouse would scoff at.
● Right Click to open the GUI and select a size.
● Sneak + Right Click to shrink yourself.
● Left Click an entity to shrink it.
● Right Click a shrunken entity with a Glass Bottle to pick it up.
Keep a villager in your pocket for good luck!

quests.title: Vein Miner?
desc: There is no dedicated vein miner mod in Enigmatica 9 since we’ve got a variety of very cool tools that offer the same features and more.
AoE Mining? Vein Mining? Spooky Mining at a Distance? Yeah, we’ve got that.
The following quests will help highlight some of the more notable options. Enjoy!

quests.title: Pneumatic Jackhammer
desc: Starting at the Diamond tier of drill bit, the Pneumatic Jackhammer is capable of vein mining ores and wood. It’s got a number of other modes as well to help with clearing an area in a more controlled fashion.
At the Netherite tier, it gains the ability vein mine any block, if desired.

item.name: Skyseeker's Drill Bit / Soulstrider's Drill Bit

quests.title: Meka-Tool
desc: With Vein Mining Units installed, the Meka-Tool gains the ability to vein mine ores and logs. It may optionally be toggled to apply to any block.
Additionally, the Blasting Unit allows it to mine a large area up to 9x9, with the radius and all other options configured in the Module Tweaker menu.

item.name: Module Vein Mining Unit / Module Blasting Unit

quests.title: Chainsaw
desc: When applied to an Axe, the Chainsaw enchantment will cause the axe to fell entire trees, rather than a single block at a time.

quests.title: Skyseeker's Handaxe
desc: The Skyseeker’s Handaxe natively has the ability to chop whole trees, making short work of any logging operation.

quests.title: Spells
desc: Included with the Novice’s Spellbook is the Glyph of Break, which is used for any sort of block breaking.
Available at Tier 2, the Glyph of Fell acts on Trees, Mushrooms, Cactus, or any other vegetation, cutting them down in one swift action.
Apply the Glyph of AOE after either of these glyphs to increase the number of blocks they will break.
Example: Touch > Fell or Break > AOE x8

item.name: Novice Spell Book / Mage's Spell Book / Archmage Spell Book

quests.title: Excavators
desc: Upgrades to basic Shovels and Hammers, these tools mine a 3x3 area.
Apply Power of the Depth to them to increase the depth of mining. Each level of the enchant will cause the tool to mine another block deep.

quests.title: Flux Tools
desc: The Fluxbore and Fluxsaw both accept Integral Components and Radial Upgrades, allowing them to break blocks in ever increasing areas.

quests.title: Infinity Tools
desc: With each level of charge, the Infinity Drill and Infinity Saw work in ever increasing areas. The Drill works in a simple radius around the point of mining, while the Saw cuts trees from the top down in a large area.

quests.title: Engineer's Tools
desc: The Mining Drill and Buzzsaw both operate with liquid fuels, accepting most liquid fuels in the pack.
The Drill itself is capable of up to a 3x3 mining area, while the Buzzsaw will attempt to cut down whole trees.

item.name: Iron Drill Head / Skyseeker's Drill Head / Botanist's Sawblade / Rockcutter Sawblade

quests.title: Superior Shields
desc: Creeping Creepers got you down? Zealous Zombies getting all up in your face? Salacious Skeletons just won’t let you mine in peace?
Get a shield! But not just any shield, Superior Shields are worn in Curio slots and protect their wearer automatically, even from dastardly attacks from behind.
Superior Shields have three important stats that determine how well they protect:
● Hit Points
The number of hearts of damage they’re capable of blocking before needing to recharge.
● Recharge Rate
The number of seconds it takes to recharge half a shield.
● Recharge Delay
Time in seconds without taking damage before the shield begins to recharge.

All together, these stats mean that a shield will only be effective in situations where the bearer is not under constant assault, once the Hit Points are diminished, the bearer needs to move away from danger to allow them to recharge. So, they’re excellent for those unexpected attacks, but won’t keep you alive forever.

In addition to their basic stats, they may also be enchanted with a number of interesting effects, such as curing the bearer of all potion effects when the shield is depleted or applying Poison to anything that damages the shield.

quests.title: Tool Belt
desc: Need help juggling all those tools? Craft a Tool Belt!
The Tool Belt holds two tools by default but may be expanded to up to nine slots by adding Belt Pouches in an Anvil.

While worn in a curio slot, the belt allows quick swapping between any of the tools stored in it. Check the Key Binds menu for options. By default, opening the tool swap menu is on R and opening the belt’s inventory to add or remove tools is on V.
