quests.title: Mining Gadget
quests.subtitle: Frickin' Laser Beams
desc: A powered tool capable of mining blocks from a distance.
Be aware, this device requires a lot of energy to power it. You'll need something to deliver that energy wirelessly, such as a Player Transmitter to truly make use of this device.
Danger: Class 4 Laser Device. Avoid eye or skin exposure.
Notable Upgrades
● Torch Placer
● Silk Touch
● Fortune
● Filterable Void Upgrade
● Magnet Upgrade

item.name: Mining Gadget MK3 / Mining Gadget MK1 / Mining Gadget MK2

quests.title: Cloud in a Bottle
quests.subtitle: Head in the Clouds
desc: Ever wish you could start building a platform in the sky without having to nerd-pole your way up there?
Well, if you can't fly you may still need that nerd-pole. If you can, however, grab a bottle of cloud to act as a starting point for the platform.

Using a glass bottle between y192 and y196 will get you a Bottled Cloud. Right-Clicking the air again will place the cloud, allowing other blocks to be placed against it. It will disappear after a few moments, but will go back into your bottle on it's own if another block is placed against it in time.

quests.title: Time in a bottle
quests.subtitle: Just to Spend it With You...
desc: Save every day like a treasure and spend them on whatever you like.
Sneak Right-Click most machines to spend stored time on them, speeding them up briefly.

quests.title: Vein Miner?
desc: There is no dedicated vein miner mod in Enigmatica 9 since we’ve got a variety of very cool tools that offer the same features and more.
AoE Mining? Vein Mining? Spooky Mining at a Distance? Yeah, we’ve got that.
The following quests will help highlight some of the more notable options. Enjoy!

quests.title: Pneumatic Jackhammer
desc: Starting at the Diamond tier of drill bit, the Pneumatic Jackhammer is capable of vein mining ores and wood. It’s got a number of other modes as well to help with clearing an area in a more controlled fashion.
At the Netherite tier, it gains the ability vein mine any block, if desired.

item.name: Skyseeker's Drill Bit / Soulstrider's Drill Bit

quests.title: Meka-Tool
desc: With Vein Mining Units installed, the Meka-Tool gains the ability to vein mine ores and logs. It may optionally be toggled to apply to any block.
Additionally, the Blasting Unit allows it to mine a large area up to 9x9, with the radius and all other options configured in the Module Tweaker menu.

item.name: Module Vein Mining Unit / Module Blasting Unit

quests.title: Chainsaw
desc: When applied to an Axe, the Chainsaw enchantment will cause the axe to fell entire trees, rather than a single block at a time.
Crafted Steeleaf Axes even come pre-enchanted!

quests.title: Skyseeker's Handaxe
desc: The Skyseeker’s Handaxe natively has the ability to chop whole trees, making short work of any logging operation.

quests.title: Spells
desc: Included with the Novice’s Spellbook is the Glyph of Fell, which acts on Trees, Mushrooms, Cactus, or any other vegetation, cutting them down in one swift action.
Available at Tier 2, the Glyph of Break is used for any sort of block breaking.
Apply the Glyph of AOE after either of these glyphs to increase the number of blocks they will break.
Example: Touch > Fell or Break > AOE x8

item.name: Novice Spell Book / Mage's Spell Book / Archmage Spell Book

quests.title: Excavators
desc: Upgrades to basic Shovels and Hammers, these tools mine a 3x3 area.
Apply Power of the Depth to them to increase the depth of mining. Each level of the enchant will cause the tool to mine another block deep.

quests.title: Infinity Tools
desc: With each level of charge, the Infinity Drill and Infinity Saw work in ever increasing areas. The Drill works in a simple radius around the point of mining, while the Saw cuts trees from the top down in a large area.

item.name: Infinity Nuke / Infinity Hammer / Infinity Drill / Infinity Trident …

quests.title: Engineer's Tools
desc: The Mining Drill and Buzzsaw both operate with liquid fuels, accepting most liquid fuels in the pack.
The Drill itself is capable of up to a 3x3 mining area, while the Buzzsaw will attempt to cut down whole trees.

item.name: Iron Drill Head / Skyseeker's Drill Head / Botanist's Sawblade / Rockcutter Sawblade

quests.title: Superior Shields
desc: Creeping Creepers got you down? Zealous Zombies getting all up in your face? Salacious Skeletons just won’t let you mine in peace?
Get a shield! But not just any shield, Superior Shields are worn in Curio slots and protect their wearer automatically, even from dastardly attacks from behind.
Superior Shields have three important stats that determine how well they protect:
● Hit Points
The number of hearts of damage they’re capable of blocking before needing to recharge.
● Recharge Rate
The number of seconds it takes to recharge half a shield.
● Recharge Delay
Time in seconds without taking damage before the shield begins to recharge.

All together, these stats mean that a shield will only be effective in situations where the bearer is not under constant assault, once the Hit Points are diminished, the bearer needs to move away from danger to allow them to recharge. So, they’re excellent for those unexpected attacks, but won’t keep you alive forever.

In addition to their basic stats, they may also be enchanted with a number of interesting effects, such as curing the bearer of all potion effects when the shield is depleted or applying Poison to anything that damages the shield.

item.name: Bronze Shield / Electrum Shield / Constantan Shield / Ironwood Shield …

quests.title: Tool Belt
desc: Need help juggling all those tools? Craft a Tool Belt!
The Tool Belt holds two tools by default but may be expanded to up to nine slots by adding Belt Pouches in an Anvil.

While worn in a curio slot, the belt allows quick swapping between any of the tools stored in it. Check the Key Binds menu for options. By default, opening the tool swap menu is on R and opening the belt’s inventory to add or remove tools is on V.

quests.title: Armorer
desc: Armorers provide a variety of enchanted armor which can be quite useful early on. They can also be a convenient source of Bells.

quests.title: Butcher
desc: Butchers mostly buy raw meats and sell cooked meats. To the lucky few, however, they might have a Rabbit’s Foot available to trade.

quests.title: Cartographer
desc: Perhaps best known for their maps to nearby treasures and monuments, Cartographers also provide a number of interesting items such as banner patterns or Antique Ink, which gives maps a fancy faded look for decorative purposes.

quests.title: Cleric
desc: Clerics buy and sell a many precious materials such as Gold and Lapis. They can be an excellent source of Ender Pearls as well, however, with no combat required.

quests.title: Farmer
desc: Farmers will buy and sell a variety of crops. They can also sell Suspicious Stews and other treats.

quests.title: Fisherman
desc: Have some spare fish to sell? Fishermen will buy raw fish and sell cooked fish. They’ll also offer enchanted Fishing Rods.

quests.title: Fletcher
desc: Need a Bow or Crossbow? Perhaps just some arrows without the hassle of killing Chickens? Fletchers are the answer. They’ll even sell enchanted equipment occasionally.

quests.title: Leatherworker
desc: Leatherworkers are an excellent source for leather goods such as armor or Saddles.

quests.title: Librarian
desc: Always a classic, Librarians are well known for their propensity of selling Enchanted Books, among other things. It should be noted that some efforts have been taken to reduce the number of enchants that will appear in their trades to avoid the need to constantly re-roll to get a desirable enchant.
Available Enchants:
● Protection
● Fire Protection
● Blast Protection
● Projectile Protection
● Feather Falling
● Reflective Defenses
● Bane of Illagers
● Smite
● Obliteration
● Splitting
● Soulbound
● Holding
● Capacity
● Infinity
● Nature's Mend
● Comb Cutter
● Temptation
● Lure

quests.title: Stone Mason
desc: Buying and selling various stones and bricks, Stone Masons are particularly useful as a source of Quartz blocks.

quests.title: Shepherd
desc: Primarily trading in wools and dyes, Shepherds have an artistic side and will occasionally sell paintings as well.

quests.title: Toolsmith
desc: Toolsmiths provide a variety of enchanted tools which can be quite useful early on. They can also be a convenient source of Bells.

quests.title: Weaponsmith
desc: Weaponsmiths provide a variety of enchanted weapons which can be quite useful early on. They can also be a convenient source of Bells.

quests.title: Fluix Researcher
desc: Fluix Researchers can be an excellent early source for Certus Quartz and Sky Stone, as well as selling Inscriber Presses without needing to go out looking for a crashed meteor.

quests.title: Pressure Mechanic
desc: Pressure Mechanics sell a wide variety of Pneumatic devices, specialized ammo for Miniguns, and even circuit boards.

quests.title: Forager
desc: Foragers will purchase a variety of spare mushrooms that you may have lying about.

quests.title: Shady Wizard
desc: Trading in all manner of arcane goods, Shady Wizards are particularly useful for obtaining ritual tablets, familiar shards, and even rare Caster Tomes.

quests.title: Engineer
desc: Engineers mostly buy and sell building materials such as concrete and scaffolding. They will, however, sell maps to Mineral Deposits at high levels.

quests.title: Machinist
desc: Machinists are perhaps most useful for the Blueprints they provide, being one of the only reliable sources for Arc Furnace Electrode Blueprints. They also sell tools, drill heads, and various machine parts.

quests.title: Electrician
desc: Electricians offer a variety of wires and electrical components, as well as Faraday armor to keep you safe around exposed wires.

quests.title: Gunsmith
desc: Trading in gun parts and ammo, Gunsmiths can be invaluable for creating a powerful Revolver as they offer unique parts with special properties like increased luck or firing rate.

quests.title: Outfitter
desc: One of the stranger Villager workstations, the Immersive Engineering Outfitter requires a Banner placed on the floor (not on a wall) with any shader applied to it. Applying a shader is as simple as right clicking the placed Banner with a Shader.
These will then sell a variety of Shader Grabbags, allowing easy access to many random shaders to apply to compatible items such as Revolvers, Mining Drills, and more.

item.name: Common Shader Grabbag / Uncommon Shader Grabbag / Rare Shader Grabbag / Epic Shader Grabbag …

quests.title: Villagers
desc: Several mods add villagers, and it isn’t always a simple task to figure out what workstation goes with which villager.
The following quests cover the workstations used by each villager and attempt to give a brief description of what trades might be found.
